GTTS.label: Safe Mode - Prototype Changes Only
GTTS.description: Enabling Safe Mode prevents the mod from making any runtime changes to the game. This means that the per map mod settings will have no effect. It means that the game speed has to be manually adjusted. Many of the per map settings can be configured when the map is generated, such as pollution and biter expansion options, but other need to be adjusted manually. See the readme for more information.

GTTS.label: Target FrameRate
GTTS.description: This sets the UPS target for the game to run at, and therefore the scaling ratios for prototype speeds. Belt speeds are accurate at the following UPS (480, 240, 160, 120, 96, 80, 60, 48, 40, 32, 30, 24, 20, 19.2, 16, 15 and 12).

GTTS.label: Increase Fluid Flow Speed (Read tooltip before using)
GTTS.description: When enabled, changes fluid box heights and base levels to increase fluid flow rates at low UPS, at higher UPS this will significantly slow fluid flow. This can also introduce severe oscillations in fluid networks. Use with caution. It is safe to enable and disable for testing without consequence.

GTTS.label: Adjust the Game Speed
GTTS.description: When disabled, the mod will not change the game speed. It will have to be manually controlled.

GTTS.label: Reset the UPS to 60
GTTS.description: When enabled, and until it is disabled, the UPS will be set back to the previous value. This is useful if you want to remove the mod, this can be checked, and the game saved before removal to return the game speed to normal.

GTTS.label: Adjust Hand Crafting Speeds
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change each characters crafting speed.

GTTS.label: Adjust the Pollution Spread Rates
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the map's pollution spread and absorption rates.

GTTS.label: Adjust the Biter Evolution Rate
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the biter's evolution over time rate.

GTTS.label: Adjust the Biter Expansion Times
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the biter's expansion speed.

GTTS.label: Adjust Group Formation Times
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the biter's group formation times.

GTTS.label: Adjust Day and Night Length
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the day and night cycle length for the base surface of Nauvis.

GTTS.label: Adjust Wind Speed
GTTS.description: Enabling this option will change the wind speed for the base surface of Nauvis.

SensibleStationNames.description: How far (in chunks) to look for things that might identify a station.  The full radius is only used if no relevant entities cannot be found nearby.\n\nHigher values may reduce performance.

SensibleStationNames.description: Who can toggle the debug overlay.  The overlay may negatively affect UPS and thus it is suggested you restrict it in multiplayer games.

TreePlant.label: Repairable trees
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make repair packs work on trees.

TreePlant.label: Biter-proof trees
TreePlant.description: Enable this to disable attacks on trees - i.e. biters destroying trees and rocks to get to their target.

TreePlant.label: Long-life stumps
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make stumps last much longer than normal so that you can repair them more easily.

TreePlant.label: Mineable stumps
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make the stumps mineable and drop their parent tree type placeable anew. This is the core of the mod.

TreePlant.label: Increased stump hitbox
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make stumps have bigger hitboxes to make mining them easier.

TreePlant.label: Trees drop selves
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make trees drop themselves as well as their wood.

TreePlant.label: Trees drop seeds
TreePlant.description: Enable this to make trees sometimes drop seeds which can replant them elsewhere.

TreePlant.label: Tree healing capsule repairs pollution damage
TreePlant.description: If true, the tree healing capsule will repair pollution damage.

TreePlant.label: Allow rocks to be moved around
Preserve decoratives
TreePlant.description: Whether to preserve decoratives from being removed by building near them. Adds some naturalism and can reduce pollution with some mods.

ThoroughProcessing.label: Allow infinite mineral resources
ThoroughProcessing.description: Adds deposits of infinite minerals. If the Resource Spawner Overhaul is enabled, these pools will be located in the center of the usual ones.

ThoroughProcessing.label: Allow deposits of rich ores
ThoroughProcessing.description: Deposits of rich iron and copper ore will appear, when generating maps.

ThoroughProcessing.label: Edit smelting recipes
ThoroughProcessing.description: As a result of smelting copper and iron ore, in addition to the copper and iron plates, iron slag and a copper sludge will be obtained.

palettecleanser.label: Main color scheme
palettecleanser.description: (More profiles coming soon!)  Select from the available profiles designed to work around various forms of color vision deficiency.  Or, if you're an advanced user, you can choose Custom, then edit color-schemes.lua in the mod's zip folder to choose your own palette.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance resource and terrain colors on map
palettecleanser.description: Resource patches will have much clearer color differences.  Plus, in a shocking twist of colorist cruelty, we mute the map colors of sandy beach tiles so they aren't as distracting.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance roboport service area colors
palettecleanser.description: Roboport logistics and construction service areas are highlighted with alternate hues both in the world, and on the map.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance turret and grenade range colors
palettecleanser.description: Capsules, grenades, turrets, and artillery ranges all get a boost in visibility.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance electric pole and drill service area colors
palettecleanser.description: Electric poles and electric drills benefit from a higher-contrast service area overlay.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance circuit colors
palettecleanser.description: Adjusted colors provide a clearer distinction between Electronic and Advanced Circuits.  Processing Units get a boost, too.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance fluid colors in recipes, pipes, and tanks
palettecleanser.description: Light oil and related recipes and icons get a bright new color.  Other fluids also look nicer, with enhanced contrast in pipes and tanks.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance logistic chest and inserter colors
palettecleanser.description: Inserters get some spiffy new colors and logistic chests are easier to distinguish.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance explosive shell and cluster grenade icons
palettecleanser.description: Cluster grenades get a radical new splash of color, and explosive cannon shells get some explosive markings.

palettecleanser.label: Enhance technology GUI colors
palettecleanser.description: Changes color of available techs to light blue, and nudges the hue of unavailable-red away from conditionally-available-orange.

palettecleanser.label: Use thicker signal wires
palettecleanser.description: Thicker signal wires and power lines really stand out against the background.

palettecleanser.label: Preserve signal wire colors during highlight
palettecleanser.description: Preserve wire colors during mouseover-highlight (at the expense of reduced highlight contrast).

palettecleanser.label: Signal wire colors
palettecleanser.description: Red and Green are not always easy to distinguish, so replace one with a fancy new spool of Blue wire and build the Nauvis Network in style.

mini-machines.label: New Icon Handling for Mini Machines
mini-machines.description: New icon handling method, replacing the old, smaller icons, for compression arrows which imply "miniaturization". Applies to all mini machine icons. Defaults to true. This setting may be removed at a later date.

mini-machines.label: Mini Machine Tech Tree
mini-machines.description: Creates miniaturization tech tree for all mini machines. If disabled, all machines are unlocked by the same technology as their original entities. Defaults to true.

mini-machines.label: Mini Machine Balance
mini-machines.description: Applies the below balance changes to all mini machines. 66% recipe cost, 75% crafting speed, and module reduction are properly balanced default values. Default to true.

mini-machines.label: Mini Machines Recipe Cost Percentage Reduction
mini-machines.description: Mini machines recipe cost set to percentage of base machine recipe. At 100%, uses same amount of ingredients as base machine. Defaults to 66%. Higher amounts are harder.

mini-machines.label: Mini Machines Crafting Speed Percentage Reduction
mini-machines.description: Mini machines crafting speed set to percentage of base machines crafting speed. At 100%, has same crafting speed as base machine. Defaults to 75%. Lower amounts are harder.

mini-machines.label: Mini Machines Module Reduction
mini-machines.description: When enabled, reduces the module slots of all mini machines by 1. Mini machines retain base machine module slots when disabled. Defaults to true. Harder when enabled.

mini-machines.label: Mini Miner Resource Radius Reduction
mini-machines.description: When enabled, reduces the resource radius of mini mining drills. Mini miner will retain resource radius as base machine when disabled. Defaults to true. Harder when enabled.

mini-machines.label: Mini Assemblers
mini-machines.description: Enables mini assemblers and mini assembler research.

mini-machines.label: Mini Furnaces
mini-machines.description: Enables mini furnaces and mini furnace research.

mini-machines.label: Mini Refineries
mini-machines.description: Enables mini refineries and mini refinery research

mini-machines.label: Mini Miners
mini-machines.description: Enables mini miners and mini miner research

Noxys_Waterfill.label: Waterfill recipe override
Noxys_Waterfill.description:
This setting allows you to completely override the recipe for waterfill.

!!! WARNING !!!

A mistake in this setting can cause unexpected problems so make sure you have it correct!
Make a backup of your `mod-settings.dat` file prior to modifying this setting.

The format is as follows: type:item=amount
You can add more that one by seperating multiple of these entries by a comma.

Example: fluid:water=1000,item:explosives=10,item:processing-unit=1
This would be the same as hard recipe difficulty.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Round all numbers in recipes to the nearest prime to make ratios in production chains even harder. Does not affect item properties like belt speeds, only recipes. Overrides the regular rounding setting for recipes. Default disabled.

RandomRecipes.label: Randomize all recipes
RandomRecipes.description: Randomize all recipes, except for a few defined on the blacklist like iron and copper plate smelting, and rocket parts. If disabled, only a select few recipes on the whitelist in the config.lua file will be randomized. Default enabled.

RandomRecipes.label: Enable blacklist
RandomRecipes.description: If enabled, certain items in a list in config.lua (by default, Kovarex Enrichment, copper and iron plates) will not be randomized, even if "Randomize all recipes" is enabled. Default enabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Enable Blacklist
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: If enabled, certain items (by default, Kovarex Enrichment, copper and iron plates) will not be randomized, even if "Randomize all recipes" is enabled. (There is also another blacklist in the config.lua file that will prevent recipes like barreling from being randomized that would break the game completely. You can only disable that one in the config file.). Default enabled.

RandomRecipes.label: Always randomize product amounts
RandomRecipes.description: If enabled, the amount of products will always be randomized. If disabled, only products in recipes with ingredients that are needed once are randomized, so that recipes don't get cheaper on average. Default enabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Always randomize product amounts
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: If enabled, the amount of products will always be randomized. If disabled, only products in recipes with ingredients that are needed once are randomized, so that recipes don't get cheaper on average. Default enabled.

RandomRecipes.label: Randomization range
RandomRecipes.description: How much the randomized numbers can deviate from the normal values. For example, the default range of 4 means ingredient amounts can range from 1/4 to 4 times of their normal value. The higher the range, the higher the variations will be. Default 4.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomization range
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: How much the randomized numbers can deviate from the normal values. For example, the default range of 4 means ingredient amounts can range from 1/4 to 4 times of their normal value. The higher the range, the higher the variations will be. Default 4.

RandomRecipes.label: Difficulty
RandomRecipes.description: Possible values: 0 to 10. Lowering tends to make recipes cheaper, belts faster, assembling machines consume less power etc. 0 is extremely easy. 10 is extremely difficult. Default 5.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Difficulty
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Possible values: 0 to 10. Lowering tends to make recipes cheaper, belts faster, assembling machines consume less power etc. 0 is extremely easy. 10 is extremely difficult. Default 5.

NauvisDay.label: Base pollution factor
NauvisDay.description: A (decimal) multiplier for the pollution production. Multiplied against internal values. Increase this to make even MORE pollution. Lower bound clamped at 1.0.

NauvisDay.label: Acid rain threshold
NauvisDay.description: The minimum amount of air pollution in a chunk before it can start spawning acid rain.

NauvisDay.label: Water pollution threshold
NauvisDay.description: The minimum amount of air pollution in a chunk before it will start contaminating the water.

NauvisDay.label: Water recovery threshold
NauvisDay.description: The maximum amount of air pollution in a chunk before contaminated water will start cleaning again; MUST be much (several times cleanup) less than the polluting threshold or you get water flipping back and forth.

NauvisDay.label: Polluted water tile cleanup
NauvisDay.description: The amount of air pollution removed when a water tile turns polluted and if cleaned released when it turns back (multiplied against cleanup release factor).

NauvisDay.label: Water cleanup release factor
NauvisDay.description: The fraction (decimal) of pollution release (of that originally absorbed) when a polluted water tile converts back to clean water.

NauvisDay.label: Use depleted oil fields for waste storage wells
NauvisDay.description: Whether oil that reaches its minimum value should be converted to an empty well for pollution wells. If false empty wells (reskinned) generate in the world instead. You do NOT want to change this on existing worlds as the internal entity names are different.

NauvisDay.label: Enable Steam-Powered Furnace
NauvisDay.description: If you have another mod adding something similar, or do not want non-vanilla machines, you can disable the steam-powered furnace (ie a low-pollution smelting option).

NauvisDay.label: Enable Gas-Powered Boiler
NauvisDay.description: If you have another mod adding something similar, or do not want non-vanilla machines, you can disable the gas-powered boiler (ie a lower-pollution steam-production option).

NauvisDay.label: Enable Bomb Flies
NauvisDay.description: Whether to spawn a new enemy type in high-pollution areas at higher evolution factors - flying mobs that go near a defensive wall and blow a small hole in it.

NauvisDay.label: Bomb Fly pollution threshold
NauvisDay.description: The minimum pollution a spawner must be surrounded by to spawn a Bomb Fly.

NauvisDay.label: Enable Filtered Refinery
NauvisDay.description: If you have another mod adding something similar, or do not want non-vanilla machines, you can disable the filtered refinery (a less polluting refinery).

NauvisDay.label: Steam Powered Furnace Speed Multiplier

NauvisDay.label: Pollution Chemical Processing Consumption
NauvisDay.description: A multiplier for how much sludge pollution chemical processing (eg into sulfuric acid) should consume. Set to zero to disable that processing entirely. Note that the design is supposed to be that processing is only a way to make some use of some pollution, not a way of disposing of all of it. This scales the outputs as well as the inputs.

NauvisDay.label: Pollution Chemical Processing Yield
NauvisDay.description: A multiplier for how much sludge pollution chemical processing should yield, to be combined with the base multiplier option. This option allows modifying the yield without modifying the sludge consumption.

ResourceLabels.label: Label calculation interval
ResourceLabels.description:
The resource labeling algorithm scans all charted chunks for resources. This interval determines how many ticks should pass between each chunk scan.

Higher values increase performance, but it takes longer to show all resource labels.

Default: 20, Minimum: 0 (not recommended)

True:

cut-and-paste.label: Replace mode
cut-and-paste.description:
Specify what to do with conflicting entities when pasting a copy/cut blueprint.

When different:
Recreate destination entity if it has a different type than the source.
When the entities are identical, the destination entity's settings and direction will be copied from source if possible (else it will be deconstructed and replaced). Circuit wires will be kept.

Always:
Conflicting entities are always desconstructed even if they are of the same type. The original circuit wires will also be recreated if both entities are of the same type.

Never: conflicting entities are never deconstructed (this doesn't apply to trees which are always deconstructed by the game when force-placing blueprints).

cut-and-paste-016.label: Replace mode
cut-and-paste-016.description:
Specify what to do with conflicting entities when pasting a copy/cut blueprint.

When different:
Recreate destination entity if it has a different type than the source.
When the entities are identical, the destination entity's settings and direction will be copied from source if possible (else it will be deconstructed and replaced). Circuit wires will be kept.

Always:
Conflicting entities are always desconstructed even if they are of the same type. The original circuit wires will also be recreated if both entities are of the same type.

Never: conflicting entities are never deconstructed (this doesn't apply to trees which are always deconstructed by the game when force-placing blueprints).

Krastorio2_Modules.label: Efficiency module pollution reduction bonus
Krastorio2_Modules.description: Add an additional pollution reduction to efficiency modules.[color=orange]\nIn the base game, the pollution multiplier depends only on the power consumption multiplier, which is capped at -80%. This pollution reduction multiplier can reduce the pollution further up to another -80%. The new formula is: pollution per second x power consumption multiplier [in %, capped at -80%] x pollution multiplier [in %, capped at -80%][/color]\nWith this it is possible to reduce pollution up to 4% of the original value, but this is mainly used to counterbalance the large energy consumption multipliers of fully beaconed setups and make higher tiers of efficiency modules a viable option. (Default: enabled)

Krastorio2_Modules.description: [color=orange]With the new modules fully beaconed Advanced assembling machines or Advanced chemical plants can reach such a high craft speed that some recipes can go over 60 operations per second, making the game engine not iterate all recipe cycles correctly. The game can only make 1 craft/tick (60 sec).[/color]\nEnable this option to multiply all numbers of the recipes that can reach that cap by 10. All ratios and input/sec and output/sec remain the same.\nWhile this is not enabled by default, it is advised to enable it once you reach the endgame and start using fully beaconed setups with the new modules of this mod. (Default: false)

Krastorio2_Modules_Updated.label: Fix speed capped recipes
Krastorio2_Modules_Updated.description: [color=orange]With the new modules fully beaconed Advanced assembling machines or Advanced chemical plants can reach such a high craft speed that some recipes can go over 60 operations per second, making the game engine not iterate all recipe cycles correctly. The game can only make 1 craft/tick (60 sec).[/color]\nEnable this option to multiply all numbers of the recipes that can reach that cap by 10. All ratios and input/sec and output/sec remain the same.\nWhile this is not enabled by default, it is advised to enable it once you reach the endgame and start using fully beaconed setups with the new modules of this mod. (Default: false)

Krastorio2_Modules.label: Recipes whitelist
Krastorio2_Modules.description:
Add a name of a recipe to this list to have it included in the list of recipes being modified by the recipe speed cap fix. By default, all recipes for Krastorio 2 and the base game of Factorio that require a change are already included. If you play with other mods that add recipes that you fully module, add them here.
[color=orange]Use this formula to determine if the recipe is affected by the speed cap limitation:
[max machine speed] x [max productivity bonus] / (60 x [crafting time])
If this is bigger than 1 the recipe will be affected by the limitation and should be added to this list if you plan to fully speed module it.
[/color]For example, to include the recipes of electronic circuits and advanced circuits (alredy enabled by default) use the following formatting:
electronic-circuit, advanced-circuit
[color=orange]Enable F4 ➜ show_debug_info_in_tooltips and hover over a recipe to get its recipe-name in case you are not sure if the name is correct. If the same name appears on the whitelist, the blacklist takes priority.[/color]

MoreSciencePacks.label: Dynamic stacksizes (fix loss)
MoreSciencePacks.description: Sets stacksizes for packs based on output (IF stacksize is less than max yield). New feature. Untested. May require corrections / simplification. Report issues if found.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Tech-Tree Scanning Permutations:
MoreSciencePacks.description: Due to the data-ordering method LUA uses for technology, more permutations are required for complex tech trees. If some technology isn't getting the packs added to them that they should (based on those required by the research's prerequisites) a higher number may be required. In testing 2-5 is usually sufficient for most mod-pack-selections.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Due to the data-ordering method LUA uses for technology, more permutations are required for complex tech trees. If some technology isn't getting the packs added to them that they should (based on those required by the research's prerequisites) a higher number may be required. MoreSciencePacks.label: Levels of Efficiency Research per MSP pack type (requires OmniLib):
MoreSciencePacks.description: If OmniLib is enabled, global results multiplier is ignored and this value is used instead. Technologies and recipes are generated dynamically and will auto-update all entities as research is completed. Each research level for each pack provides an additional yield equal to that pack's configured result value below (except for packs that would exceed MSP-OMNI maximum-yield, in which case, yield improvement is capped). Default: 10.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Levels of Efficiency Research per MSP pack type (requires OmniLib):
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: If OmniLib is enabled, global results multiplier is ignored and this value is used instead. Technologies and recipes are generated dynamically and will auto-update all entities as research is completed. Each research level for each pack provides an additional yield equal to that pack's configured result value below (except for packs that would exceed MSP-OMNI maximum-yield, in which case, yield improvement is capped). MoreSciencePacks.label: MSP-OMNI maximum-yield
MoreSciencePacks.description: If OmniLib is enabled, efficiency techs improve yield for science-crafting. This sets a max yield amount and staggers improvement/per-research-level to fit within this set boundary (designed as a limit to Module Science and Atomic Bomb science yields). Default: 400.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: MSP-OMNI maximum-yield
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: If OmniLib is enabled, efficiency techs improve yield for science-crafting. This sets a max yield amount and staggers improvement/per-research-level to fit within this set boundary (designed as a limit to Module Science and Atomic Bomb science yields). Default: 400.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Include Legacy recipes (Does nothing if OmniLib is disabled)
MoreSciencePacks.description: Ignored if omniLib is disabled. If OmniLib is enabled, this re-inserts the original recipe for each pack type into the technologies that enable their efficiency research. These basic recipes do not meet the format being searched-for when omniLib auto-updates all entities after research completes, thus, to benefit from efficiency, if these early recipes are enabled alongside OmniLib, assembly machines must have their recipes updated to the first level  of efficiency before they begin auto-updating as efficiency levels improve. Default: False.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Ignored if omniLib is disabled. These basic recipes do not meet the format being searched-for when omniLib auto-updates all entities after research completes, thus, to benefit from efficiency, if these early recipes are enabled alongside OmniLib, assembly machines must have their recipes updated to the first level  of efficiency before they begin auto-updating as efficiency levels improve. Default: False.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Cross-Mod Integration Engine
MoreSciencePacks.description: Mod integration function written by usafphoenix. Adds science packs to non-blacklisted modded technologies. This should not result in a game that is impossible to research any specific technologies, but under very specific conditions this may occur. If it does, you can either add the technology to the blacklist (and this mod will no longer add science packs to the ingredient list, or submit a bug report listing what technologies are impossible. please provide modlist and modsettings info and screenshots that show why the technology can't be completed..)

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Cross-Mod Integration Engine
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Mod integration function written by usafphoenix. Adds science packs to non-blacklisted modded technologies. This should not result in a game that is impossible to research any specific technologies, but under very specific conditions this may occur. If it does, you can either add the technology to the blacklist (and this mod will no longer add science packs to the ingredient list, or submit a bug report listing what technologies are impossible. please provide modlist and modsettings info and screenshots that show why the technology can't be completed..)

MoreSciencePacks.label: Reset recipe unlocks to vanilla
MoreSciencePacks.description: Reset the location of MSP pack ingredient recipe_unlocks to the vanilla setting. For some items, this will mean the item can be crafted from the start of the game. for others, it will mean reversing the change another mod made to the game progression. This can resolve certain game progression issues, or may cause them, but this function can be toggled on and off.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Reset recipe unlocks to vanilla
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Reset the location of MSP pack ingredient recipe_unlocks to the vanilla setting. For some items, this will mean the item can be crafted from the start of the game. for others, it will mean reversing the change another mod made to the game progression. This can resolve certain game progression issues, or may cause them, but this function can be toggled on and off.

MoreSciencePacks.label: unlock all packs from start of game
MoreSciencePacks.description: Begin the game with the recipes for all 30 MSP science packs enabled without requiring any research to make the packs. This does not extend to the ingredients required to craft the packs, so they won't be able to be crafted until you obtain the necessary ingredients, but this is another method for resolving cyclic-dependency conflicts caused by other mods. Options are nice.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: unlock all packs from start of game
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Begin the game with the recipes for all 30 MSP science packs enabled without requiring any research to make the packs. This does not extend to the ingredients required to craft the packs, so they won't be able to be crafted until you obtain the necessary ingredients, but this is another method for resolving cyclic-dependency conflicts caused by other mods. Options are nice.

MoreSciencePacks.label: 30 Packs are Intermediates
MoreSciencePacks.description: Use with "Remove packs from research cost (Game Progression Fix)" as well as MomoTweaks mod to treat MSP's 30 Packs as Intermediate crafting ingredients for vanilla packs only. Removes slots from labs, and slightly simplifies logistic headache....at a cost of even more complex crafting. DO NOT TOGGLE THIS during a game with active labs or labs containing MSP packs.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: 30 Packs are Intermediates
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Use with "Remove packs from research cost (Game Progression Fix)" as well as MomoTweaks mod to treat MSP's 30 Packs as Intermediate crafting ingredients for vanilla packs only. Removes slots from labs, and slightly simplifies logistic headache....at a cost of even more complex crafting. DO NOT TOGGLE THIS during a game with active labs or labs containing MSP packs.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Economics Integration
MoreSciencePacks.description: Allow Purchase of Packs using AllAboutMoneyMod. Recipes are less efficient than crafting the packs using their primary recipe, but in a difficult situation, sometimes the cost can be worth it. Included as a secondary method for dealing with mod incompatibilities or game progression issues.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Economics Integration
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Allow Purchase of Packs using AllAboutMoneyMod. Recipes are less efficient than crafting the packs using their primary recipe, but in a difficult situation, sometimes the cost can be worth it. Included as a secondary method for dealing with mod incompatibilities or game progression issues.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Debug Logging
MoreSciencePacks.description: Print information to the log file stating which science packs this mod attempts to add to technologies. Error messages resulting in technologies not existing will print to the log file regardless of what is selected, most-helpful for mod-integration programming by the authors. (Default: False)

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Debug Logging
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Print information to the log file stating which science packs this mod attempts to add to technologies. Error messages resulting in technologies not existing will print to the log file regardless of what is selected, most-helpful for mod-integration programming by the authors. (Default: False)

MoreSciencePacks.label: Debugging: Error on Fail (terminates game if error detected)
MoreSciencePacks.description: Force the game to quit if MSP detects situations that may prevent game completion, such as: impossible science progression, incomplete technology tree parsing, or inability to add correct science packs to vanilla or modded technology. Backup your modsettings.dat file before enabling! (Default: False)

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Debugging: Error on Fail (terminates game if error detected)
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Force the game to quit if MSP detects situations that may prevent game completion, such as: impossible science progression, incomplete technology tree parsing, or inability to add correct science packs to vanilla or modded technology. Backup your modsettings.dat file before enabling! (Default: False)

MoreSciencePacks.label: Remove packs from research cost (Game Progression Fix)
MoreSciencePacks.description: Will remove All MSP packs from technology costs. For scenarios where game progression is impossible due to mod-conflict, and a player is unsure which packs to disable, or just wishes to complete a few technologies without MSP pack requirements. This will not alter recipes or items, but simply prevent MSP packs from being required in labs to complete research. Enable this temporarily to quickly resolve cyclic-dependency issues that prevent game progression, or permanently if you wish to play a (slightly-easier) game with Momo +(30)Science Mod. If you wish to disable a specific pack, however, set the output ("result") of that pack to "0" below.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Remove packs from research cost (Game Progression Fix)
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Will remove All MSP packs from technology costs. For scenarios where game progression is impossible due to mod-conflict, and a player is unsure which packs to disable, or just wishes to complete a few technologies without MSP pack requirements. This will not alter recipes or items, but simply prevent MSP packs from being required in labs to complete research. Enable this temporarily to quickly resolve cyclic-dependency issues that prevent game progression, or permanently if you wish to play a (slightly-easier) game with Momo +(30)Science Mod. If you wish to disable a specific pack, however, set the output ("result") of that pack to "0" below.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Increase module science (MSP 18) cost
MoreSciencePacks.description: Change which modules (or how many) are required for MSP pack 18, Module Science. You may wish to increase result_count as well when playing with a very costly recipe variation. Note: if bob's modules aren't enabled, or the items are interferred with by another mod, this may result in MSP 18 requiring (n)-number of tier-2 modules, instead as a backup.

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Increase module science (MSP 18) cost
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Change which modules (or how many) are required for MSP pack 18, Module Science. You may wish to increase result_count as well when playing with a very costly recipe variation. Note: if bob's modules aren't enabled, or the items are interferred with by another mod, this may result in MSP 18 requiring (n)-number of tier-2 modules, instead as a backup.

MoreSciencePacks.label: Module tier required for MSP 18:
MoreSciencePacks.description: Module tier (or quantity) required for MSP 18. Minimum: 1, Default: 2, Maximum: 16. Values 1-3 are standard modules. Values 4+ will either choose modules based upon bob's modules (if enabled) or will increase the quantity of modules required per crafting operation. (values 4-8 correspond to bob's modules of same value); Tier 9-16 correspond to the raw-variety of modules the mod adds (if enabled in config). If the chosen module tier cannot be found by MSP, (or bob's modules isn't enabled at all), ingredient amounts will be increased instead (only applies for values 4+).

MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.label: Module tier required for MSP 18:
MoreSciencePacks-for1_1.description: Module tier (or quantity) required for MSP 18. Minimum: 1, Default: 2, Maximum: 16. Values 1-3 are standard modules. Values 4+ will either choose modules based upon bob's modules (if enabled) or will increase the quantity of modules required per crafting operation. (values 4-8 correspond to bob's modules of same value); Tier 9-16 correspond to the raw-variety of modules the mod adds (if enabled in config). If the chosen module tier cannot be found by MSP, (or bob's modules isn't enabled at all), ingredient amounts will be increased instead (only applies for values 4+).

ctg.label: Enable mod
ctg.description: Uncheck this to disable this mod entirely.

ctg.label: Remove default water
ctg.description: Suppresses Factorio's default water generation. If you uncheck this, water will be generated both by Factorio and by this mod. You probably want to leave this option on.

ctg.label: Water color
ctg.description: Water can be blue or green. Green water absorbs 5/6 as much pollution as blue water.

ctg.label: Terrain preset
ctg.description: Choose which terrain generation pattern you would like to use. See the example screenshots for an idea of what each of the suggested options generates. Or, use "custom" to program your own terrain generation pattern below.

ctg.label: Custom terrain pattern
ctg.description: If you chose "custom" above, this setting should be a lua expression that specifies the desired terrain pattern. See the README and examples for details. If your expression is very long, you can use variables called "v1" through "v8" whose values you specify below.

ctg.label: v1 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v1". You can use "v2" through "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v2 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v2". You can use "v3" through "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v3 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v3". You can use "v4" through "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v4 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v4". You can use "v5" through "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v5 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v5". You can use "v6" through "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v6 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v6". You can use "v7" and "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v7 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v7". You can use "v8" here. Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: v8 =
ctg.description: A lua expression whose value will be saved in the variable "v8". Leave it as "nil" if you do not need it.

ctg.label: Random seed
ctg.description: If 0, then a random seed will be randomly chosen at the beginning of the game. Otherwise for values 1 to 2^32, specifies a seed for the random number generator. If the same seed is used with the same settings, then the same map will be generated. (If in doubt, just use 0.)

ctg.label: Spawn landfill chest
ctg.description: If enabled, start the game with a steel chest filled with landfill.

ctg.label: Force starting water
ctg.description: Creates a puddle next to the origin

ctg.label: Big scan
ctg.description: Testing feature: Scan a large area at the beginning of the game

ctg.label: Take screenshot
ctg.description: Testing feature: Take a screenshot of the map (use included python script)

ctg.label: Take zoomed screenshot
ctg.description: Testing feature: Take a zoomed screenshot of the map (use included python script). Can be slow!
If disabled, the map will be generated with no water and the remaining water settings will have no effect.

creative-mode.label: Unhide items
creative-mode.description: Unhide the items and entities provided by Creative Mode from the slot filters, so you can select them in matter source's filters, logistic requester slots, deconstruction filters, etc. But they will be visible even when Creative Mode is not enabled in the game.

creative-mode.label: Creative chest size
creative-mode.description:
Usable inventory size of each __ENTITY__creative-mode_creative-chest__ and __ENTITY__creative-mode_creative-provider-chest__.
An extra slot will be added for trashing.
Its value affects how many chests you need to place for one item cycle. Larger inventory size means fewer chests are needed. However, it is also more likely to cause performance issue when hovering the chests.
Changing its value for an existing game will cause item regrouping.

creative-mode.label: Creative chests contain hidden items
creative-mode.description: Whether __ENTITY__creative-mode_creative-chest__ and __ENTITY__creative-mode_creative-provider-chest__ should contain hidden items.\nSome items are hidden for good reasons, like rocket parts, which is meaningless even if you can get it.\nChanging this value for an existing game will cause item regrouping.

Clockwork.label: Daylength Multiplier
Clockwork.description: Multiplier on the total length of a day/night solar cycle. A vanilla day is 6 minutes, 56.6 seconds. Example: setting this to 4 will result in a 27 minute 47 second day.\nWarning: You can change this setting at any time, but accumulator capacity modification requires a restart.

Clockwork.label: Dusk Start Time
Clockwork.description: Time when dusk starts. These values cannot be equal and must be in this order from least to greatest:\ndusk -> evening -> morning -> dawn.\nBy default, 0.5 (the midpoint between evening and morning) is midnight.

Clockwork.label: Evening Start Time
Clockwork.description: Time when evening starts. The night is darkest after this time. These values cannot be equal and must be in this order from least to greatest:\ndusk -> evening -> morning -> dawn.\nFor a longer night, make Evening and Morning further apart.

Clockwork.label: Morning Start Time
Clockwork.description: Time when morning starts. The darkest night is over after this time. These values cannot be equal and must be in this order from least to greatest:\ndusk -> evening -> morning -> dawn.

Clockwork.label: Dawn Start Time
Clockwork.description: Time when dawn starts. These values cannot be equal and must be in this order from least to greatest:\ndusk -> evening -> morning -> dawn.

Clockwork.label: Sun Never Rises
Clockwork.description: Neverending night mode. Once it sets, the sun never rises.\nDisable while a map is running to resume the normal day/night cycle.

Clockwork.label: Grace Before First Night (minutes)
Clockwork.description: Delay before the first night comes in minutes. For use with 'Sun Never Rises'.\nChanging this while a map is running will restart the grace period from the beginning.

Clockwork.label: Warn When Grace Ends
Clockwork.description: Provides a warning when the neverending night is coming.

Clockwork.label: Adjust Accumulator Capacity
Clockwork.description: Adjusts the capacity of accumulators to be proportionate to the new overall cycle length.

Clockwork.label: Capacity Multiplier
Clockwork.description: Capacity multiplier of accumulator. This should usually be the same as "Daylength Multiplier", but exists as a separate setting since accumulators cannot be changed dynamically.

Clockwork.label: Enable Flares
Clockwork.description: Enables an early game light source: flare capsules that can be thrown. Duration scales with the accumulator capacity multiplier.

Clockwork.label: Start Time
Clockwork.description: Time of day the game will start at. Default of 0.0 is high noon (12:00pm) with vanilla dawn and dusk settings. This should not be set to night time if you're using "Grace Before First Night". This setting only takes effect on a new game, or when Sun Never Rises is changed to enabled.

Clockwork.label: Pitch Black Nights
Clockwork.description: Nights are completely black - nothing can be seen without lights.

Clockwork.label: Multi-Surface Mode
Clockwork.description: Clockwork will attempt to determine which surfaces represent outdoors areas (such as other planets), and apply its settings to all of these surfaces. Disable this if Clockwork interferes with surfaces other mods add.

Clockwork.label: Disable Nightvision
Clockwork.description: Disables the power armor nightvision recipe and technology. Factorio will crash if no nightvision item/equipment exists, so if this setting is enabled in a running game, already-built NV is rendered inert rather than removed.

bobrevamp.label: Nuclear power overhaul
bobrevamp.description: If enabled, this setting will change nuclear reactor 2 into a thorium reactor, and nuclear reactor 3 into a deuterium reactor, and restructure research accordingly.

bobsmodslocale.label: Nuclear power overhaul
bobsmodslocale.description: If enabled, this setting will change nuclear reactor 2 into a thorium reactor, and nuclear reactor 3 into a deuterium reactor, and restructure research accordingly.

bobrevamp.label: Oil and sulfur overhaul
bobrevamp.description: If enabled, this setting will make changes to the oil processing production chain.\nIt also removes base game sulfur and sulfuric acid recipes and adds a means to get sulfur and sulfur dioxide if MCI is installed.

bobsmodslocale.label: Oil and sulfur overhaul
bobsmodslocale.description: If enabled, this setting will make changes to the oil processing production chain.\nIt also removes base game sulfur and sulfuric acid recipes and adds a means to get sulfur and sulfur dioxide if MCI is installed.

bobrevamp.label: New oil and sulfur overhaul
bobrevamp.description:
If enabled, this setting will make more realistic changes to the oil processing chain.
It replaces the petroleum gas output of oil processing with sour gas, which can be processed into petroleum gas.
It removes base game sulfur and sulfuric acid recipes and adds hydrogen sulfide to the sour gas processing recipe if MCI is installed.
it will take priority over the older oil and sulfur overhaul.

bobsmodslocale.label: New oil and sulfur overhaul
bobsmodslocale.description:
If enabled, this setting will make more realistic changes to the oil processing chain.
It replaces the petroleum gas output of oil processing with sour gas, which can be processed into petroleum gas.
It removes base game sulfur and sulfuric acid recipes and adds hydrogen sulfide to the sour gas processing recipe if MCI is installed.
it will take priority over the older oil and sulfur overhaul.

bobrevamp.label: Extra chemistry
bobrevamp.description: If enabled, this setting will expand some of the simplified chemical processes to make them more realistic.\nThis will effect Nitrogen dioxide, Nitric acid, Sulfuric acid, Lithium perchlorate, Calcium chloride, sodium carbonate, Cobalt oxide and Petroleum gas cracking to Hydrogen recipes.

KrastorioPorted.label: Difficult gold

KrastorioPorted.label: Add loaders

KrastorioPorted.label: Clean concrete
KrastorioPorted.description: Set Decorative Removal = 95% for vanilla covering. If this option turn on, then when you place a ground covering, such as concrete, grass and bushes will be removed with a 95% probability. If this option turn off, then you have grass and bushes on you concrete and stone bricks (vanilla).

KrastorioPorted.label: Remove infinite oil
KrastorioPorted.description: Remove infinite oil. It's ok and recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: Nuclear rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Everything is redone. Now you can build compact and powerfull Nuclear stations. It's very efficient and ups-frendly, but produce fuel become much more expensive. In vanilla 100k uranium ore give 3k uranium-235, now around 0.8k-1k. Also reduced bonus from a neighbor and...never destroy a working reactor! This part of mod highly recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: Increase stacks size
KrastorioPorted.description: Increases stacks. Mainly for resources.

KrastorioPorted.label: Change bullets recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Adds coal into the "firearm magazine" recipe and makes "piercing rounds magazine" cheaper.

KrastorioPorted.label: Slightly improve vanilla fuel
KrastorioPorted.description: Useful option if you play with difficult enemies. You can also disable this option if you want to complicate the game.

KrastorioPorted.label: Improve power poles
KrastorioPorted.description: Increases the size of the supply area and the length of the connection.

KrastorioPorted.label: Science packs rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: More balanced recipes for Krastorio. Highly recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: Bob's Enemies rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Rebalances enemies for using with Krastorio. Highly recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: Technology rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Changes vanilla technology. Highly recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: Keep infinite technology
KrastorioPorted.description: If technology rebalance is enabled, and this option is enabled, infinite technologies remain infinite(and other become infinite), otherwise will be limited (default: false)

KrastorioPorted.label: Circuits rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Changes recipes for circuits. Highly recommended.

KrastorioPorted.label: More waste!
KrastorioPorted.description: Adds stone into recipe for enriching iron and copper.

KrastorioPorted.label: Powerful beacon
KrastorioPorted.description: Makes "Singularity beacon" twice as powerful. That is, makes it the same as it was before version 1.2.11. The beacon had to be changed because it was too powerful and caused some bugs in the game. Enabling this option is NOT RECOMMENDED, but if the update broke your factory or ratios, then you can enable it. It will not break your game. More information about this bug is written in the changelog (1.2.11 update).

KrastorioPorted.label: More train cargo space with more fuel consume
KrastorioPorted.description: If enabled, train cargo space is higher but train will consume more fuel, this is meant for reduce train deliveries (default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Damage rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Rebalance all damage done by player weapons (Turrets, ammo...)(default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Damage bonuses rebalance
KrastorioPorted.description: Rebalance the bonus given by technologies to ammo and turrets damage and attack speed(default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Double beacon slots
KrastorioPorted.description: Doubles the beacon module slot(default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Productivity beacon
KrastorioPorted.description: Enable productivity effect in beacons and in singularity beacons(default: disabled)

ZRecycling.label: The scaling factor of items required

From the drop-down, select the scaling factor of items you must insert into the Recycling Machine before you get the original ingredients back.

E.g. With a scaling factor of 1 you would recycle 1 electronic circuit to produce 1 iron plate and 3 copper cables.

With a scaling factor of 2, you would need 2 circuits to get back the same amount of plate and cable.

 If the scaling count exceeds the stack_size it, is adjusted downwards.

ZRecycling.label: Recycling Machine Crafting Speed Relative To Assembling
ZRecycling.description:
Slow down the Recycling Machines Crafting Speed relative to the equivalent Assembly Machines.
Select a value from the drop-down.
= means that Recycling Machine crafts at the same speed as the Assembling Machine.
1/2 means that a Recycling Machine crafts at half the speed of of an Assembling Machine, etc.

bobtech.label: Burner power phase
bobtech.description:
Locks non-burner powered technology behind research.
Warning:
This setting is not designed to work with with AAI Industry, which also adds a lot of early stage research. Key conflicting areas include the fact that this mod sees Steam power as something that comes between Burner and Electricity (See steam powered assembling machine and mining drill as examples), where AAI changes the offshore pump to require electricity, and the boiler, and steam engine are a more advanced method to get electricity after the burner electric generator.
In some situations, the game fails to load if this option is turned on when AAI Industry is installed.

production-monitor.label:
Production Statistics Monitor: 
-Right click this button to toggle show/hide everything but this button. 
-Left click this button with an empty cursor to open a fluid selection window (left click this button again to close fluid window). 
-Click this button with an item in cursor to add the item. 
-Overwrite an item by dropping it on an existing item. 
-Once added Left click an item to move up, Right Click to move down. 
-Middle click or left/right click + modifier key (default:shift) to delete.

wireless-power.description: Normal efficiency will impose a large percentage cost to power transferred over each tesseract. High-Efficiency halves that cost. Perfect removes all percentage costs. Warning: Perfect will greatly reduce the benefit of advancing to the higher tiers of Tesseract.
Normal efficiency will impose a huge percentage cost to the power grid to use. High-Efficiency halves that cost.

Enables the global power drain incurred for having at least one Tesseract placed of a given tier. The drain starts at 1MW and is multiplied by 5 for each tier of Tesseract that is placed. eg, having any Tesseract MK2s costs 5 MW and having any Tesseract MK3s costs 25. If disabled, higher tiers of Tesseract have no downside to use besides the cost of materials.
Enables the warmup phase where each new tesseract placed on the map requires a certain amount of power before it becomes operational.
If true, personal tesseracts will only output 65% of their normal power.
Enables some debugging messages to the console.

SupplyDrop.label: Oversized drop should overflow into more crates:

RealisticReactors.label: Reactor power output and efficiency
RealisticReactors.description:
This setting controls the power output and fuel efficiency of the reactors.

Ownly's calculation gives you slightly different behaviour for different fuel cell types. The maximum output and efficiency will always be on the highest temperature (+10% per neighbour).

With Ingo's calculation you have to monitor the temperature more carefully. If you want to have a maximum output with good efficiency, you have to connect your reactors (max 4). On a single reactor the efficiency will drop quickly with high temperatures.

See the forum post or the included ODT-charts (-> mod folder) for more details on both modes

RealisticReactors.label: Static power consumption for ECCS
RealisticReactors.description: When static is chosen, the reactor will consume 1 MW while the core is being cooled by ECCS.\nOtherwise it will consume 1 MW per 20 MW of cooling

RealisticReactors.label: SCRAM behavior
RealisticReactors.description:
limit to current cell = The reactor will slowly power down until the scam duration is over or the current fuel cell is depleted.

stop half-empty = Reactor will take another fuel cell if current one depletes before SCRAM duration is over. The cell will stay half-consumed in the reactor when it stops.

consume additional cell = Same as above but the cell will be depleted when the reactor stops.

decay heat (v1.0.x)= Current fuel is removed and decay heat is produced by script (like in version 1.0.x)

RealisticReactors.label: Lifetime of the radioactive clouds
RealisticReactors.description: Sets the duration (in seconds) how long radioactive clouds will stay\n(1 - 80 - 9999999)

RealisticReactors.label: How long to emit radioactive clouds on meltdown?
RealisticReactors.description: When the reactor melts, it will emit radioactive clouds from the condensed water. The clouds will move over the map affected by the wind.\nSet a duration for how many seconds this will happen\n(0 - 100 - 9999999)

RealisticReactors.label: Nuclear fallout appearance
RealisticReactors.description:
Invisible = You will only notice the contaminated area by the geiger-counter sound

Half-transparent = floating orange particles

Less transparent = Same as above, but better visible

Green veil = The area will get colored green, but very hard to see in zones with low radiation

RealisticReactors.label: Lifetime of nuclear fallout
RealisticReactors.description: Sets the duration (in seconds) how long fallout contamination will stay\n(1 - 600 - 9999999)

shia-clear-inserter.label: General: Use locked chest slots
shia-clear-inserter.description: If a cest does have locked slots, they will be unlocked before putting back items and locked again afterwards. If the chests normally are stuffed with items, that may be helpfull to have a save way to always clean the inserters.

shia-clear-inserter.label: Combinator: Ignore combinator "OFF"-setting
shia-clear-inserter.description: If not checked, inserters in front of the combinater will not be affected if the combinator output is set to "OFF".

shia-clear-inserter.label: Combinator: Ignore one missing inserter in line
shia-clear-inserter.description: If disabled, the check will stop as soon as it does not encounter an inserter. If enabled, 2 spaces will be checked and only stops if both are empty.

shia-clear-inserter.label: Train: Check trains directly
shia-clear-inserter.description: Will do the check for any train leaving a station (if arrived in automatic mode and is not empty at leaving). The check will be done for the areas on both sides of every cargo wagon connected to the train. Wagons which are not aligned horizontally or vertically will be skipped!

shia-clear-inserter.label: Train: Area to check in width
shia-clear-inserter.description: Set the width of the area to check at the sides of every cargo wagon. If facing upwards, the area extends to the left and right. (Facing sidewards it sets the range for up and down.)

shia-clear-inserter.label: Train: Extend area to check in length
shia-clear-inserter.description: Increase the area in length. If facing up/down, the area also extends up and down OVER the length of the wagon. (Facing sidewards the area extends to left and right over the length of the wagon).

shia-clear-inserter.label: Deconstruction: Use with deconstruction planer
shia-clear-inserter.description: "off" will do nothing when deconstructing. "inserter only" will be the normal behavior of just cleaning the inserter. "inserter and ground" will clean the inserter and also the area at the drop position of the inserter if there is an item on the ground. Will skip this if the item is on a different entity like a belt.

shia-clear-inserter.label: Cleaning Planner: Split by count
shia-clear-inserter.description: Only inserters in full automatic cleaning mode: If disabled, the calculation of all inserters will be split over the count of frames which is set at the "Split value" (60 = 1 second / at least one inserter per frame). If active, every frame will run the check for the number of inserters set at "Split value".

shia-clear-inserter.label: Cleaning Planner: Split value
shia-clear-inserter.description: The count of either the frames or the inserters. Please see the "Split by count" tooltip.

shia-clear-inserter.label: General: Cleaning effect
shia-clear-inserter.description: Shows a small visual effect every time a cleaning happens. "off" disables this function. "laser" shots a laser beam from start-point to end-point of each cleaning. (This are just visual effects and doesn't do anyhing to the game itself / also runs if a cleaning was NOT succesfull)

shia-clear-inserter.label: Cleaning Planner: Visual indicator
shia-clear-inserter.description: Shows a visual indicator for inserters in full automatic mode. "off" disables this function. "arrow" shows a small arrow in the opposite direction of the inserter. "cloud" shows a small cloud at the inserter. (This are just visual effects and doesn't do anyhing to the game itself)

boblibrary.label: Enable Bob's resource generator
boblibrary.description: This library contains a Resource generator for 0.17, based on the 0.17 resource generator system. However, the version as part of 0.17.51 of Factorio fixes a lot of issues that this resource generator attempted to fix in the older version, and is no longer needed.\nThe library will check if the new generator is available and use it automatically, or use this generator if it is not, however, this option is available to force enable my custom generator even if you're using the newer version of Factorio.

bobsmodslocale.description: This library contains a Resource generator for 0.17, based on the 0.17 resource generator system. However, the version as part of 0.17.51 of Factorio fixes a lot of issues that this resource generator attempted to fix in the older version, and is no longer needed.\nThe library will check if the new generator is available and use it automatically, or use this generator if it is not, however, this option is available to force enable my custom generator even if you're using the newer version of Factorio.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Turn on everything
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Turns on every feature in the mod, except for the electric furnace changes. Because it completely overwrites the recipe, it isn't completely compatible with any changes another mod might make.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Bob electronics compat fixes
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: This setting controls whether or not my mod will update some other mods recipes that use "electronic-circuit" to use "basic-circuit" if and only if bob's electronics is present. This is to fix issues in mods such as hacked splitters where they don't update to the basic boards when the normal ones do.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Cheaper circuit network tech
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Removes the green science packs from the circuit network tech.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Updates to the loader tech
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Changes the first loader tech (from 5dim's automization mod) to only use red science packs.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Move 5dim's loader unlock location
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Moves the unlock tech for 5dim's loader. It keeps the tech in the same spot, so there's no worries about compatability.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Tweaks for belt sorter mod
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Moves the first belt sorter to the logistics tech. Because it's a logistical thing. Makes sense to me.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Electric furnace tech change
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: This setting moves the electric furnace to the logistics tech, so it can be unlocked much earlier in the game.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Furnace recipe change
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Enables the recipe change for the electric furnace to use green circuits instead of red ones.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Landfill tech change
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Removes the green science pack cost from the landfill tech.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: Science pack & lab fix
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Removes tin from the red science pack and the lab if you have 5dim's ores and Angel's Refining mods.

GN Factorio Tweaks.label: More Science Packs & Angel's refining patch
GN Factorio Tweaks.description: Changes the recipe for the first pack from more science packs to use the base Angel's refining ores, instead of the vanilla iron & copper, which can cause early-game to be extremely difficult.

Noxys_Trees.label: Tree dying factor from fire
Noxys_Trees.description:
Percentage of how many trees should be removed after they've been burnt by fire.
Vanilla default is 0.8 (80%).

Set this to 0 to not alter this behavior.

Noxys_Trees.label: Emmision multiplier
Noxys_Trees.description: A multiplier of how much pollution is consumes by trees.

Noxys_Trees.label: Enabled
Noxys_Trees.description: When enabled trees will spread and die.

Noxys_Trees.label: Debug mode
Noxys_Trees.description: Enables the output of debug messages.

Noxys_Trees.label: Debug Interval
Noxys_Trees.description: The interval in ticks between debug messages.

Noxys_Trees.label: Degrade tiles
Noxys_Trees.description: Over time slowly degrades floor tiles that block tree growth until the trees can grow there again.

Noxys_Trees.label: Overpopulation kills trees
Noxys_Trees.description: If a chunk is overpopulated it will slowly kill off trees at random in that chunk.

Noxys_Trees.label: Kill trees near unwanted
Noxys_Trees.description: Randomly kills trees that are near biter bases, uranium ore or player entities. This also affects the death of trees by lack of fertility or too much pollution.

Noxys_Trees.label: Ticks between operations
Noxys_Trees.description: Allows fine grained control over the performance of this mod and the speed at which the trees expand.

Noxys_Trees.label: Chunks per operation
Noxys_Trees.description: Allows fine grained control over the performance of this mod and the speed at which the trees expand.

Noxys_Trees.label: Enable chunks per operation scaling bias
Noxys_Trees.description:
Allows fine grained control over the performance of this mod and the speed at which the trees expand.

WARNING: This option makes tree growth more consistent throughout a playthrough but will cost more performance the bigger the map becomes.

Therefore this is a choice between consistent performance versus consistent tree spreading.

Noxys_Trees.label: Chunks per operation scaling bias
Noxys_Trees.description: Allows fine grained control over the performance of this mod and the speed at which the trees expand.\n\nChunks per operation are multiplied with the total chunks divided by this value (if enabled) (this * (TotalChunks / ScalingBias)).

Noxys_Trees.label: Minimum distance between trees
Noxys_Trees.description: Minimum distance between trees for trees to be able to grow.

Noxys_Trees.label: Minimum distance to enemies
Noxys_Trees.description: Minimum distance to enemy bases or worms for trees to be able to grow.

Noxys_Trees.label: Minimum distance to uranium ore
Noxys_Trees.description: Minimum distance to uranium ore for trees to be able to grow.

Noxys_Trees.label: Minimum distance to player entities
Noxys_Trees.description: Minimum distance to player entities for trees to be able to grow.\n\nSet this to 0 to skip this check and thus slightly increase performance.

Noxys_Trees.label: Minimum distance to degradable tiles
Noxys_Trees.description: Minimum distance to tiles that are considered to be degradabel (regardless of if tile degredation is enabled or not). Set to 0 to disable this check.\n\nWARNING: This option impacts performance more than any of the other "minimum distance" options and has a potential to cause periodic lag spikes especially if you use larger numbers.

Noxys_Trees.label: Tree deaths by lack of fertility minimum
Noxys_Trees.description: If the fertility of the ground is lower than this value the tree on top of it has a chance to die.

Noxys_Trees.label: Tree deaths by pollution bias
Noxys_Trees.description:
How quickly trees die from pollution.

Set this to 0 to disable deaths by pollution.

Additional trees attempted to be killed = math.ceil(pollution / this).

Noxys_Trees.label: Trees to grow per chunk percentage
Noxys_Trees.description:
Allows fine grained control over the performance of this mod and the speed at which the trees expand.

Each chunk will at least try to generate one tree but this percentage can increase it to more based on the existing trees in the chunk.

If the percentage is 0.01 (1%) and the chunk has 200 trees it will try to generate 2 additional trees per operation.

Noxys_Trees.label: Maximum trees per chunk
Noxys_Trees.description: If there are more trees than this number in a chunk it will not expand any trees in that chunk.\n(Vanilla dense forests seem to be around 512 trees per chunk)

Noxys_Trees.label: Expansion distance
Noxys_Trees.description: How far in tiles a tree can generate from its originating tree.

Noxys_Trees.label: Surfaces
Noxys_Trees.description: A comma seperated list of all the surfaces the tree mod should be active on.\n\nBy default this is only '1' which is 'Nauvis'.

Geothermal.label: Geothermal wells need water input
Geothermal.description: Should the geothermal wells require water input, or should the water be 'provided' by the well? Requiring input makes logistics much more complicated. Note that changing this means you will have to replace any existing wells.

Geothermal.label: Geothermal power production multiplier
Geothermal.description: Adjust this to control how much power geothermal plants provide.

Geothermal.label: Geothermal fluid production multiplier
Geothermal.description: Adjust this to control how much fluid each well provides. Directly correlates to per-well generation capacity, where each 25% increase represents 1-2 more steam engines. At 1x, each well can run 1.2 exchangers, which is about 3 steam engines at 1x power multiplier.

Geothermal.label: Generation Frequency
Geothermal.description: A multiplier to control how often geothermal patches will generate.

Geothermal.label: Generation Patch Size
Geothermal.description: A multiplier to control how large geothermal regions are. Has no effect with AlienBiomes installed.

Geothermal.label: Enable colored geothermal patches
Geothermal.description: AlienBiomes compatibility; Whether the geothermal patches spawning in colored magma biomes take on that color, as well as a chemical impurity representing that color.

Geothermal.label: Geothermal biome rules
Geothermal.description: Which biomes the geothermal patches are permitted to spawn in. Note that they have hardcoded per-biome frequencies as well, and restricting to biomes that do not actually exist will be the same as selecting "everywhere".

Geothermal.label: Enable Insulated Fluid Wagon
Geothermal.description: Whether a thermally insulated version of the fluid wagon should be enabled, to permit carrying heated water without it losing its temperature.

Geothermal.label: Byproduct generation rate
Geothermal.description: A multiplier for the yield of byproducts from AlienBiomes colored geothermal patches.

research_causes_evolution.label: Evolution effect weighting
research_causes_evolution.description: How to weight evolution effect of technologies. Default is to increase more early, and then taper off, like vanilla evolution. Equal means all technologies have the same effect. Late gives a gentle start to the game, with later technologies effecting evolution more.

research_causes_evolution_grimerxfix.label: Evolution effect weighting
research_causes_evolution_grimerxfix.description: How to weight evolution effect of technologies. Default is to increase more early, and then taper off, like vanilla evolution. Equal means all technologies have the same effect. Late gives a gentle start to the game, with later technologies effecting evolution more.

research_causes_evolution.label: Include upgrades (recommended)
research_causes_evolution.description: Can (non-infinite) upgrade technologies contribute to evolution. Recommended for smoother evolution. The old behaviour of the mod was to ignore all upgrades.

research_causes_evolution_grimerxfix.label: Include upgrades (recommended)
research_causes_evolution_grimerxfix.description: Can (non-infinite) upgrade technologies contribute to evolution. Recommended for smoother evolution. The old behaviour of the mod was to ignore all upgrades.

RoboTank.label: Ammo check period
RoboTank.description: Time between checks for a RoboTank being out of ammo, in ticks.  Raising this improves performance a little, but tanks spend more frames without ammo.

RoboTank.label: Ammo magazines to load at once
RoboTank.description: When a RoboTank turret runs out of ammo, move this many magazines from tank inventory into the turret.  A larger number means the turret runs out, and hence momentarily stops firing, less often.

RoboTank.label: Diagnostic log verbosity
RoboTank.description: Adjusts the level of detail logged to factorio-current.log.  0: None, 1: Problems, 2: Squad maintenance events such as being stuck, 3: Changes to internal data structures, 4: Details of algorithms.

NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.label: The interval between tree grow cycle in ticks
NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.description: Standard 120 (60-360): lower value results in faster grows, rate of 60 seemed too high after exploring the world a bit.

NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.label: Hard limit on number of trees
NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.description: Standard 800k: Large number of trees takes time to save and load, any other aspect of the game gets slower. If you kill enough trees, they will start growing again.

NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.label: Threshold growth
NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.description: Standard 0.8: Threshold rate to start dropping grow speed: if numTrees < max_trees * tree_decrease_start

NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.label: Threshold pollution
NaturalTreeExpansionReloaded_016.description: Standard 1500: If pollution exceeds the threshold, trees will die in the area. There will be no new trees here.

better-air-filtering.label: Update interval
better-air-filtering.description: Updates are implemented efficiently and are spread over an UPDATE INTERVAL amount of ticks. The default of 20 gives three updates per second. 30 would result in 2 updates per second for example.

the-flood.label: Flood Speed

UtilizationMonitor.label: Enabled
UtilizationMonitor.description: Whether or not the mod should be enabled. This option is usefull if you want to measure a new part of your factory, but generally want to preserve FPS.

UtilizationMonitorBlargh.label: Enabled
UtilizationMonitorBlargh.description: Whether or not the mod should be enabled. This option is usefull if you want to measure a new part of your factory, but generally want to preserve FPS.

UtilizationMonitor.label: Show labels
UtilizationMonitor.description: Whether or not labels should be shown. The working time average will still be calculated.

UtilizationMonitorBlargh.label: Show labels
UtilizationMonitorBlargh.description: Whether or not labels should be shown. The working time average will still be calculated.

UtilizationMonitor.label: Updates per tick
UtilizationMonitor.description: The number of entities to update each tick. This has a great impact on performance.

UtilizationMonitorBlargh.label: Maximum updates per tick
UtilizationMonitorBlargh.description: The maximum number of entities to update each tick.  If this is insufficient to track all the entities needed, a console message will be generated (once), and this limit enforced, but the data will start being averaged over more than 60 seconds.

UtilizationMonitor.label: Iterations per label update
UtilizationMonitor.description: How many iterations of updates are run before the label is updated. The smaller the value is the smaller is the observed timespan of the entity.

math7-library.description: bool=Enable backtraces. Recommended for debugging and reporting bugs.

math7-library.label: bool=Trace-level logging
math7-library.description: bool=Enable full (trace-level) logging. For debugging only. This increases log size significantly.

Xagros_TUONELA_TurretDelay.label: Turret delay time
