Generic_Logistic_Chest.label: Error: __1__ generic chests could not be created because they no longer exist
Generic_Logistic_Chest.description: Error: __1__ generic chests could not be created because they no longer exist

Generic_Logistic_Chest.label: Different generic chest was placed, it will not be included when making a selection
Generic_Logistic_Chest.description: Different generic chest was placed, it will not be included when making a selection

Generic_Logistic_Chest.label: Chest Data Purge Period Length
Generic_Logistic_Chest.description: Length of time between chest data cleanup (for ghosts timing out) (Time in minutes)

Generic_Logistic_Chest.label: Fast Replace Lag
Generic_Logistic_Chest.description: Length of time (in ticks (60 UPS = 60 ticks per second)) to ignore fast replace of a generic chest onto a mod replacement chest. If this is too low then drag fast replacing generic chests onto normal logistic chests will convert directly to generic chests with the UI open. A high number means you will have to wait a little longer to fast replace from normal chest -> generic replacement -> generic.

FTweaks.label: Bigger material stack sizes
FTweaks.description: If true raw materials (ore, plates etc) stack to 200.

FTweaks.label: Cheaper steel
FTweaks.description: Bobplates-style; reduces cost to 2 iron per steel and halves smelt time.

FTweaks.label: Harder silo
FTweaks.description: Makes the rocket silo much harder both in terms of research and resources.

FTweaks.label: Force manual silo crafting
FTweaks.description: Forces manual-only crafting of rocket silos. Only meaningful with the Harder Silo option enabled.

FTweaks.label: Harder reactors
FTweaks.description: Greatly increases the technology progression required to research nuclear reactors.

FTweaks.label: Harder rockets
FTweaks.description: Makes the rocket launches more difficult by making the resultant noise SERIOUSLY upset the local wildlife.

FTweaks.label: Tiered armor
FTweaks.description: Makes the armor progression more natural; also makes each stage require the previous so that old armor still has value.

FTweaks.label: Smaller tree selection box
FTweaks.description: This halves the size of tree hitboxes, allowing easier placement of entities around them.

FTweaks.label: Enable Wood Decomposition
FTweaks.description: This controls two oil-processing recipes to convert wood - raw and planks - into oil products.

FTweaks.label: Enable Advanced Research Satellite
FTweaks.description: Should a tier-2 research satellite be obtainable? It has a higher space science yield per rocket (and per rocket cost), but costs far more to create.

FTweaks.label: Smarter Concrete
FTweaks.description: Whether to replace the iron ore in the concrete recipe with iron sticks, which is both more friendly to factory setups and more realistic.

FTweaks.label: Early-Game technology cost decrease factor
FTweaks.description: The factor by which to decrease the costs of a few entry-level technologies (eg Automation I) so that high-difficulty saves do not force the manual crafting of hundreds of science packs before they can begin to be automated. Usually equal to the technology price multipler.

FTweaks.label: Split Gun Turret recipe into manual and automated variants
FTweaks.description: Whether to split the gun turret recipe into a more-expensive-but-faster-to-craft manual version (for making early game defences less painful to build), and a slightly-cheaper-but slower version for assemblers.

FTweaks.label: Split Science Pack 1 recipe into manual and automated variants
FTweaks.description: Whether to split the red science pack recipe into a more-expensive-but-faster-to-craft manual version (for making the first research into automation less painful), and a slightly-cheaper-but slower version for assemblers.

FTweaks.label: Make each BobMod robot part require the previous tier
FTweaks.description: If enabled, this changes the recipes for BobMod robot parts - frames, tools, and robot brains - so that each tier is crafted from the previous tier plus the difference in cost in original recipes (eg if T4 costs 4 CPUs and 6 transitors, and T3 0 CPUs and 2 Transistors, the T4 will now cost 4 CPUs, 4 Transitors, and a T3).

FTweaks.label: Cheaper High-Tier Belts
FTweaks.description: BobMods integration; Makes the blue, green, and purple belts use fewer gears and bearings (just count, not type) to avoid each unit of belt costing hundreds of units of material. Additionally, if logistic science packs exist (which contain a blue belt in their recipe), this option prevents technologies using it from being extraordinarily expensive to research.

FTweaks.label: Enable Coal Decomposition
FTweaks.description: This controls a recipe to break down coal into its chemical constituents - carbon, sulfur, and hydrogen. Only works when those items/fluids exist.

FTweaks.label: Add pipe to green science
FTweaks.description: Whether to add one unit of iron pipe to the green (logistic) science pack recipe. This was an idea raised in FFF #275 and never actually implemented.

FTweaks.label: Replace water with steam in advanced oil recipes
Make fluid resource patches eventually deplete and disappear
Counteract expensive-tech for upgrade techs
FTweaks.description: Whether to apply the "tech demultiply" behavior to "pure upgrade" technologies like bullet damage, train braking force, and lab speed

FTweaks.label: Make Construction Drones invincible
FTweaks.description: Useful given their tendency to run off into biter swarms.

FTweaks.label: Improved Artillery Strength
FTweaks.description: Whether to make artillery stronger, to compensate for things like wider pollution spread, stronger nests, or more aggressive biter expansion. Increases both range and damage per shot.

AutomaticTrainDeployment.label: Auto/manual for created trains
AutomaticTrainDeployment.description: Which state should trains be created in? Or use circuit signal A on the output stop to decide.

AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.label: Auto/manual for created trains
AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.description: Which state should trains be created in? Or use circuit signal A on the output stop to decide.

AutomaticTrainDeployment.label: Use S to control starting speed
AutomaticTrainDeployment.description: Whether or not to use circuit signal S to set starting speed of created trains.

AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.label: Use S to control starting speed
AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.description: Whether or not to use circuit signal S to set starting speed of created trains.

AutomaticTrainDeployment.label: Delete on approach
AutomaticTrainDeployment.description: Deletes the train on ARRIVE_STATION instead of WAIT_STATION.

AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.label: Delete on approach
AutomaticTrainDeployment_Updated.description: Deletes the train on ARRIVE_STATION instead of WAIT_STATION.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Entity to deploy
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: The actual entity that gets created.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Item to consume
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: The item that gets removed from the inventory.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Entity deploy per capsule
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: How many entities are spawned from 1 capsule.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Maximum accepted wastage
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: Example: if the target is 6 entities, and 1 capsule spawns 5, that would be a wastage of 4 entities. The second capsule is only deployed if the wastage is not above the max accepted wastage.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Minimum capsules remaining
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: How many capsules should always remain in the player's inventory. Autodeploy stops if this amount (or lower) is reached.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Maximum capsules per pass
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: How many capsules 1 launcher may throw per pass. Stacks with multiple launchers in the power armor. The default of 100 is oriented at 'unlimited', lower this for a more realistic experience.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Aggression factor
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: Configure the deploy aggression based on the player's playstyle. The default of 1.0 is oriented at bot-only warfare. Lower this value if bots are used as secondary warfare; as support to for example the flamethrower. Numbers higher than 1 can be used, however this is not advised as it will waste capsules.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Debug print
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: Prints ingame debug information for the player.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Debug log
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: Writes enemy information to a log file.

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Enemy visibility range
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: At what distance do enemies get triggered by the player and attack. This directly affects the scan distance and thus performance!

Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.label: Maximum vehicle speed for dispatch
Auto_Deploy_Destroyers.description: How fast can a player in a vehicle go until automatic deployment stops? Default of 0.9 is around 200 km/h.

Todo-List.label: Show "Todo List" button.
Todo-List.description: If enabled will always show a "Todo List" button in the top left.\nIf disabled the todo list can only be accessed by its hotkey (default shift-t).

Todo-List.label: Show debug log messages in the chat window.
Todo-List.description: If enabled the mod will print debug messages to the chat window.\nAttention: there are a lot of them :)

Todo-List.label: Todo list window height
Todo-List.description: The height of the todo list window. Default is 600.

Todo-List.label: Auto-assign tasks
Todo-List.description: If there is only one player in the game, auto-assign the task to this player.

Todo-List.label: Edit task on middle click
Todo-List.description: If enabled the middle click will open the edit popup. Default on right click.

Todo-List.label: Text style
Todo-List.description: Text style for the todo list. Questlog changes the wording to a questlog.

Unlimited-Resources.description: The amount to set resources to

Nautilus-Infinite-Ores.label: Resource amount
Nautilus-Infinite-Ores.description: The amount to set resources to

CJsInfiniteOres.label: Resource amount
CJsInfiniteOres.description: The amount to set resources to

Unlimited-Resources.description: Warning! Unchecking this will cause lag spikes that can desync multiplayer

Nautilus-Infinite-Ores.label: Disable interval refill
Nautilus-Infinite-Ores.description: Warning! Unchecking this will cause lag spikes that can desync multiplayer

CJsInfiniteOres.label: Disable interval refill
CJsInfiniteOres.description: Warning! Unchecking this will cause lag spikes that can desync multiplayer

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Round numbers
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Round randomized numbers above a certain threshold so that it looks nicer. Affects everything: recipes and item properties like belt speed, energy consumption, etc. Always rounds inventory sizes to 5. Default enabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize recipes
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize all recipes, except for a few defined on the blacklist like iron and copper plate smelting, and rocket parts. Alternatively, randomize only a select few recipes on the whitelist in the config.lua file. Or disable randomization of recipes altogether.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize iron and copper plates (Blacklist)
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize Iron and Copper Plates. Disabling will override the "Randomize Everything" setting by using the blacklist. Default disabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize kovarex enrichtment process (Blacklist)
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize kovarex enrichment process. Disabling will override the "Randomize Everything" setting by using the blacklist. Default disabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Mod: Whistlestop Factories: sync bulk recipes
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Bulk recipes from the WhistleStop Factories mod will have the same ratios as the regular recipes (ignoring rounding). Will override the "Randomize Everything" setting. Default enabled.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomization of properties
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: "Randomize Everything" will randomize all available properties of items and entities like insert speed, belt speed, etc. The full experience for hardcore players. "Randomize recommended properties" will only randomize some properties, and ignore some that very easily break the game (like modules, or locomotives). "Do not randomize properties" will not randomize any entity or item properties, only the crafting recipes if randomization of recipes is set. "Custom" lets you individually pick and choose from the settings below. Any other option besides "Custom" will overwrite the individual settings (inserter speed and all below).

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize belt and pipe underground lengths
Randomize ammunition
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize the damage of ammunition and potential effects

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize number of module slots
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize the number of module slots of all entities that take modules: mining drills, assembly machines, labs, rocket silo, etc.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize personal equipment
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize personal equipment like armor resistances, armor grid sizes, personal roboports, shields, etc. Not recommended.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize locomotives
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize locomotive stats like max power, top speed, air resistance, breaking force, etc. Not recommended.

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize beacons
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize beacon efficiency and area

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize power poles
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize power pole coverage area and wire reach

zKenirasRandomRecipes.label: Randomize rocket parts needed
zKenirasRandomRecipes.description: Randomize how many rocket parts are needed per rocket

long-mine-research.label: Enable T5 long mine technology
long-mine-research.description: Whether the Tier 5 long mine technology will be enabled.\nIt depends on T5 long reach technology.\nDo not change this for an existing game!

long-reach-research.label: Enable T5 long mine technology
long-reach-research.description: Whether the Tier 5 long mine technology will be enabled.\nIt depends on long mine technology and T5 long reach technology.\nDo not change this for an existing game!

long-reach-research-upgrade.label: Enable T5 long mine technology
long-reach-research-upgrade.description: Whether the Tier 5 long mine technology will be enabled.\nIt depends on long mine technology and T5 long reach technology.\nDo not change this for an existing game!

long-reach-research-upgrade-017.label: Enable T5 long mine technology
long-reach-research-upgrade-017.description: Whether the Tier 5 long mine technology will be enabled.\nIt depends on long mine technology and T5 long reach technology.\nDo not change this for an existing game!

long-reach-research-upgrade-017-f.label: Enable T5 long mine technology
long-reach-research-upgrade-017-f.description: Whether the Tier 5 long mine technology will be enabled.\nIt depends on long mine technology and T5 long reach technology.\nDo not change this for an existing game!

omnimatter_compression.label: Time overload setting.
omnimatter_compression.description: When a technology takes longer than the time in the dialogue box, it will be ignored until you increase your research capacity.

omnimatter_compression.label: Compensate stack sizes.
omnimatter_compression.description: Changes the base compression maths to prevent odd rounding in fluid based items such as barrels. /n if your recipes are too expensive, try changing this setting.

omnimatter_compression.label: Minimal compression tech cost.
omnimatter_compression.description: Add a compression tech for costs above this regardless of other settings. (default is 2000, to align with vanilla space-science)

omnimatter_compression.label: Always compress science packs.
omnimatter_compression.description: Put the names of the science packs that you always want to compress in the dialogue box.

omnimatter_compression.label: 1x1 tile sized compressors.
omnimatter_compression.description: Resizes the autocompressor, concentrator and condensator to 1x1 tiles from 3x3.\n[color=red]Changing this setting on an existing save may break your production lines![/color]

omnimatter_compression.label: Compressed building energy usage multiplier.
omnimatter_compression.description: Compressed buildings will use energy*multiplier*compression rate instead of energy*compression rate

omnimatter_compression.label: Compressed building material cost multiplier.
omnimatter_compression.description: Compressed buildings will take compression rate * cost multiplier to build.\ni.e. At a compression rate of 2 and a cost multiplier of 2, a compact solar panel worth 2 regular panels will take 4 panels to build.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Tree stump fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks a tree stump will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 54000 (15 minutes).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Biter corpse fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks biter corpses (including spitters and spawners) will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 54000 (15 minutes).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Building remnant fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks the building remnants will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 162000 (45 minutes).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Rail remnant fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks the rail remnants will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 54000 (15 minutes).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Character corpse fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks your character corpse (with all your items) will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 54000 (15 minutes).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.label: Character footprint fading time
Noxys_QuickerStumpFade.description: This value indicates how long in ticks your character footprints will stay before fading away. Vanilla default is 600 (10 seconds).\n\nSet to 0 to disable this feature.

pallets.label: Items per pallet
pallets.description: Number of items that can be loaded onto a pallet.

pallets.label: Limit pallets to a single stack
pallets.description: Limit pallets to hold a single stack of items. When enabled, the minimum of the stack size and number of items per pallet is used.

NapusJaggedOres.label: Starting Radius
NapusJaggedOres.description: The radius of which there's no ores.

NapusJaggedOres.label: Ore Scaling
NapusJaggedOres.description: The pace at which the ores increase. This value is multiplied onto the ores.

NapusJaggedOres.label: Stone Weight
NapusJaggedOres.description: This decides how much stone should spawn compared to the other ores values.

NapusJaggedOres.label: Coal Weight
NapusJaggedOres.description: This decides how much coal should spawn compared to the other ores values.

NapusJaggedOres.label: Iron Weight
NapusJaggedOres.description: This decides how much iron should spawn compared to the other ores values.

EndgameCombat.label: Strengthen green biters
EndgameCombat.description: If enabled, makes the green behemoth biters have 5x more health, and adds some laser resistance. Designed to make the lightning turret more desirable against them.

EndgameCombat.label: Strengthen green worms
EndgameCombat.description: If enabled, makes the green behemoth worms have much more health (comparable to vanilla behemoth biters). Designed to make the superpowerful nest-clearing weaponry (eg neutron bomb) more desirable against them.

EndgameCombat.label: Turret ammo warning threshold
EndgameCombat.description: When a turret with ammo has less than this many rounds left (each magazine item is worth 10 rounds), it will raise a "low ammo" alarm. One third that amount will raise a "critical ammo" alarm. Note that it takes 3-4 basic rounds to kill one small biter. Note: For ammo worth a lot more than 10 rounds, the warnings will likely trigger based on stack size instead: Three or fewer will trigger a low-ammo alarm, and one will trigger a critical alarm.

EndgameCombat.label: Repeat turret monitoring alarms
EndgameCombat.description: Whether the alarms should be repeated as long as the triggering condition remains true, as opposed to playing once when it becomes true then falling silent.

EndgameCombat.label: Dynamic turret alarms
EndgameCombat.description: Whether to base "low ammo" alarms on the total dealable damage by a turret, compared against the evolution factor, instead of just ammo amount - marginally more expensive to calculate, but this only matters in bases with thousands and thousands of turrets. This overrides the threshold option.

EndgameCombat.label: Napalm Shells ignite trees
EndgameCombat.description: With this enabled, trees in the range of a napalm shell will catch fire. Disable this if you want to be able to use them without causing forest fires.

EndgameCombat.label: Shockwave turrets require advanced circuits
EndgameCombat.description: Whether shockwave turrets should require advanced circuits (and thus plastic, and thus oil processing) to make. Not as meaningful with BobMods installed due to the recipe changes to electronics.

EndgameCombat.label: Artillery AoE range

EndgameCombat.label: Required satellite launches for Orbital Bombardment

Keep in mind that there is always at least one additional launch for the destroyer satellite(s) itself. Note that if the nuclear shells space science option is enabled, this value is doubled.

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Preparation time

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Additional equipment recipes
Wave_Defense_Unlimited.description: Adds smaller versions of common equipment items\n(Recommended if you play without start-items)

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Satellite round every x rounds

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Super armor

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Bounty multiplier

Wave_Defense_Unlimited.label: Early game accelerator

deadlock-beltboxes-loaders.label: Show alt-mode icons on beltboxes

ja-mod.description: The planet's lower temperature extremes. Decrease to add more frozen snow and ice. Increase to make frozen areas less common or impossible. Default is -50.

alien-biomes.label: Temperature Range: High
alien-biomes.description: The planet's higher temperature extremes. Increase to add more volcanic areas. Decrease to make volcanic areas less common or impossible. Default is 150.

ja-mod.label: Temperature Range: High
ja-mod.description: The planet's higher temperature extremes. Increase to add more volcanic areas. Decrease to make volcanic areas less common or impossible. Default is 150.

ja-mod.label: Humidity Range: Low
ja-mod.description: The planet's lower humidity extremes. Decrease to add more desert. Increase to make desert areas less common or impossible. Default is 0.

alien-biomes.label: Humidity Range: High

alien-biomes.label: Remove All Vegetation
alien-biomes.description: If enabled, all grassy terrain, trees, and plant-based decoratives will be removed (unless added by a different mod). This allows you to simulate a dead planet, moon, or asteroid.

ja-mod.label: Remove All Vegetation
ja-mod.description: If enabled, all grassy terrain, trees, and plant-based decoratives will be removed (unless added by a different mod). This allows you to simulate a dead planet, moon, or asteroid.

alien-biomes.label: Remove Obsolete Tiles
alien-biomes.description: Alien Biomes replaces a lot of the vanilla tiles. The obsolete tiles can be removed to free up additional tile slots so more mods that add tiles can be used (there is a limit of 255 tiles). Doing so might cause problems with other mods that require those vanilla tiles.

ja-mod.label: Remove Obsolete Tiles
ja-mod.description: Alien Biomes replaces a lot of the vanilla tiles. The obsolete tiles can be removed to free up additional tile slots so more mods that add tiles can be used (there is a limit of 255 tiles). Doing so might cause problems with other mods that require those vanilla tiles.

alien-biomes.label: Tile Speed Reduction %
alien-biomes.description: Some tiles (like hot volcanic terrain) reduce player speed. Reducing this number means the terrain will slow you less.

biter-spire.label: Minimum base size
biter-spire.description:
The minimum amount of biter spawners needed in a base for a biter spire to spawn.

Note: The mod checks a 3x3 chunk area for biter spawners. The higher this value is, the rarer biter spires will be.

Minimum: 1 / Maximum: 1000 / Default: 10

biter-spire.label: Power generation (W)
biter-spire.description: The base value for power generated by the biter spires in Watts (W). This value scales with the distance from spawn if "Scale with distance" is set to "true".\n\nMinimum: 1W / Maximum: 1PW / Default: 10MW

biter-spire.label: Scale with distance
biter-spire.description: Determines whether the base value for power generation is scaling with the distance to spawn (0,0). \n\nDefault: true

biter-spire.label: Distance scale factor
biter-spire.description:
The factor that is multiplied with the distance and the base value. The formula is power_generated = base_value * (1 + distance_scale_factor * distance). The distance is calculated using the max-norm.

Note: By default the biter spire will output twice the base power at 1000 tiles, three times the base power at 2000 tiles, and so on. (Linear Scaling)

Minimum: 0 / Maximum: 100 / Default: 0.001

Reactor Interface.label: Update interval
Reactor Interface.description: Tick delay between reactor interface updates

vanilla-loaders-hd.label: Recipe overhaul
vanilla-loaders-hd.description: Overhaul loader recipes with a complete rewrite. When Bob's Logistics "Transport belt overhaul" is enabled, recipes will align with Bob's mods. Turn off to use vanilla recipes. See mod page for more details.\n\n[color=#9cdcfe]Default:[/color] [color=green]Enabled[/color]

vanilla-loaders-hd.label: Recipes include inserters
vanilla-loaders-hd.description: Include inserters in loader recipes. Requires "Recipe overhaul" and Bob's Logistics "Transport belt overhaul" to be enabled.\n\n[color=#9cdcfe]Default:[/color] [color=green]Enabled[/color]

vanilla-loaders-hd.label: Loader Redux: Reskin only
vanilla-loaders-hd.description: Vanilla Loaders will do nothing but reskin Loader Redux. No recipe changes will be made, nor a basic loader added.\n\n[color=#9cdcfe]Default:[/color] [color=red]Disabled[/color]

kry-inserters.label: Simple long handed upgrade
kry-inserters.description: Long inserters are crafted only from base inserter, and drop the base inserter when mined, allowing for simple upgrade/removal

kry-inserters.label: Burner inserter fuel leech
kry-inserters.description: Enables the fuel leech setting for all types of burner inserters.

WireShortcuts.label: Keep wires in recipes (NOT RECOMMENDED)
WireShortcuts.description: If enabled, colored wires in the rare modded recipes are not removed but replaced by identical surrogates. Not recommended, can potentially cause trouble, but if you must.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Exponentially expensive modules
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Modules of each level now cost 2 modules of the previous level to craft (5 for God modules), making modules exponentially expensive in their level.  The intent is to encourage use of the lower level modules, which are otherwise rarely relevant.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Nerfed modules
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: The positive effects of the various modules are weakened, and their negative side-effects significantly increased.  In particular, speed (and raw speed) modules no longer make machines more efficient, and productivity (and raw productivity) modules come with severe energy and speed costs.  God modules (if enabled) become what raw productivity modules used to be.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Expensive combined modules
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: The combined-effect modules require different ingredients, including higher-tier plates.  If Bob's alien alloys are enabled, they will be required.  God modules (if enabled) are now crafted from other modules.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Nerfed beacons
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Mk2 and mk3 beacons have reduced range and increaed energy cost and hold fewer modules.  They also now generate pollution.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Expensive beacons
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Mk2 and mk3 beacons require pollution producing modules to craft.  With exponentially expensive modules enabled, this makes them very expensive, meaning that mk1 or mk2 beacons are a sensible choice in many situations.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Require modules for rocket control units
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Use either raw speed module 8s (if enabled) or speed module 8s as an ingredient in rocket control units.  If exponential modules are enabled then one module suffices for 20 rocket control units, so that they are not too expensive.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Require space science packs to craft god modules
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Add space science packs as an ingredient for crafting god module 1.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Research cost multiplier for god modules
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: With the other changes god module research becomes cheaper than its prerequisites.  This multiplier (at the default value of 10) sets more reasonable research costs.

CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.label: Require god modules for some Space X components
CoppermineBobModuleRebalancing.description: Those components which previously required all three module types now require god modules instead.  Has no effect if god modules are disabled.  If exponentially expensive modules are enabled then the number of god modules is scaled down to keep the requirements reasonable.

railloader.label: Allowed items
railloader.description: Types of items handled by bulk rail loaders and unloaders.\n\nThis setting is checked when a train arrives at a station.

railloader.label: Show configuration messages
railloader.description: Whether flying text should be shown over loaders and unloaders when handled item types change.

floating-damage-text.label: Damage text string format
floating-damage-text.description: Formatting for the text displayed when an entity is damaged.\nThis uses the same formatting as C's printf function.  The first argument is the damage dealt; the second argument is the damage type.  It is recommended to use %s for both specifiers.  See the FAQ on the mod portal page for more information.  Can be set empty to not display anything.\nDefault: %s

floating-damage-text.label: Decimal digit rounding
floating-damage-text.description: Number of digits after the decimal point to round to.  Negative numbers round to powers of 10.\n[-6 : 2 : 6]

floating-damage-text.label: Damage against allies color
floating-damage-text.description: Color text of damaged allies (players, cars, and tanks)\nFormat is r,g,b where r, g, and b are each a number between 0 and 255.\nDefault: 255,127,0

floating-damage-text.label: Damage against enemies color
floating-damage-text.description: Color text of damaged enemies (biters, spawners, and worms)\nFormat is r,g,b where r, g, and b are each a number between 0 and 255.\nDefault: 200,0,0

floating-damage-text.label: Damage against neutrals color
floating-damage-text.description: Color text of damaged neutral entities (neither ally nor enemy)\nFormat is r,g,b where r, g, and b are each a number between 0 and 255.\nDefault: 200,200,200

none - no notifications

only_helper - help notifications (but not transfer notifications)

BlueprintExtensions.label: Snap to edge centers blueprint first
BlueprintExtensions.description:
ON: Snapping to an edge centers the blueprint on the opposite axis.
OFF: Snapping to an edge does not move the blueprint on the opposite axis.

Setting this to OFF means that snapping to North + snapping to East is the same effect as snapping to Northeast, useful if you have limited keybind space (e.g. no numpad).

SubtleMapTileColors.description:

BlueprintExtensions.label: Increment version when updating blueprints (normal)
BlueprintExtensions.description:
Blueprint Extensions can add a version number to blueprints it updates.

OFF: Blueprint labels are always copied as-is.

IF PRESENT: A blueprint label ending in "v.###" or "v###" will have the version number incremented.

ALWAYS: Like IF PRESENT, but "v.2" will be added to blueprint labels if no version number is present.

This setting only applies when using regular mouse drag to select the new blueprint area.

BlueprintExtensions.label: Show buttons for in-place blueprint rotation
Action upon landfilling a blueprint
BlueprintExtensions.description:
UPDATE IN-PLACE: Adds landfill to the current blueprint.  The resulting changes cannot be undone.

MAKE A COPY: Creates an identical copy of the current blueprint with landfill added.  Changes can be undone by switching to the original blueprint.

MAKE A TEMPORARY COPY: The copy is deleted when cleared from the cursor.  Temporary copies can be made permanent by manually dropping them in an inventory or the blueprint library.

Better-Power-Armor-Grid.label: Armor & Equipment division
Better-Power-Armor-Grid.description: This setting enables the division between "aggro" (combat) and "engineering" (industrial) equipment. If active, you won't be capable of putting specific types of equipment in the vanilla power armors (Roboports, exoskeletons, etc.). They'll be, indeed, compatible only with the industrial armors. (The same concept, but reversed, applies for the highest tiers of lasers and shields.) This feature is made to simplify playthroughs with non-optimized mods.

fpp.label: Less module slots
fpp.description: Less module slots in higher upgrades. Especially in higher tiers, many automation machines and miners have a lot of module slots in an imbalanced way. Check this box to keep it more "normal".

fpp.label: Maximum upgrade tier
fpp.description: The maximum possible upgrade tier (1 to 14). 6 or 13 is not recommended.

fpp.label: Upgrade tier colorization

fpp.label: Upgrade tier icon set
fpp.description: Select the set of icons for upgraded devices. Roman == roman numbers. Standard == Color-layed icons. None == All icons are the same.

fpp.label: Variety of mixed ores
fpp.description: Choice for variety of mixed ores. Either for keeping it simple with less different mixed ores or keep the game hard with many different mixed ores. Insane++ will additionally remove all vanilla ressources.

fpp.label: Variety of colors
fpp.description: Choice for variety of colors possible.

fpp.label: Productivity modules
fpp.description: Settings for the possibility of productivity modules. This is only related to FPP-recipes and won´t touch vanilla recipes in any way.

fpp.label: Additional logistics
fpp.description: Additional logistic entities for more variation, like more different chests or more belts.

fpp.label: Difficult start
fpp.description: Check this box for additional research required on start. This stretches the early phase of game.

fpp.label: Aliens
fpp.description: Make the fights with aliens in later game more interesting. Be careful; the option "legion" could be frustrating at later game stage.

fpp.label: Upgrade stone synthetics
fpp.description: Players are not forced anymore to search for blackstones and essencestones on surface, they are both syntheticable (Upgrade tiers 6 and 8).

PavementDriveAssist.label: Scan rate [ticks]
PavementDriveAssist.description:
This parameter determines the amount of ticks for one driving assistant scan (i.e. if set to "2" there are 30 scans per second).

Set this value to 1 if you want maximum precision (causing additional load).
Set this to "3" or greater to reduce the load on your CPU, at the cost of decreased precision. 
Please keep in mind, that setting this to very high values will make the driving assistant increasingly sluggish and finally useless at higher speeds!

PavementDriveAssist.label: Tile score ranking
PavementDriveAssist.description: Use this parameter to customize your road tile priority. On default, asphalt tiles will be prioritized over concrete ones and those again over stone path tiles. The driving assistant will try to steer your vehicle onto the tile with highest score (i.e. if you use stone as your road tile within an concreted base, set "Stone > Concrete". \nAsphalt values will be only considered if mods providing such tiles are present.

PavementDriveAssist.label: Score for asphalt pavement
PavementDriveAssist.description: This variable determines how much the drive assistant will try to keep the vehicle on the given floor type. If multiple different floor types are present at once, then the floor type with the highest score will be interpreted as a "street". If, for example, you want to drive on stone roads in an otherwise concreted factory, you need to set the score value of stone path higher than that of concrete pavement.

Rampant.description: Requires Rampant new enemies to have any affect. This number represents the number of times a regional faction group can mutate into other factions. Regional faction groups adapt over time typically to a faction that is strong against the type of damage they are being killed with. Death threshold for mutation is based on evolution. (4500 Deaths:<50% Evolution, 7500:<70%, 11000:<90%, 16000)

Rampant.label: AI: Faction Base Distance Modifier
Rampant.description: Modifies the distance between factions as a percentage change. Low percentages may impact performance.

Rampant.label: AI: Print Faction Mutations
Rampant.description: Display a message to the chat console when a faction mutates based on the number of enemies killed

Rampant.label: AI: Adaption Modifier
Rampant.description: Modifies the number of units or enemy buildings that must be destroyed before the adaptation happens based on the damage types that killed the units or buildings. This modifier is a percentage change using the following as starting place (Default deaths events starts at 4500 under 0.5 evo, under 0.7 is 7500, under 0.9 is 11000, and +0.9 is 16000)

Rampant.label: World: Units affected by tiles
Rampant.description: Units are affected by tile movement modifiers

Rampant.label: Map: Revert Enemy Map Color
Rampant.description: Reverts the enemy map color to the vanilla enemy map color

Rampant.label: World: Unit Nest breath air
Rampant.description: Now unit spawners breath air so they are affected by things like poison capsules

Rampant.label: Projectiles: Use blockable projectiles
Rampant.description: Use the projectile attacks that are blockable. This should be checked if you are using the new enemies.

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Starting chunk attack threshold
Rampant.description: The total score that a chunk must reach in order for an attack wave to spawn. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves. Scaling linearly with evolution factor (starting threshold @ 0.0 evolution)

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Ending chunk attack threshold
Rampant.description: The total score that a chunk must reach in order for an attack wave to spawn. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves. Scaling linearly with evolution factor (ending threshold @ 100.0 evolution)

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Max biter group size that can be directly formed
Rampant.description: If you wish to change how the attack wave scales with evolution you will need to modify the config.lua in the zip file.

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Max number of attack groups that can be active at once
Rampant.description: More squads requires more UPS.

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Max number of building groups that can be active at once
Rampant.description: More builders requires more UPS.

Rampant.label: Safety: Enable building safety.
Rampant.description: This needs to be toggle for the safe building toggles to work. This will cause entities made safe to regenerate with the destructible flag set to false, which causes them to never be targeted or damaged again.

Rampant.label: Safety: Make curved rails safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make curved rails safe from biters

Rampant.label: Safety: Make straight rails safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make straight rails safe from biters

Rampant.label: Safety: Make big electric poles safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make big electric poles safe from biters

Rampant.label: Safety: Make rail chain signals safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make rail chain signals safe from biters

Rampant.label: Safety: Make rail signals safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make rail signals safe from biters

Rampant.label: Safety: Make train stops safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make train stops safe from biters

Rampant.label: AI: Nocturnal Mode
Rampant.description: Toggling this will cause Rampant attack waves to spawn at night. Works better with the clockwork mod or a mod that extends night.

Rampant.label: AI: Difficulty Scaling
Rampant.description: Between 0.0 and 100.0. This scales how many action points the ai gets per logic cycle to perform actions like making attack waves. 0.3 - very easy, 0.75 - easy, 1.0 - medium, 1.25+ - hard

Rampant.label: AI: Print Point Spending to Chat
Rampant.description: Print a message to chat whenever Rampant spends points. Includes GPS coordinates. Keep disabled for the hardest Rampant experience. Heads up: can fill up chat quickly during busy battles!

Rampant.label: AI: Print Point Gains to Chat
Rampant.description: Print a message to chat whenever Rampant gains points. Does not show passive point generation. Keep disabled for the hardest Rampant experience. Heads up: can fill up chat quickly during busy battles!

Rampant.label: Safety; Increase wall resistance to spitters
Rampant.description: Toggling this will cause a %60 acid resistance to be added to all wall entities to reduce the damage done by spitters to walls.

Rampant.label: Safety: Make lamps safe from biters
Rampant.description: Make lamps safe from biters

Rampant.label: Optimization: Remove blood particles (Reduces lag spikes)
Rampant.description: The blood particles that are created when biters are being killed can cause UPS spikes, this removes them.

Rampant.label: Notification: Enable attack wave warnings
Rampant.description: Shows a message warning players that an attack wave is incoming

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Enable the swarm
Rampant.description: This reduces the size of the unit collision_mask causing them to reduce pathing collisions and smooth out the attacks

Rampant.label: World: Enable new enemies
Rampant.description: Adds news enemies that will be dispersed over the world. This increases the RAM requirements. With 1 variation for each biter, worm, and nest and 5 tiers expect upto a 2GB RAM increase. With 20 variations and 10 tiers set expect up to 9GB RAM increase. Variations add randominess to each tier of biter, worms, or nests. Tiers are the power level of the biters.

Rampant.label: World: Enemy Random Seed
Rampant.description: The seed that powers all of the unit generation, so change this if you want the enemy stats to change

Rampant.label: World: Enemy deadzone frequency
Rampant.description: The percentage of zones that start without worms or nests

Rampant.label: World: Enemy Variations
Rampant.description: This number corresponds to the number of variations per tier. This adds randominess to each tier power level. Min 1, Max 20

Rampant.label: World: Enable Bobs as a faction
World: Enable NE as a faction
Safety: Disallow Friendly Fire Splash Damage
Rampant.description: Prevents enemy spitters and worms from damaging units or buildings from the same force through splash damage

Rampant.label: World: Beginning enemy level
Rampant.description: This is the starting level of the enemy that will be used when generating the set of enemies for the specified number of tiers and increases linearly to the end tier for as many tiers selected. Roughly healthwise each tier is a follows (1-15,2-75,3-150,4-250,5-1000,6-2000,7-3500,8-7500,9-15000,10-30000). min 1, max 10

Rampant.label: World: Ending enemy level
Rampant.description: This is the ending tier level that is reached after increasing linearly from the start tier for as many tiers selected. Roughly healthwise each tier is as follows (1-15,2-75,3-150,4-250,5-1000,6-2000,7-3500,8-7500,9-15000,10-30000). min 1, max 10

Rampant.label: AI: Enable Migration
Rampant.description: This will allow the ai to expand its worms and nests. Respects the map settings for biter expansion.

Rampant.label: AI: Enable Peaceful
Rampant.description: The Rampant AI can roll the peaceful state. If this is disabled and the biters roll the peaceful state, they are instead changed to aggressive or migrating state depending on AI: Enabled Migration setting. This does not relate to whether your map has Factorio's Peaceful Mode enabled or disabled. Disable for the hardest Rampant experience.

Rampant.label: AI: Print State Changes to Chat
Rampant.description: Gives you information in the game chat about Rampant's AI state. Messages are displayed for each surface. Disable for the hardest Rampant experience.

Rampant.label: DEBUG: Print Temperament Changes to Chat
Rampant.description: Prints to chat AI temperament information that controls AI state rolls. This is used for debugging.

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Use Player Proximity as attack trigger
Rampant.description: Include player pheromones amount for threshold on chunks with biter nests that will generate a Rampant attack wave. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Player score contribution threshold
Rampant.description: The score that a chunk must reach for it to contribute to the attack threshold. Increasing reduces player pheromone cloud impact.

Rampant.label: World: Unkillable logistic bots
Rampant.description: This will make logistic bots immune to all damage

Rampant.label: World: Unkillable construction bots
Rampant.description: This will make construction bots immune to all damage

Rampant.label: Attack Wave: Shrink Nests and Worms
Rampant.description: Reduce the collision box size of nests and worms by 50%. May cause overlapping entities due to the collision box being smaller than the entity graphic.

Rampant.label: AI: Enable Raiding AI
Rampant.description: Toggles the ai raiding parties from outside your pollution cloud

Rampant.label: AI: Enable Siege AI
Rampant.description: Toggles the ai siege parties from outside your pollution cloud that attack or nest

Rampant.label: World: Laser Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Laser Biter Faction, Laser is major resistance, electric is a minor resistance. Has Biters and Spitter unit types.

Rampant.label: World: Wasp Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Wasp Biter Faction, Spitter only units and each spitter spits small drones.

Rampant.label: World: Spawner Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Spawner Biter Faction, Only Spitters produced by spawners and spitters make eggs that hatch into biters.

Rampant.label: World: Regenerative Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Regenerative Biter Faction, High health regeneration, major weakness to fire, minor resistance to physical, minor resistance to explosive.

Rampant.label: World: Fast Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Fast Biter Faction, High rate of movement, minor resistance to explosive.

Rampant.label: World: Inferno Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Inferno Biter Faction, Only Spitters that spit flaming acid that burns everything. Major resistance to Acid & Fire, Minor weakness to poison.

Rampant.label: World: Nuclear Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Nuclear Biter Faction, Only Biters that explode like a atomic bomb. Major weakness to explosive.

Rampant.label: World: Electric Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Electric Biter Faction, Only Biters with a short range attack that hits multiple entities in a line. Major resistance to Electric, Minor resistance to Laser.

Rampant.label: World: Fire Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Fire Biter Faction, Major resistance to Acid & Fire.

Rampant.label: World: Suicide Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Suicide Biter Faction, Only Biters that explode when they attack. Minor resistance to Poison, Major weakness to explosive.

Rampant.label: World: Brutal Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Brutal Biter Faction, Only Biters. Major resistance to physical, Major resistance to explosive, Minor Weakness to Electric.

Rampant.label: World: Acidic Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Acid Biter Faction, Major resistance to Acid, Minor resistance to Poison.

Rampant.label: World: Sapper Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Sapper Biter Faction, Major resistance to Electric, Minor resistance to Laser. Destroying powered structures creates draining crystals.

Rampant.label: World: Poison Biter Faction
Rampant.description: Poison Biter Faction, Only Biters. On death creates a cloud that heals biters and hurts player objects. Major resistance to Poison, Minor weakness to Electric, Minor weakness to Explosive, Minor weakness to Laser, Minor resistance to Fire.

Rampant.label: Projectiles: Non biter force colliding projectiles
Rampant.description: Biter projectiles no longer collide with other biters, worms or nests. Everything else still collides with biter projectiles.

Rampant.label: Compatibility: Enable full map scanning
Rampant.description: This setting causes the game map to slowly be scanned for entities created or destroyed outside of the factorio event system. (If a mod isnt using script_raised_built or script_raised_destroyed this will cause Rampant to still eventually be consistent with the game map)

Rampant.label: Biter, Spitter, Worm, Nest, and Hive Corpse Fade Time
Rampant.description: The time in seconds for how long biter corpses stay around

Rampant.label: Enable corpse fade time
Rampant.description: Enable the fade time to reduce or increase biter, spitter, worm, spawner, and hive. If disabled, no alterations are made to corpse times.

Rampant.label: AI: Temperament Rate Modifier
Rampant.description: Change how quickly Rampant will hit extremes in the ai temperament stat which control attacking and expanding. This is a percentage increase or decrease with 1 being equal to 100%.

SatelliteRadar.label: Scaling
SatelliteRadar.description:
The default number of satellites required for each level increases by 1 for every chunk added to the always visible area of a radar. Scale the number of satellites required as desired.

Formula for each level:
# satellites=scaling*(4*level^2+8*level)
Level goes from 1 to 17

Minimum value: 0.1

Game will restart after value is changed.

LeveledEnemies.label: Difficulty
LeveledEnemies.description: Controls how powerful the high-level enemies become.

LeveledEnemies.label: Paced Evolution
LeveledEnemies.description: Check this to make the evolution cap between 0 and 1 scale with critical research progress.  (progress towards launching the rocket.)  The cap is removed after evolution 1.

LeveledEnemies.label: Leveling Start
LeveledEnemies.description: Select the evolution level for when enemies should start leveling up.

LeveledEnemies.label: Leveling End
LeveledEnemies.description: Select the evolution level when enemies should max out at level 10. Setting to greater than 1 will expand the evolution range.  (it gets scaled back to 0 to 1 in the game.  See readme if you're confused.)  Must be at least 1.

Flow Control.label: New subgroup for pipe items
Flow Control.description: Moves pipes, pumps and valves to a new line in the crafting menu.

Flow Control.label: Picked up pipes become base pipes
Flow Control.description: When picking up T-Junction, elbow or straight pipes, it reverts back to normal pipes.

factorimon.label: Debugging enabled
factorimon.description: Start with a heap of items and fast crafting to test out the features of the MOD.

Natural_Evolution_Enemies.label: Enable: Alien Expansion Group Size Dynamic
Natural_Evolution_Enemies.description: Enable: Manages Unit Group Size. Makes early game easier and late game harder. This will replace NE Expansion mod.

BasicKit.description: Start with a steam engine, boiler and offshore pump instead of a solar panel.

BasicKit.label: Add accumulator to inventory
BasicKit.description: The accumulator allows the player to run the assembly machine at night if using solar.

TinyStart.label: Main Power Option
TinyStart.description: Choose between:\n[font=default-bold]I)[/font] a low output (150kW), micro fusion reactor\n[font=default-bold]II)[/font] 4 solar panels (120kW).

TinyStart.label: Slot 2 Option

Choose between:
[font=default-bold]I)[/font] an additional micro fusion reactor
[font=default-bold]II)[/font] a low performance energy shield
[font=default-bold]III)[/font] 4 additional solar panels
[font=default-bold]IV)[/font] 2 extra batteries.

TinyStart.label: Mini-Slot Option
TinyStart.description:
Choose between:
[font=default-bold]I)[/font] an extra battery OR
[font=default-bold]II)[/font] 2 additional solar panels (60kW).

TinyStart.label: Roboport Type
TinyStart.description: Choose between basic (Mark I, 20 bots) or Mark II roboports (50 bots). Mark II roboports have very high energy demands; choosing additional power options in other slots is recommended.

Powered_Entities.label: Entity Exclusion List

a-better-start.label: Better Start Supplies
a-better-start.description:
Select your starting set.

Small: Speed up your pre-automation grind.
Steel Axes, more plates, gears, yellow belts, coal, drills, 
NO TECHNOLOGIES.

Starter: Skip the pre-automation grind
More of everything in the previous tier, eletric drills, stone furnaces, inserters, enough boilers and steam-engines with one offshore-pump.
INCLUDES TECHNOLOGIES: Automation, Electronics, Toolbelt, Logistics, Electric Energy Distribution

Medium: Includes robots
Everything in the previous tier, long inserters, construction robots, personal roboport, assembling machines, electricity, car, labs, pipes.
INCLUDES TECHNOLOGIES: Automation, Electronics, Toolbelt, Logistics, Electric Energy Distribution

Big: Everything in the previous tier, more well-equipped power armour, electric and advanced circuits, assembling machine 2, lots of belts, oil refining equipment, logistic network equipment.
INCLUDES TECHNOLIGIES: Automation, Steel-processing, Automation-2, Oil-processing, Plastics, Advanced-electronics, Sulfur-processing, Battery, Toolbelt, Electronics, Engine, Electric-engine, Flying, Robotics, Logistic-robotics, Construction-robotics, Logistic-system, Fluid-handling.

Will-o-the-Wisps_updated.label: Forest pollution factor
Will-o-the-Wisps_updated.description: Wisps appear in forested places at night according to the formula "1 + factor * relative-pollution", where relative-pollution is 0 for unpolluted areas and 1.0 for the most polluted areas.\nExample: Setting this factor to 5 will make wisps appear in most polluted areas 6x as likely ("1 + 5*1"), 0 will make chances equal, and a factor of -0.9 will have them spawn largely away from pollution ("1 - 0.9 * 1 = 0.1", so they are 10x less likely to spawn on the most polluted chunks than on non-polluted ones).

InlaidUVLamp.label: Forest pollution factor
InlaidUVLamp.description: Wisps appear in forested places at night according to the formula "1 + factor * relative-pollution", where relative-pollution is 0 for unpolluted areas and 1.0 for the most polluted areas.\nExample: Setting this factor to 5  make wisps appear in most polluted areas 6x as likely ("1 + 5*1"), 0  make chances equal, and a factor of -0.9  have them spawn largely away from pollution ("1 - 0.9 * 1 = 0.1", so they are 10x less likely to spawn on the most polluted tile(s) than on non-polluted ones).

Will-o-the-Wisps_updated.label: Wisp chance [purple]
Will-o-the-Wisps_updated.description:
Chance of spawning purple will-o'-wisps in random forests at night. Must be in 0-1.0 range.
Sum of the chances for all wisp types can be:
- Less than 1, in which case wisps spawn less in general
- Greater than 1 - values will be used as weights, i.e. p=y=r=1 is the same as p=y=r=0.33.

InserterFuelLeech.label: Minimum target fuel items
InserterFuelLeech.description: Inserters leech appropriate fuel items from pickup target's burner inventories until a drop target's burner inventory holds at least this amount of items.\nDefault is 5.

InserterFuelLeech.label: Maximum ticks between updates
InserterFuelLeech.description: Each tick, N / T inserters get updated where N is the count of placed inserters in the game and T is the value of this setting. If N < T, one inserter gets checked every tick. If increasing this, you might also want to increase "Maximum pickup distance variation".\nThe value is a tradeoff between impact on UPS for big amounts of inserters and reliability of detection of an inserter's hand hovering above its pickup target. Too high values lead to starved drop targets. Too low values will kill UPS if lots of inserters are managed.\nDefault is 90 (1.5 seconds at normal game speed with full UPS).

InserterFuelLeech.label: Maximum pickup distance variation
InserterFuelLeech.description: Maximum distance (measured in tiles) between the hand of an inserter and its pickup location to consider it hovering over its pickup target. Keep this small to prevent visible teleporting of items.\nSet this to 10.0 to get BurnerLeech's teleport-to-hand behaviour.\nDefault is 0.3.

InserterFuelLeech.label: Use trickle-fuel cheat

PickerBlueprinter.label: Increment version when updating blueprints (normal)
PickerBlueprinter.description:
Blueprint Extensions can add a version number to blueprints it updates.

OFF: Blueprint labels are always copied as-is.

AUTO: A blueprint label ending in "v.###" or "v###" will have the version number incremented.
\ON: Like IF PRESENT, but "v.2" will be added to blueprint labels if no version number is present.

This setting only applies when using regular mouse drag to select the new blueprint area.

PickerBlueprinter.label: Increment version when updating blueprints (alternate)
PickerBlueprinter.description:
Blueprint Extensions can add a version number to blueprints it updates.

OFF: Blueprint labels are always copied as-is.

AUTO: A blueprint label ending in "v.###" or "v###" will have the version number incremented.
\ON: Like IF PRESENT, but "v.2" will be added to blueprint labels if no version number is present.

This setting applies when using SHIFT + drag to select the new blueprint area.

PickerBlueprinter.label: Snap to edge centers blueprint first
PickerBlueprinter.description:
ON: Snapping to an edge centers the blueprint on the opposite axis.
OFF: Snapping to an edge does not move the blueprint on the opposite axis.

Setting this to OFF means that snapping to North + snapping to East is the same effect as snapping to Northeast, useful if you have limited keybind space (e.g. no numpad).

PickerBlueprinter.label: Invert horizontal axis when snapping
PickerBlueprinter.description: Snap to East/West moves that edge of the blueprint to under the cursor rather than aligning the blueprint to that edge.

PickerBlueprinter.label: Invert vertical axis when snapping
PickerBlueprinter.description: Snap to North/South moves that edge of the blueprint to under the cursor rather than aligning the blueprint to that edge.

ChokePoint.label: Terrain Seed Mixin
ChokePoint.description: This affects the seed used for the terrain program (and how it is combined with the map seed). Use this to get a new distribution with an existing map.

ChokePoint.label: Terrain Scale
ChokePoint.description: A simple multiplier for the raw scale of the overall pattern; larger values means the web of rivers is "scaled up" in size, with larger continents inside them.

ChokePoint.label: River Thickness
ChokePoint.description: A simple multiplier for how thick the dividing rivers should be. Only applies for some map generation algorithms.

ChokePoint.label: Allow Traversible Shores
ChokePoint.description: Whether to allow the generator to make the innermost shores "mud water", which is traversible to you (slowly) and to biters (normal speed). This looks better, and makes transport a bit easier, but means that walls cannot be 100% effective.

ChokePoint.label: Distance Falloff (% per 100 tiles)
ChokePoint.description: How much the effect of the river generation should fade with distance. At 100%, the rivers will be half-width at 50 tiles and not generate at all past 100 tiles. This makes the worldgen gradually faster to compute the further you go, without affecting chokepoints near spawn, which are the ones that really matter from a gameplay perspective.

space-exploration.description: If another mod adds a way to get space science, then that method will be used. If there is no way to make it, then Space Exploration can either remove it or use it as an Optimisation science pack.

space-exploration.label: Never show lifesupport GUI
space-exploration.description: If checked, the lifesupport GUI will never be shown, even if you are suffocating.

space-exploration.description: Uncheck to disable the zone preview window in the Universe Explorer. If you have some of Factorio's debug overlays active, the preview window can reduce FPS.

space-exploration.label: Construction pylon charging points
space-exploration.description: Uncheck to remove construction pylon charge points. This helps control bot charging behaviour, but you may need to add other charging options along long distance routes.

space-exploration.label: Coronal Mass Ejection max interval
space-exploration.description: The max interval for repeating Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs). The value is in hours, 0 = disabled. The first CME is scripted to the first minute of the game and is mostly harmless. The second is delayed by roughly 48 hours. The delay between repeats is between 50% and 100% of the max interval setting. A non-zero setting only applies to new events; once an ETA has been set, it won't be affected. A zero setting will clear all scheduled CMEs, though it may take up to a minute for the change to take effect.

space-exploration.label: Bonus starting resource patches
space-exploration.description: Adds some additional small resources patches to the starting area. The resource patches are in a cluster to reduce time running between resources.

space-exploration.label: Show overhead Nav-Sat Uplink button
space-exploration.description: Show a small button on the top left of the screen to toggle the Navigation Satellite Uplink.

space-exploration.label: Show overhead Universe Explorer button
space-exploration.description: Show a small button on the top left of the screen to toggle the Universe Explorer.

space-exploration.label: Scan search budget
space-exploration.description: Satellite scanning: The number of chunks that can be checked for chart status. High values let it speed through already scanned chunks to get to the uncharted edge.

space-exploration.label: Scan chart budget
space-exploration.description: Satellite scanning: The number of chunk requests that can be added to the charting buffer in parallel. New chart requests won't be made if the previous chunks have not finished.

space-exploration.label: Supercharger individual port charge rate (MW)
space-exploration.description: Sets the charging rate of each individual charging port in the supercharger, in MW (does not affect maximum charge rate). Minimum (default) value is 90 MW, enough to charge a vanilla robot in one tick, up to 1000 MW, or 1 GW, the maximum charge rate of the supercharger.

space-exploration.label: Plague max runtime
space-exploration.description: The max runtime for the bio weapon, in minutes. After a plague has been running for this amount of time all biological entities are destroyed. This may end up removing the enemy revenge attacks before they are finished. The setting is intended to save UPS, not to make the game easier.

space-exploration.label: Alert when satellite discovers nothing
space-exploration.description: When a satellite is launched you get an alert telling you what was discovered. This setting can disable the alert if nothing was discovered.

space-exploration.label: Show help tooltip on pin buttons
space-exploration.description: Show an expanded tooltip on the pin buttons that gives instructions on how to use them.

space-exploration.label: Scan alert interval
space-exploration.description: The interval in seconds between surface scan update alerts. Revealing surfaces increases game save file size so it is best not to leave one on and forget it.

space-exploration.label: Hide low-priority zones in dropdown menus
space-exploration.description: Hide low-priority zones in dropdown menus for destination selection. When on, only zones with priority greater than or equal to the value set in the "Priority threshold" setting will be shown. Zone priority can be modified in the Universe Explorer.

space-exploration.label: Priority threshold
space-exploration.description: Threshold value, below which a zone will not be shown in dropdown menus for destination selection. Does nothing if "Hide low-priority zones in dropdown menus" is off.

space-exploration.label: Snap blueprinted spaceship clamps
space-exploration.description: If a spaceship clamp is included in a blueprint, snap the blueprint to the rail grid to make sure that the clamp can be placed.

space-exploration.label: Scan max range
space-exploration.description: Satellite scanning: The maximum range (in tiles) that scanning is allowed to go from the surface origin before stopping. Planets will never be scanned beyond their radius and the maximum planet radius is 10000 tiles. Values larger than 10000 tiles will only apply to space zones.

Predefined ingredients will be more expensive in all the recipes. Has vanilla and mod support.
Set to 1 to ignore.

(Minimum=0.1; Maximum=10; Default=1)

customarathon.label: Add expensive circuits
customarathon.description: Includes circuits in the expensive ingredients. It will have a cascading effect with regular ingredients.

customarathon.label: Placeable items, machines and equipment cost multiplier
customarathon.description:
All entities and items with use will be affected. Expensive machines will make expansion more meaningful and overall increase the value of optimal builds.
Set to 1 to ignore.

(Minimum=0.1; Maximum=20; Default=2)

customarathon.label: Multiplier for tier scaling
customarathon.description:
Exponentially raises the cost of higher tier machines and equipment. A great way to scale the production up even for the mall. The multiplier is very sensitive as it uses exponential function.
Set to 1 to ignore.

(Minimum=0.5; Maximum=2; Default=1)

customarathon.label: Double the input for successive tiers
customarathon.description: Works for item types such as belts, inserters, modules, but not assemblers. Twice as many of that item type will be required for the next tier.

customarathon.label: Crafting time multiplier
customarathon.description:
Crafting time multiplier for machines and equipment.
Set to 1 to ignore.

(Minimum=0.1; Maximum=10; Default=1)

customarathon.description: Add ammos to the machine/equipment expensive list

customarathon.description: To counteract expensive machines, this option essentially offers new dummy items. The recipes will use the standard costs, making science unaffected by most of the previous settings.\nSafe warning: loading time can be significantly longer.

zero-infinity-chests.description: Sets the number of inventory slots in infinity chests. Default is 48.\nWARNING: Extremely large values can slow down the game when opening the chest inventory.

zero-infinity-chests.description: Infinity items will be searchable when setting filters or circuit conditions. This does NOT affect the availability of the items themselves.

zero-infinity-chests.label: Infinity Entities Resist All Damage
zero-infinity-chests.description: Adds resistances to all modded damage types to all infinity-type entities.

zero-infinity-chests.label: Infinity Chest Graphics
zero-infinity-chests.description: 0.16 infinity chests look like logistic chests with inverted colors.

zero-infinity-chests.label: Use Compilatron Chest Shadow
zero-infinity-chests.description: The compilatron chest is the same shape as an infinity chest but has a much cleaner shadow graphic. As of 0.17.1, the normal infinity chest shadow has excessive artifacts around the edges.

zero-infinity-chests.label: Quiet Infinity Pipe
zero-infinity-chests.description: Default pipes have a setting that increases the volume of their sound effects depending on the rate of flow. Infinity pipes can have ridiculous flow rates, so the sounds can get incredibly loud.

zero-infinity-chests.label: Infinity Pipe Volume
zero-infinity-chests.description: Sets the maximum volume of infinity pipes. Default is 100.

transparent-inventory.label: Enable opening inventories of other players.
transparent-inventory.description: This easily allows enabling or disabling the complete mod, without requiring the mod to be removed from the server. Default is enabled.

transparent-inventory.label: Each player can control if someone can access their inventory.
transparent-inventory.description: When this is enabled, players can decide theirselves if other players should be able to access their inventory. If this is disabled, the client-side setting has no effects and the admin is able to control this. Default is enabled, as well as on the client (each individual player).

transparent-inventory.label: Inventory owner is being informed when someone opens their inventory.
transparent-inventory.description: Usually when some player opens the inventory of any other player, the owner of the inventory is being informed via console message which player access his inventory. When disabled, this does not happen. Default is enabled.

transparent-inventory.label: Mode for provided user list:
transparent-inventory.description: The mode which players should have access to inventories of other players. When using "Only listed users" only listed users at "Defined users list" are allowed to open inventories. When using "All users, except listed ones" (default) all players are allowed to do so, except listed ones.

transparent-inventory.label: Defined users list: (separated by comma)
transparent-inventory.description: A defined list of players, separated by comma (,). Important to notice: Case-insensitive and use of wildcards is only possible when regex is disabled! Wildcard works using an asterisk (*), so for example super* also matches superman and supergirl. Default is empty.

transparent-inventory.label: Enable regex support for users list.
transparent-inventory.description: For advanced users it is possible to enable regex support for the user lists. Multiple regex strings possible. Important: When enabling regex, the values are case-sensitive and the wildcard using asterisk (for easier use) will be disabled. Wildcards in Lua are usually .*. Please also notice that Lua regex is quite different from other programming languages, therefore please see further information in the Lua documentation. Default is disabled.

transparent-inventory.label: Should have other players have access to your inventory?
transparent-inventory.description: When enabled, other players do have access to your inventory. It is important to note, that this option has lower priority than server-side settings and therefore can be bypassed by an admin setting on the server. On own servers with good friends it is generally recommended to keep this enabled.

Pollution_statistics.label: Graph refresh rate
Pollution_statistics.description: (Default 15, Min 1, Max INF.) How often (in ticks) does the mod graph the result data. Note that this option must not equal the lower option. At 1, the graph is perfect to the data supplied, but has a large UPS cost. 60 is a good starting point for UPS efficiency. Campaign default: 240.

Pollution_statistics.label: Pollution polling frequency
Pollution_statistics.description: (Default 180, Min 1, Max INF.) How often (in ticks) does the mod poll the pollution level. Note that this option must not equal the upper option. Higher value generate less accurate data, but have less of a UPS cost. Campaign default: 240.

Pollution_statistics.label: Pollution graph scale constant
Pollution_statistics.description: (Default 400) Affects the vertical scale of the pollution graph. Note that changing this value in an existing save will not affect data generated after the change, meaning it will be distorted in comparison to the current scaled data. The scale of the graph is a reciprocal of this value. Campaign default: 800

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Factor | Player Count
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Factor to increase resource usage by. This is usually the target player count per team. Default is 3.

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Fuel Value Divisor
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Divisor to decrease fuel value of wood and coal by. A high divisor will render coal miners useless. See mod FAQ page for details. Default is 3.

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Increased Tree Yield
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Since wood usage is increased this means more chopping. Check this box if you do NOT want that. Default is on.

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Increased Rock Yield
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Since stone usage is increased this means more picking. Check this box if you do NOT want that. Default is on.

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Affect Offshore Pump
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Also decrease offshore pump's pumping speed by given factor. Default is on.

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Be Verbose

WeNeedMoreDrills.label: Affect Sulfur
WeNeedMoreDrills.description: Since Bob's Ores introduces sulfur as a resource.
