extra_biter_control.label: Game Starting Evolution Percentage
extra_biter_control.description: The game will start at this evolution percentage and not be allowed to go below it. Game default value is "0". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Maximum Evolution Percentage
extra_biter_control.description: The game will not be able to have evolution above this percentage. Game default value is "100". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biters Collision Box Percentage
extra_biter_control.description: Set the biters collision box percentage of default. A smaller collision box allows them to move around each other easier, but also more can attack a building at once. Game default value is "100". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spitter Collision Box Percentage
extra_biter_control.description: Set the spitters collision box percentage of default. A smaller collision box allows them to move around each other easier, but also more can attack a building at once. Game default value is "100". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biters and Spitters Minimum Ticks Pursue
extra_biter_control.description: The minimum time that all biters and spitters will pursue for regardless of distance, before giving up. Game default value is "600". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biters and Spitters Maximum Tiles Pursue
extra_biter_control.description: The maximum tiles that pursuing biters and spitters will pursue for before giving up. Game default value is "50". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biters and Spitters Tiles Vision
extra_biter_control.description: How many tiles a biter or spitter will spot targets at. Game default value is "30". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biters and Spitters Immune To Belts
extra_biter_control.description: Biters and spitters are not affected by belts. Game default value is "No".

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Max Pollution Absorption
extra_biter_control.description: Maximum pollution each spawner is able to absorb per tick. Game default value is "20". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Percentage Pollution Absorption
extra_biter_control.description: Percentage of areas pollution each spawner will try to absorb per tick. Game default value is "1". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Max Concurrent Units
extra_biter_control.description: How many units the spawner can have concurrently on the map not including those in an attacking party. Game default value is "7". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Max Nearby Friendly Units
extra_biter_control.description: The limit of nearby (default 10 tiles) friendly units this spawner will stop producing new units at, will include other spawner's units within area. Some of this spawners units will patrol beyond the nearby radius at times and so not be counted during this time. Game default value is "5". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Min Evolution Unit Creation Tick Cooldown
extra_biter_control.description: The tick cooldown on spawners making units when evolution is at 0%. Sliding scale based on evolution percentage. Game default value is "360". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Max Evolution Unit Creation Tick Cooldown
extra_biter_control.description: The tick cooldown on spawners making units when evolution is at 100%. Sliding scale based on evolution percentage. Game default value is "150". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Spawner Call In Biters To Defend Tiles Range
extra_biter_control.description: The range (tiles) that a spawner will call in biters from when it is attacked. Game default value is "50". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Worm (turret) Call In Biters TO Defend Tiles Range
extra_biter_control.description: The range (tiles) that a worm (turret) will call in biters from when it is attacked. Game default value is "40". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Pathfinder Maximum Concurrent Long Path Processing
extra_biter_control.description: Maximum concurrent long path (over 100 tiles) processing tasks that will be done. Over-rights the config key "max_clients_to_accept_any_new_request". Higher values may cause lag. Game default value is "10". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Pathfinder Maximum Concurrent Total Path Processing
extra_biter_control.description: Maximum concurrent total path (long and short) processing tasks that will be done. Over-rights the config key "max_clients_to_accept_short_new_request". Higher values may cause lag. Game default value is "100". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Pathfinder Maximum Steps Processed Per Tick
extra_biter_control.description: Maximum number of steps processed per tick. Increasing this reduces biter pathfinding waits, but increases max UPS usage for pathfinding. Game default value is "100". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biter and Spitter Death Blood Enabled
extra_biter_control.description: Disabling death blood reduces UPS spikes when killing large groups of enemies. Game default value is on, but it can't be forced on via the mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Biter and Spitter Death Corpse Decay Seconds
extra_biter_control.description: How long in seconds biter and spitter corpses take to decay. Very high numbers of corpses can cause high FPS load. Game default value is "900", 15 minutes. "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod. Setting to 0 will not create any biter and spitter corpses.

extra_biter_control.label: Maximum Number of Enemy Unit Groups Gathering Simultaneously
extra_biter_control.description: How many enemy unit groups can be gathering for an attack at the same time. Game default value is "30". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

extra_biter_control.label: Maximum Enemy Unit Group Size
extra_biter_control.description: Maximum number of enemy units that can be in an attack group. Game default value is "200". "-1" to remain unchanged by this mod.

biter_reincarnation.label: Turn to rock chance
biter_reincarnation.description: The percent change of a biter turning in to a rock on death. Rocks are large reincarnations and will obey the setting to push movable entities, crushing others. Combined event chances can be greater than 100%.

biter_reincarnation.label: Turn to cliff chance
biter_reincarnation.description: The percent change of a biter turning in to a cliff on death. Cliffs are large reincarnations and will obey the setting to push movable entities, crushing others. Combined event chances can be greater than 100%.

biter_reincarnation.label: Large reincarantions push things away
biter_reincarnation.description: If enabled when large things are created they will try and push movable things out of their way. Anything not moved will be crushed.

biter_reincarnation.label: Max reincarnations per second
biter_reincarnation.description: This only includes biters that are within the reincranate chance, but will include failed reincarante attempts due to no valid placement for a tree. Reincarantions are spread out over the second to balance CPU load.

biter_reincarnation.label: Max reincarnation queued seconds
biter_reincarnation.description: Max seconds a reincarnation can be queued for before its discarded. This is to stop bulk reincarnation events from causing a very long running queue.

heavyfreight.label: Fuel Cost Multiplier
heavyfreight.description: Multiplier to fuel consumption.  100x is balanced for Angels (due to coke pellets total MJ per stack), 50x if you use my fuel stack balance mod. 10x is easier but still with noticible cost and 400x will require refuling or higher quality fuel for all but short runs.  1x uses default settings.

heavyfreight.label: Restrict Fuel Inventory Size
heavyfreight.description: Restricts fuel inventory size to 1 to make higher quality fuel more valuable.  NOTE: You will need to manage fuel carefully if you use more than one type.

heavyfreight.label: Reduce brake effectivity
heavyfreight.description: Reduces effeciveness of brakes so trains take longer to stop.  At 4 stopping distance is slightly longer than time to accelerate to full speed.  Set to 8 if you want brakes/acceleration to be similar after upgrading tech.  Set to 2 for less of an effect, or 1 to disable.

inbuilt_lighting.label: Power Poles Lighted Wire Reach Percentage
inbuilt_lighting.description: The percentage of each power pole's wire reach that is lit. Scales with power pole reach. Setting to 0 will remove the lights. Mod Default Setting = 100

inbuilt_lighting.label: Inbuilt Light Power Usage (watts)
inbuilt_lighting.description: The power usage of each inbuilt light. When set to 0 watts no electrical network is required for them to work. Anything above 0 watts requires active electricity for them to work. A standard light is 5000 watts. Mod Default Setting = 0.

inbuilt_lighting.label: Turrets Edge Tiles Lighted
inbuilt_lighting.description: If all turrets are lighted and the number of tiles beyond the edge lit. Setting to 0 is just the turret size. Setting to -1 disables the feature. Use in early game only as once above 500 turrets it can slow down UPS/game speed. Mod Default Setting = -1

inbuilt_lighting.label: Require Resarch First
inbuilt_lighting.description: Adds a cheap early game research that must be completed to get the lighting feature.

inbuilt_lighting.label: Light Brightness
inbuilt_lighting.description: The range is from 0 (no light) to 1 (full light). 0.6 is the default value.

Bioluminescence.label: Make biters glow in the dark
Use LuaRendering control script lights
Bioluminescence.description: Whether the lights on the plants use the LuaRendering mod scripting system for adding lights. This is cleaner and more reliable, but is markedly worse for client framerate performance on large maps. If this option is false, the lights will be accomplished with hidden entities instead, which does not have the FPS impact, but is messier and may cause weird issues like rails not working properly if placed directly adjacent to glowing plants, or lights persisting after their plant is removed.

pipelayer.label: Show deconstruction warning
pipelayer.description: When enabled, show a warning with the number of pipes marked for deconstruction when deconstructing a pipe connector.

pipelayer.label: Update period
pipelayer.description: How often in ticks to update a network.\n\nIncrease to reduce UPS consumption, decrease for more frequent fluid transfers.

pipelayer.label: Transfer threshold
pipelayer.description: The minimum amount of fluid for an input and the minimum amount of space for an output to transfer fluid between them.\n\nIncrease to reduce UPS consumption (you may also need to increase Connector capacity), decrease to reduce buffered fluid.

pipelayer.label: Show network IDs
pipelayer.description: Shows numbers over underground pipes identifying what network they are a part of.

pipelayer.label: Marker range

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-bold][color=230,208,175]Available default settings[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description: These presets are currently loaded. If there is more than one, all of them are loaded on top of each other.\nTo see the generated default values, reset to defaults.\n[font=default-bold][color=230,208,175]This setting does nothing[/color][/font], it's just information for you, so there's no point in choosing anything.

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-bold][color=230,208,175]Randomizer seed[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description: Change this value to generate different recipes.\n\n[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]0[/color] min: [color=230,208,175]0[/color] max: [color=230,208,175]1099511627775[/color][/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Crafting time randomization[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How random can crafting times be (and with which values can recipe times be multiplied).

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]Medium (0.25x to 2x)
Huge (0.2x to 5x)[/color] - unlike other options, picks the values from a continuous range[/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Dependency checking[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How are dependencies checked.

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]Linear[/color]
[color=230,208,175]None[/color] - Recipes can contain ingredients which are not unlocked yet. May cause deadlocks.
[color=230,208,175]Linear[/color] - Technologies are evaluated in a random order, while checking dependencies. Recipes can contain ingredients which are not necessarily available, but are unlockable.
[color=230,208,175]Branched[/color] - Each recipe unlocked by a technology contains ingredients only from the tech's prerequisites. Significantly slower.[/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Resource ratio variance[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How much can "resource ratio" differ from the original.
[color=230,208,175]For example [recipe=automation-science-pack] takes some [item=copper-ore] and slightly more [item=iron-ore].[/color]

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]2[/color] min: [color=230,208,175]1[/color] max: [color=230,208,175]5[/color]
This setting scales exponentially. Small tweaks lead to big changes.[/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Complexity variance[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How much can "recipe complexity" differ from the original.
[color=230,208,175]For example [recipe=automation-science-pack] is about as complex as [recipe=electronic-circuit] and both are more complex than [recipe=iron-chest] despite being cheaper.[/color]

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]2[/color] min: [color=230,208,175]1[/color] max: [color=230,208,175]5[/color]
This setting scales exponentially. Small tweaks lead to big changes.[/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Recipe cost variance[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How much can "recipe cost" differ from the original.
[color=230,208,175]For example [recipe=steel-plate] is 2.5 times more expensive than [recipe=iron-gear-wheel].[/color]

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]2[/color] min: [color=230,208,175]1[/color] max: [color=230,208,175]5[/color]
This setting scales exponentially. Small tweaks lead to big changes.[/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: [font=default-semibold][color=230,208,175]Hidden recipes[/color][/font]
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
How to treat hidden recipes.
[color=230,208,175]Hidden recipes are usually fixed recipes (like rocket parts) or auto-generated recipes (such as recycling).[/color]

[font=default-small-semibold]default: [color=230,208,175]Don't randomize[/color][/font]

ZRecipeRandomizer.label: Raw resources
ZRecipeRandomizer.description:
Here you can set when is which raw resource unlocked and how much is it worth.
Usage [color=230,208,175](prerequisites : resources : value)[/color].
For example [color=230,208,175]([item=electric-mining-drill][fluid=sulfuric-acid] : [item=uranium-ore] : 3)[/color].
[color=230,208,175]Write prerequisites as [technology=name] or a list of [item=name] and [fluid=name], keep empty for no prerequisites.
Write resources as a list of [item=name] or [fluid=name].
Value is a number representing how much are the resources worth.
Spaces are ignored.
You can set multiple valueas for a resource, each with different prerequisites.[/color]

[font=default-small-semibold]default value controlled by [color=230,208,175]available default settings[/color][/font]

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per worm killed
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by worms being killed. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per biter unit killed
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by biter units being killed. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per Rampant hive killed
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by Rampant hives being killed. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per Spawner killed
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by spawners being killed. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per tile absorbed pollution
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by pollution being absorbed by tiles. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per tree damaged by pollution
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by pollution damaging trees. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per tree absorbed pollution
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by pollution being absorbed by trees. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per Spawner absorbed pollution
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by pollution being absorbed by spawners. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Recalculate evolution when settings change
RampantEvolution.description: When this setting is checked the evolution will be recalculated from the beginning of the game when mod settings change. This will not be a perfect reconstruction of the past evolution.

RampantEvolution.label: Interval to show evolution in console or gui in minutes
RampantEvolution.description: This is the interval that the evolution will be displayed on the console or in the gui. /rampantEvolution in the console will display the stats on-demand.

RampantEvolution.label: Enable console messages showing evolution
RampantEvolution.description: This is the setting to enable evolution to be displayed on the console at the specified interval. /rampantEvolution in the console will display the stats on-demand.

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per pollution generated
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by pollution being generated. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Evolution per second elapsed
RampantEvolution.description: This setting changes how evolution should be affected by time elapsed in seconds. This number should be treated the same as the vanilla pollution, spawner, and time sliders in terms of how to interpret it

RampantEvolution.label: Pause vanilla evolution factors (Permanent)
RampantEvolution.description: If you have an existing save that you want to use this mod on and you want to pause the original map evolution settings. THIS IS PERMANENT, IF YOU REMOVE THE MOD WITH THIS SETTING CHECKED THE EVOLUTION WILL STAY PAUSED. UNCHECKING SHOULD RE-ENABLE THE VANILLA EVOLUTION.

RampantEvolution.label: Peak evolution minimum percentage
RampantEvolution.description: Everytime the evolution goes up, this percentage is multiplied by evolution and stored as the lowest value the evolution can reach. So if you set the mod setting to 0.25 and your evolution hits 10% the lowest your evolution can go to is 2.5%

RampantEvolution.label: Reconstruction accuracy (0 is auto based on ticks)
RampantEvolution.description: The number of delta counts to compute at a single point. The higher the number the worse the accuracy for recalculating evolution. The tradeoff is low numbers will take a long time to finish recalculating. When this number is 0 it will be auto calcaluted based on the number of ticks in the game. On auto mode, accuracy starts at 20 and moves to 4000 based on x where x is game.ticks / (80 hrs). At 4000, an 80 hour game will take ~15 minutes to recalculate.

HallOfFame.label: Volume Modifier

HallOfFame.label: Zoom Modifier
HallOfFame.description: Different resolution screens will display the simulations at different zoom levels. Adjust this value if it doesn't fit nicely on your screen. Lower values for smaller screens, and higher for bigger screens. Default 1.

HallOfFame.label: Mute Sound-Driven Simulations
HallOfFame.description: Mute all simulations that are sound driven, e.g. Daft Punk.

HallOfFame.label: Simulations with Moving Camera
HallOfFame.description: Enable simulations with a moving camera, e.g. the camera following Gotyoke in the TAS speedrun. Disabled by default for a more comfortable viewing experience.

LogisticRequestManager.label: Create the GUI without checking for technologies
LogisticRequestManager.description: May help to access LRM if another Mod removes the technologie 'logistic-robotics'. Try the command [color=yellow]/lrm force_gui[/color] first before enabeling this!

LogisticRequestManager.label: Create a preset to clear the inventory
LogisticRequestManager.description: The preset consists of requests for all existing items. For all that don't provide an equipment grid themselves, the upper limit is set to zero to remove them from the inventory.\n[color=yellow]This setting does only have an effect on player creation or when loading a game with an old version of LRM![/color]

LogisticRequestManager.label: Create a preset that contains every item without requesting it
LogisticRequestManager.description: The preset consists of requests for all existing items. The lower limit is set to zero, the upper limit to ∞ at each item, so they are neither requested nor removed from the inventory.\n[color=yellow]This setting does only have an effect on player creation or when loading a game with an old version of LRM![/color]

LogisticRequestManager.label: Use character as default target for LRM GUI
LogisticRequestManager.description: Use the character as default target for all interactions with the Logistic Request Manager GUI if no entity that supports logistic requests is opened.

LogisticRequestManager.label: Allow constant combinators to be used similar to chests
LogisticRequestManager.description: Use constant combinators to apply requests that can be manipulated by the logic circuitry. They can also be used as source for a preset, if this setting is enabled.

LogisticRequestManager.label: Append requests at the end
LogisticRequestManager.description: If true, existing gaps will not be filled when appending presets to existing requests.

LogisticRequestManager.label: Always add blueprint items to requests
LogisticRequestManager.description: Items requested for blueprints are added to existing requests, regardless of the setting "Add presets to requests" below. (default: enabled)

LogisticRequestManager.label: Set max value for new item requests for blueprints to ∞
LogisticRequestManager.description: If enabled, new item requests that are generated for blueprints will be configured with max=∞, otherwise with max=min, if a max-value is applicable (for player character etc.). (default: disabled)

LogisticRequestManager.label: Add presets to requests
LogisticRequestManager.description: If enabled, presets can be added to existing requests instead of replacing them. (default: "with modifier")

LogisticRequestManager.label: Round item requests up to next full stack
LogisticRequestManager.description: If enabled, item-requests will be rounded up to the next full stack when applied. (default: "with modifier")

LogisticRequestManager.label: Save chest-presets with max=∞
LogisticRequestManager.description: If enabled, the max value of a request will be set ∞ when saving a preset from a chest (or constant combinator). Otherwise it max will be set to the same value as the configured (min-)value (default: "with modifier")

LogisticRequestManager.label: Modifier to add presets to requests
Modifier to round up to next stack when applying preset
Modifier to save new request from chests with max=∞
GUI: preset-slot updates per Tick
LogisticRequestManager.description: Configures, how many GUI-slots are updated per tick. Can help to increase performance, wenn previewing very large presets. 0: no limit (default)

LogisticRequestManager.label: Warn when saving a large preset
LogisticRequestManager.description: When saving a preset with more than 100 items print a hint pointing to the settings.

WideChestsLogistic.description: Requested items in merged requester chests will be copied to all split chests.

Quick-Charge-Personal-Bots-Continued-Plu.description: This settings determines how often (in ticks) the script to add energy will run.

Quick-Charge-Personal-Bots-Continued-Plu.description: This modifies the speed at which the personal roboport charges worker robots

EditorExtensions.label: Include hidden items in aggregate chests
Allow changing aggregate chest filters [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: By default, aggregate chest filters are unchangeable, because the mod will overwrite any changes whenever mod configuration changes. If you wish to be able to edit the filters despite this, check this option.

EditorExtensions.label: Editor fill built entity energy buffers
Editor inventory size [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: This option cannot be changed at runtime.\nAll of the below options are defaults, and can be changed at runtime via the map editor GUI.

EditorExtensions.label: Show character tab in editor GUI
Show infinity filters in editor GUI
Default infinity filters [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: Infinity filters that will be applied to your inventory when you enter the editor for the first time.\n[color=255,57,48]Change this from the main menu, otherwise it will not effect new games![/color]

EditorExtensions.label: Hijack debug world [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: Control + click the "Single player" button to spawn a new 50x50 freeplay world. This setting hijacks this debug world to replace it with lab tiles, research all technologies, and give you the EE loadout.

EditorExtensions.label: Snap infinity pipe filter to adjacent crafter inputs [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: When you place an infinity pipe directly next to a crafter fluid input, it will automatically set its filter to provide that fluid.

EditorExtensions.label: Sync inventory and cursor between play modes [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: When in cheat mode, your inventory and cursor stack will be synced between the editor and normal play.

EditorExtensions.label: Prevent initial pause [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: Prevent the game pausing the simulation when you enter the editor for the first time. The paused state can be changed from the time editor menu.

EditorExtensions.label: Start in editor [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: Automatically enter the map editor when entering the debug world or testing scenario.\nDebug world requires "Hijack debug world" to be enabled.

EditorExtensions.label: Testing lab [img=info]
EditorExtensions.description: Automatically teleport to a testing lab when entering the map editor, then back out when you leave the editor. This allows you to easily test setups in an isolated space, while keeping your actual factory pristine. Choose between your own personal lab, and a lab shared among all players.\n\nDisabling inventory sync allows you to use this in a completely cheat-proof way in regular playthroughs.

aai-containers.label: Reduce 1x1 container collision
aai-containers.description: Maintains a consistent spacing between containers that you can walk through.

aai-containers.label: Scale container alt-icon with size
aai-containers.description: The alt-mode icon shown over the container will be scaled up with the container's footprint.

aai-containers.label: Inventory size progression
aai-containers.description: Inventory size of Wooden chest, Iron chest, Steel chest, Strongbox, Storeshouse, Warehouse. CD = Consistent density per tile for steel+. Warning: High inventory size containers reduce UPS, it is not advised to go over 540 max inventory size.

aai-containers.label: Show the container size number in the icon
aai-containers.description: By default you can see the container size with a number in the top left of the icon.

GhostInHand.label: Disable when any GUI open
GhostInHand.description: If selected, when any GUI is open (such as chest, vehicle inventory, assembling machine etc.), when you run out of the held item, the mod will assume that you placed it in the building/vehicle and will not replace it with a ghost.

KingsTurret-Shields.label: Passive energy consumption (%)
KingsTurret-Shields.description: A value of 1 here means a 10k shield cap, means 100KW drain per shield. (0.1 - [10] - 50)

KingsTurret-Shields.label: Maximum research level
KingsTurret-Shields.description: Helps alleviate failures to start due to 'Reached id limit for entity'. A value of 100 here means 100^2 or 10,000 entities will be created. Factorio has a limit of 65536 entity definitions. (5 - [25] - 100)

KingsTurret-Shields.label: Shield Compression Factor
KingsTurret-Shields.description: If set to 50, one shield has the power draw/recharge/limit/etc of 50 shields. ([1] - 1000)

hourly_autosaves.label: Save name prefix
hourly_autosaves.description: The prefix to use for the names of the hourly autosaves

hourly_autosaves.label: Autosave interval (in minutes)
hourly_autosaves.description: The number of minutes between autosaves being created

hourly_autosaves.label: Debug mode enabled
hourly_autosaves.description: Whether or not to enable debug mode (which does things like print debug messages)

stack-combinator.label: Enable debug mode [img=info]
stack-combinator.description: Debug mode enables more detailed logging of actions the mod performs. During gameplay, debug messages are printed to in-game console and to a file in `script-output` folder. During startup, they're logged to the main game log.

stack-combinator.label: Default input inversion [img=info]
stack-combinator.description: Choose which wire's input signals invert by default on newly placed combinators. See the mod's full description for more information on signal inversion.

stack-combinator.label: Maximum signal capacity [img=info]
stack-combinator.description: Maximum number of signals that a stack combinator can output. Higher values may* affect performance with large numbers of stack combinators in use.\n\n* Untested.

stack-combinator.label: Require power [img=info]
stack-combinator.description: Should the stack combinator require electricity to work?

stack-combinator.label: Signal update delay (ticks) [img=info]
stack-combinator.description: How many ticks to wait between updates (reading incoming signals and calculating outputs). Increase this if you use a lot of StaCos and it's impacting performance, but be aware that the longer the delay, the longer outdated signals remain on the circuit network.

Hiladdar_Core.label: No Cliffs on Map
Hiladdar_Core.description: Destroy all cliffs on the start up map, but allow cliffs to be generated normally after initial map generation.

Hiladdar_Core.label: Hand Crafting Speed
Hiladdar_Core.description: Research to increase hand crafting speed

Hiladdar_Core.label: Larger Inventory
Hiladdar_Core.description: Infinite research to increase player inventory

Hiladdar_Core.label: Logistics Slots
Hiladdar_Core.description: Infinite research to increase the players logistical request slots

Hiladdar_Core.label: Logistical Trash Slots
Hiladdar_Core.description: Infinite research to increase the player's logistical trash slots

Hiladdar_Core.label: Gravitanium Ore
Hiladdar_Core.description: Gravitanium Ore will be generated on the map if Gear mod is installed

IslandStart.label: (Legacy) Enable Direct Placement Mode
IslandStart.description: Enables manual tile or entity placement (rather than using the in-game mapgen system). This forms a circle and looks much less natural than using the map generation preset. This is not needed if using the map generation preset.

IslandStart.label: (Legacy) Perimeter Type
IslandStart.description: Determines the composition of your perimeter. Only works if enabled; not needed if using the map generation preset.

IslandStart.label: (Legacy) Placement Override
IslandStart.description: Forces placement of walls even on invalid or occupied terrain. This means walls will be placed over water, trees, cliffs, and so forth (without destroying them).

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Request from buffers
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: If set to true, all interfaces will automatically be set to request ammo from buffers. False lets you customize each interface.

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Loaded magazines (1-10)
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: The amount of ammo to keep in each turret. As the mod only checks each turret once every two seconds, having this too low can cause turrets to run out before the next reload. Note: 2 is enougth for vanilla turrets with even max shooting speed, but may not be enougth for modded turrets.

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Early available
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: If true the logistic turret research is substantially easier and turret interfaces are cheaper as well.

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Auto interface
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: Whether placed turrets should automatically blueprint a turret interface upon placement.

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Broadcast request slots setup
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: When set to true, changing any interface request slot will broadcast setup to other interfaces on the same logistic network. Newly created interface will also receive default setup from logistic network if any.

Logistic-Gun-Turret.label: Reloading period (60-300 ticks)
Logistic-Gun-Turret.description: During this period all turrets will be triggered once to eventually reload.
Default number of items requested by logistic interface.

QuickItemSearch.label: Auto-close window [img=info]

QuickItemSearch.label: Include hidden items in search results

combat-mechanics-overhaul.label: Worm spit blockable
combat-mechanics-overhaul.description: Worm spit can be blocked by walls. Makes worm spit into blockable projectiles. If disabled then worm spit is a stream that arcs over walls.

combat-mechanics-overhaul.label: Rockets blockable
combat-mechanics-overhaul.description: Rockets can collide with trees and enemy walls. Good for PvP.

combat-mechanics-overhaul.label: Pools affect structures
combat-mechanics-overhaul.description: Pools, such as worm acid pools, affect structures.

combat-mechanics-overhaul.label: Pools affect flying

combat-mechanics-overhaul.label: Shotguns Hit Friendly

bulkteleport.label: Fluid dematerializer fill level
bulkteleport.description: Due to Factorio fluid physics it can take a long time to fill fluid tanks the last little bit. This lowers the "full" line so teleportation triggers promptly. However, if you're pumping directly into fluid dematerializers and prefer round numbers this is safe to raise back to 1.0.

This has 2 advantages:

-Inserters will only fill 10 magazines into the turret, instead of a stack

cargo-ships-tweaks.label: Adjust inventory size

Swarmageddon.label: Number of seconds corpses remain on the ground
Swarmageddon.description: Standard factorio is 5 minutes. With each biter spawning several more, large attacks can leave thousands of corpses on the ground. Use this setting to determine how fast those corpses will disappear, in seconds.

Skymageddon.label: Number of seconds corpses remain on the ground
Skymageddon.description: Standard factorio is 5 minutes. With each biter spawning several more, large attacks can leave thousands of corpses on the ground. Use this setting to determine how fast those corpses will disappear, in seconds.

Swarmageddon.label: Maximum number of new biters per tick
Swarmageddon.description: Global limit on number of biters to spawn at once. Lower will increase performance but also make it easier (higher chance of hitting the limit and not spawning.)

Skymageddon.label: Maximum number of new biters per tick
Skymageddon.description: Global limit on number of biters to spawn at once. Lower will increase performance but also make it easier (higher chance of hitting the limit and not spawning.)

Swarmageddon.label: Reduce spawning when player is getting overrun
Swarmageddon.description: Lower number \= easier. Reduce spawns when the player is losing an average of this many units in the past minute. Goes to zero extra spawns when exceeding this value.

Skymageddon.label: Reduce spawning when player is getting overrun
Skymageddon.description: Lower number \= easier. Reduce spawns when the player is losing an average of this many units in the past minute. Goes to zero extra spawns when exceeding this value.

Swarmageddon.label: Enable or disable code to reduce spawning if getting overrun

no-wall-repair.description: Higher is more walls able to repair at a time. Lower is (somewhat) better performance.

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Roboport Range Multiplier
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description: Multiplies both construction/logistics default or previously-modded ranges by this factor.\nUse 1 for no changes, >1 to increase, or e.g. 0.5 to reduce it. Result will be rounded to nearest integer value.\nApplied before range values below.

no-take-only-throw.label: Inserter Range
no-take-only-throw.description: Default is 15. Long handed inserters are 5/3 of this. Setting this too high can lag the game with long handed inserters, best stay below ~50.

betterartillerysounds.label: Ranger multiplier
betterartillerysounds.description: Accept decimal number > 0. So if you want to reduce the range by 2, just set 0.5. If you want to double it, set it to 2. (1 = sound up to 1000 tiles)

Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.label: Roboport Range Multiplier
Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.description: Multiplies both construction/logistics default or previously-modded ranges by this factor.\nUse 1 for no changes, >1 to increase, or e.g. 0.5 to reduce it. Result will be rounded to nearest integer value.\nApplied before range values below.

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Roboport Logistics Range
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description:
Logistics bot range (radius) of the roboport.
Default/vanilla is 25 (displayed as 50x50 on roboport).
Special values: -1 - do not change it via this option, -2 - set to be equal to construction range.
Applied after multiplier above and after static construction range value (if set).

Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.label: Roboport Logistics Range
Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.description:
Logistics bot range (radius) of the roboport.
Default/vanilla is 25 (displayed as 50x50 on roboport).
Special values: -1 - do not change it via this option, -2 - set to be equal to construction range.
Applied after multiplier above and after static construction range value (if set).

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Roboport Construction Range
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description:
Construction bot range (radius) of the roboport.
Default/vanilla is 55 (displayed as 110x110 on roboport).
Special values: -1 - do not change it via this option, -2 - set to be equal to logistics range.
Applied after multiplier above and after static logistics range value (if set).

Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.label: Roboport Construction Range
Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.description:
Construction bot range (radius) of the roboport.
Default/vanilla is 55 (displayed as 110x110 on roboport).
Special values: -1 - do not change it via this option, -2 - set to be equal to logistics range.
Applied after multiplier above and after static logistics range value (if set).

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Min Range to affect it
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description: Minimum range (radius) value to affect it by range options above.\nUse this to avoid affecting roboports that are "recharge stations" and such, that have no or tiny robot range and are not supposed to have it.\nConstruction/logistic ranges on same roboport are checked and tweaked separately.

Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.label: Min Range to affect it
Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.description: Minimum range (radius) value to affect it by range options above.\nUse this to avoid affecting roboports that are "recharge stations" and such, that have no or tiny robot range and are not supposed to have it.\nConstruction/logistic ranges on same roboport are checked and tweaked separately.

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Robot Energy Multiplier
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description: Max energy value (battery capacity) multiplier for construction and logistic robots. Values >1 will allow these bots to fly longer without running out of power.

Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.label: Robot Energy Multiplier
Configurable_Roboport_Range_aaa.description: Max energy value (battery capacity) multiplier for construction and logistic robots. Values >1 will allow these bots to fly longer without running out of power.

Configurable_Roboport_Range.label: Affect Mod Roboports/Robots
Configurable_Roboport_Range.description: If enabled (default), mod will affect all roboports/robots in their respective categories, including those added by mods, and only ones from base game otherwise.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for this game
MaintenanceMadness.description: Enable this setting, if you want to use this mod for your game. Overrides all other settings.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Maintenance cost level
MaintenanceMadness.description:
Amounts of materials required for the maintenance and repair of machinery. The higher this cost, the harder it will be to keep large bases in check.

Possible values:
Reduced: 50%
Normal: 100%
Expensive: 150%
Grueling: 250%

MaintenanceMadness.label: Show machine state changes
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is set to active, a flying text is shown for a short moment every time a machine changes its state (e.g. "Malfunction" or "repaired").

MaintenanceMadness.label: Show "Repairing"-Sign for solar and accus
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is set to active, the orange "repair in progress" sign will also be displayed on solar panels and accumulators. This option is disabled by default to save on FPS.\nChanging this setting will only take effect slowly.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Expected machine life time [h]
MaintenanceMadness.description: The expected life time of a machine in hours.\n\nGreater values reduce the cost of machine replacements but somewhat increase the cost of regular repairs.

MaintenanceMadness.label: MTBM [min]
MaintenanceMadness.description: Mean time between two maintenance events in minutes.\n\nThe shorter this time, the more frequently machines have to be serviced or repaired. If you set this value to a very low value, the game may slow down if your factory is very large.

MaintenanceMadness.label: MTTM [min]
MaintenanceMadness.description: Mean time needed to service a machine.\n\nAfter this time, the machine checks if the the requested maintenance materials have been delivered. The shorter this time, the more difficult it is for robots to deliver the materials in time.

MaintenanceMadness.label: MTTR [min]
MaintenanceMadness.description: Mean time needed to repair a broken down machine.\n\nThis time increases proportionally to the age of the machine. The affected machine is completely inactive during this time. The greater this value, the more severe is the impact of broken down machines on the overal throughput of your factory.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for accumulators
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, accumulators require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for solar panels
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, solar panels require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for reactors
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, reactors require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for boilers and generators
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, boilers and generators require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for miners
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, resource miner require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for roboports
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, roboports require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for beacons
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, beacons require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Enable maintenance for labs
MaintenanceMadness.description: If this option is enabled, labs require regular servicing and repair.\n\nWARNING: This setting should only be changed in a running game.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Cycle time multiplier for solar and accus
MaintenanceMadness.description: This multiplier determines how long a maintenance cycle for solar panels or accumulators lasts.\nAging and material requirements are also multiplied. This is mostly to reduce UPS impact on large bases with significant amounts of solar panels and accumulators.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Default replacement age [%]
MaintenanceMadness.description: The default age in percent of the expected life time, from which machines start to request replacement.\n\nThe lower this value, the shorter is the mean life cycle of the machines in your factory, which increases the overall cost. Setting this to a higher value will save on materials but will also reduce your factory's throughput, as older machines tend to break down more often.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Wear reduction if idle [%]
MaintenanceMadness.description: Probability in percent that a machine will not age if it hasn't finished any goods in the last maintenance interval.\n\nThis applies to assembling machines, furnaces, refineries, mining drills, labs, reactors, boilers and generators

MaintenanceMadness.label: Extra ageing by bad maintenance [%]
MaintenanceMadness.description: This value determines the maximum percentage by which a machine ages additionally if none of the requested maintenance materials have been delivered. This effect is reduced if the requirement is partially met.\n\nHigher values increase the importance of regular maintenance. A value of 0 renders maintenance irrelevant.

MaintenanceMadness.label: Less maintenance at game start
MaintenanceMadness.description:
[font=default-bold]If enabled, the probability for maintenance and repair events is greatly reduced at game start (only 20%).[/font]

The bonus is diminished whenever a faction researches technologies that are indirect or direct prerequisites of the defined target technology ("Rocket silo" by default). Technologies are weighted according to their research costs. If the target technology is researched, the bonus expires.

[font=default-bold][color=128, 206, 240]This setting is recommended for games with a long build-up phase[/color][/font]

MaintenanceMadness.label: Less maintenance at game start: Target technology
MaintenanceMadness.description: Determines the target technology if "Less maintenance at game start" is enabled.\n\nThe name of the technology must represent a valid prototype name. If no valid name is given, the setting is reset to "rocket-silo". Randomize-Science.label: Random Seed
Randomize-Science.description: Seed used to generate recipes. Should result in the same recipes if all flags are kept the same.

Randomize-Science.label: Replace Science Recipes
Randomize-Science.description: The whole mod. Without this you can only grab your Lock String and everything else is Vanilla science recipes.

Randomize-Science.label: Allow Fluid Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Allows fluids as science pack ingredients.

Randomize-Science.label: Allow Raw Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Allows 'Tier 0' the raw ores, coal, stone, and if desired wood/fish to be science pack ingredients.

Randomize-Science.label: Allow Wood-based Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Allows wood or wood-based ingredients in science pack recipes. Having access to a lot of wood through mods might be necessary if Allow Raw is also checked.

Randomize-Science.label: Randomize Crafted-in Building
Randomize-Science.description: Allows the entity that each science pack is crafted in to be randomized. Smelting is possible if there is only 1 ingredient.

Randomize-Science.label: Require Science Packs as Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Requires 1 science pack from previous tier as one of the ingredients in next science pack recipe. Helps smooth uneven balance.

Randomize-Science.label: Max Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Maximum number of different ingredients in each randomized recipe. Includes Science Packs toward max if checked. Prioritizes Min Ingredients value.

Randomize-Science.label: Min Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Minimum number of different ingredients in each randomized recipe. Includes Science Packs toward min if checked.

Randomize-Science.label: Lower Ingredient Pool Floor by
Randomize-Science.description: Expand lower cap on ingredient pools by this many tiers. Can make later recipes easier. There are about 2 tiers for each science level. Negative values will use random from 0 to positive value.

Randomize-Science.label: Raise Ingredient Pool Ceiling by
Randomize-Science.description: Expand upper cap on ingredient pools by this many tiers. Can make any recipe impossible without mods. There are about 2 tiers for each science level but they are already at the cap of what is normally possible. Negative values will use random from 0 to positive value.

Randomize-Science.label: Allow Fish as Raw Ingredient
Randomize-Science.description: Allows fish if Allow Raw is checked. Having access to a lot of fish through mods might be necessary.

Randomize-Science.label: Remove Too Expensive Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Remove ingredients that are too expensive from the pool, tuned by difficulty multiplier.

Randomize-Science.label: Tune Ingredient Balance by Multiplier
Randomize-Science.description: Total raw value of ingredients compared to vanilla multiplier. Can use 0.01 to 100. Negative values will use random from 1 to positive integer value.

Randomize-Science.label: Output Ratio Method
Randomize-Science.description: Method for determining number of packs produced and crafting time for each recipe.

Randomize-Science.label: Output Balanced Based on Ingredients
Randomize-Science.description: Further balance the output ratio based on the ingredients. Uses Ratio setting as base but makes adjustments to number of results or craft time from there.

Randomize-Science.label: Science Pack Order
Randomize-Science.description: Which order should the higher ingredient tiers be placed? Ingredients unlocked by eariler tier can be required for later tier.

ZoomPresets.label: Preset 1 zoom level
ZoomPresets.description:
Decrease the value to zoom out. Be careful with values lower than 0.1 as it might cause performance problems. To give you an idea of what the numbers mean, these are the values defined by the base game:
3 - maximum zoom in (whether on map or not)
1 - that's the zoom level that you start with when you load a game
0.275 - maximum player zoom out; while on the map, this is the zoom-to-world threshold
0.0035 - maximum zoom out on the map

Full_Power_Coverage_017.label: Power pole list mode
Full_Power_Coverage_017.description: When in blacklist mode, all item IDs entered below will be ignored. When in whitelist mode, only the item IDs below will have their supply area altered, ignoring all others.

Full_Power_Coverage_017.label: Power pole list
Full_Power_Coverage_017.description: A list of item IDs (separated by commas) that should either be whitelisted or blacklisted (depending on mode), if you only want to change the supply area of some power poles.

Full_Power_Coverage_017.label: Pattern matching
Full_Power_Coverage_017.description: Use fuzzy matching for the blacklist item IDs. This setting should be left alone unless you know you need it.

ZoomingReinvented.label: Zoom sensitivity
ZoomingReinvented.description: Defines how big is the change when zooming in or out. Doesn't apply to zooming in on the map (unless in 'zoom to world' view). The current zoom level will be multiplied or divided by this value when you zoom in or out. Base game's value is about 1.1 when the map is closed and about 1.25 when the map is open (regardless of whether it is in the 'zoom to world' view or in the map view).

Kux-Zooming.label: Zoom sensitivity
Kux-Zooming.description: Defines how big is the change when zooming in or out. Doesn't apply to zooming in on the map (unless in 'zoom to world' view). The current zoom level will be multiplied or divided by this value when you zoom in or out. Base game's value is about 1.1 when the map is closed and about 1.25 when the map is open (regardless of whether it is in the 'zoom to world' view or in the map view).

ZoomingReinvented.label: Max world zoom out level
ZoomingReinvented.description: Defines how far you can zoom out and still see the world. In the player view it defines maximum zoom out, in the map it defines when the 'zoom to world' view switches back to the map view. Base game's value is about 0.4.

Kux-Zooming.label: Max world zoom out level
Kux-Zooming.description: Defines how far you can zoom out and still see the world. In the player view it defines maximum zoom out, in the map it defines when the 'zoom to world' view switches back to the map view. Base game's value is about 0.4.

ZoomingReinvented.label: Default map zoom level
ZoomingReinvented.description: Defines at what zoom level the map opens. Base game's value is about 0.0313. Note that map labels disappear at zoom level below 0.0157.

Kux-Zooming.label: Default map zoom level
Kux-Zooming.description: Defines at what zoom level the map opens. Base game's value is about 0.0313. Note that map labels disappear at zoom level below 0.0157.

ZoomingReinvented.label: 'Quick zoom out' map zoom level

Kux-Zooming.label: 'Quick zoom out' map zoom level
Kux-Zooming.description: Defines at what zoom level the map opens when using 'Quick zoom out'. Note that map labels disappear at zoom level below 0.0157.

ZoomingReinvented.label: Binoculars zoom level

Kux-Zooming.label: Binoculars zoom level
Kux-Zooming.description: Defines at what zoom level the map opens when using the Binoculars item.

ZoomingReinvented.label: Enable Binoculars double-action
ZoomingReinvented.description: If enabled, when using Binoculars in the map view and the labels on the map are not visible, Binoculars will first zoom in only enough to show the map labels. Using them again will zoom in to the configured 'Binoculars zoom level'.

Kux-Zooming.label: Enable Binoculars double-action
Kux-Zooming.description: If enabled, when using Binoculars in the map view and the labels on the map are not visible, Binoculars will first zoom in only enough to show the map labels. Using them again will zoom in to the configured 'Binoculars zoom level'.

ZoomingReinvented.label: Disable map zoom out after map move
ZoomingReinvented.description: Defines whether to disable map zooming out after the map position has changed (by dragging, using move controls or zooming in). This is to prevent sudden map position changes when zooming out (see known issues for explanation why this happens). If this option is selected, after you move the map, the only way to zoom out is to reopen the map, use 'Quick zoom out' or zoom in to the 'zoom to world' view and hover over some object - this will update last known map position and allow to zoom out again.

Kux-Zooming.description: Defines whether to disable map zooming out after the map position has changed (by dragging, using move controls or zooming in). MyQuickStart.label: My Quick Start Kits
MyQuickStart.description:
Select your starting kit items.

Empty:
Little harder then default.

Tiny:
Little easier then default.

Game-default.
Easy as game default!

Default-militant
As default game except with the tank and some cleanup/deratisation materials.

Small:
A few belts, undergroundys, splitters, burner mining drills and plates.

Medium:
Construction Robots, Pipes, Personal Roboport, Assembling Machines, Electricity, Car

Big:
Some Belts, Poles, Assembling Machine 2's, Logistic Chest (Request/Provider/Storage), Roboports, Logistic Robots, Construction Robots and other stuff.
Unlocks all technologies required by the logistics system.

Huge:
A piece of cake. Almost everything. Biters become sweeters. All technologies(choosable) except rocket silo, rocket fuel and rocket control units.

Custom:
As said: custom. Meaning - all is on you and you are on your own. What you want you will get.

WaterTurret.label: Interval to check turrets (in seconds)
WaterTurret.description: Set the time to wait (in seconds) before a turret is checked again. Bigger values could take some load off UPS if you have many turrets, but it may take longer until turrets look for new fires in range.\nRange: 5…30\nDefault: 10

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-water-turret__ color
WaterTurret.description: Enter the color code in HTML notation (hexadecimal number with 6 digits, e.g. "#40adbf") or as a comma-separated list of 3 numbers in the range 0…255 (e.g. "63.8, 172.7, 191.2")!

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-fire-ex-turret__ color
WaterTurret.description: Enter the color code in HTML notation (hexadecimal number with 6 digits, e.g. "#fa0f0f") or as a comma-separated list of 3 numbers in the range 0…255 (e.g. "250, 15.1, 15.1")!

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-water-turret__ range
WaterTurret.description: Minimum is the range of normal flamethrower turrets. Increasing range will also increase the UPS load, so leaving this setting on default is recommended!\nRange: 30…100\nDefault: 50

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-fire-ex-turret__ range
WaterTurret.description: Minimum is the range of normal flamethrower turrets. Increasing range will also increase the UPS load, so leaving this setting on default is recommended!\nRange: 30…100\nDefault: 50

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-water-turret__ pressure modifier
WaterTurret.description: Increasing pressure will increase the speed of the turret's stream, so it will hit enemies earlier and do more damage. However, increasing pressure will also lead to a higher fluid consumption.

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: __ENTITY__WT-fire-ex-turret__ pressure modifier
WaterTurret.description: Turrets: Increasing pressure will increase the speed of the turret's stream, so it will hit enemies earlier and do more damage. However, increasing pressure will also lead to a higher fluid consumption.

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: Turrets clean up acid splashes
WaterTurret.description: If this is active, turrets will also attack acid splashes left behind by worms or spitters. All settings that affect how fires will be attacked also apply to acid splashes.\nDefault: true

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: Choose next target based on enemy health
WaterTurret.description: When several potential targets are in range, you can prefer to attack those with most health (slow down as many enemies as possible), those with least health (kill as many enemies as possible), or ignore enemy health.

WaterTurret.label: Turrets: Use hardened pipes
WaterTurret.description: If you use hardened pipes in the recipe, fire-extinguisher turrets will require more research, and producing them will become more complicated. On the other hand, hardened pipes provide resistance (or even immunity) against several damage types …

WaterTurret.label: Damage: Modifier for steam damage
WaterTurret.description: If the turret attacks with steam, the damage is multiplied with this factor.\nRange: 5…20\nDefault: 10

WaterTurret.label: Damage: __ENTITY__WT-fire-ex-turret__ damage modifier
WaterTurret.description: Due to advanced technology, these special fire-extinguisher turrets can extinguish fires faster than normal water turrets. Here you can set the factor.\nRange: 2…50\nDefault: 15 (Still need to find a good default value!)

WaterTurret.label: Damage: Slow-down factor (in percent)
WaterTurret.description: If a mobile target is hit by a __ENTITY__WT-water-turret__ or __ENTITY__WT-fire-ex-turret__, it's speed will be changed to this percentage. 10 means the enemy will be slowed down to 10% of its original speed, 100 means it won't be slowed down at all.\nDefault: 50

WaterTurret.label: Immunity: Don't hurt spawners
WaterTurret.description: Make spawners immune to damage from steam and water.\nDefault: true

WaterTurret.label: Immunity: Don't hurt turrets/worms
WaterTurret.description: Make worms and turrets immune to damage from steam and water.\nDefault: true

WaterTurret.label: Misc: Turrets slow down everybody
WaterTurret.description: If this is active, all players and their vehicles that are hit by a water or fire-extinguiser turret will be slowed down, no matter which force they belong to (recommended for better performance). Leave this unchecked if you don't want to be slowed down by turrets of your own force!\nDefault: on

WaterTurret.label: Misc: Target preferred by __ENTITY__WT-water-turret__
WaterTurret.description: If "Fire" or "Enemy" are selected, this target will be attacked with higher priority. If you don't care, the game will choose a target automatically, which may improve UPS.\nDefault: "I don't care!"

WaterTurret.label: Misc: Extinguish fires in this radius
WaterTurret.description: If a water turret loaded with water or a fire-extinguishing turret is fighting fire, all fires in this radius around the target position will be extinguished at once.\nHint: Smaller values are more realistic, while increasing the radius should improve performance.

WaterTurret.label: Bio Industries adds new recipe
WaterTurret.description: Bio Industries will let you use __ITEM__wood-charcoal__ in the recipe of Fire extinguisher fluid. If this is on, a new recipe will be added for this, otherwise the __ITEM__coal__ in the existing recipe will be replaced with __ITEM__wood-charcoal__.\nDefault: true

WaterTurret.label: Debugging: Activate debugging output in game
WaterTurret.description: This will activate insane debugging output in the game. You should leave this turned off unless you want to help to debug this mod.\nDefault: off

WaterTurret.label: Debugging: Activate logging
WaterTurret.description: This will activate insane debugging output to the log file. You should leave this turned off unless you want to help to debug this mod.\nDefault: off

WaterTurret.label: Debugging: Add support for GVV
WaterTurret.description: The "Lua API global Variable Viewer" (gvv) allows you to inspect the global table of other mods. If you want to help debugging "Water Turret", enable this and type "\gvv" at the chat console to open the GUI of gvv.\nDefault: off

WaterTurret.label: Damage: Modifier for fire-extinguisher fluid damage
WaterTurret.description: Using extinguisher fluid will be this much more effective at extinguishing fires than using water in the Fire extinguisher turret.

NextGenEvolution.label: Pollution absorbed by spawner
NextGenEvolution.description: Pollution absorbed evolution factor changes how much evolution increases with pollution absorbed by enemy spawners. Works the same as the map setting "Enemy > Evolution > Pollution factor". Pollution that reaches nests can be several times lower than pollution produced though, since trees and ground absorb most of the pollution before it reaches any nests (on default settings). To get similar evolution factors with a similar pollution cloud a number higher than the one you would otherwise use for "Pollution factor" is recommended if you set that to 0 and want use absorbed pollution instead. And you probably also want a very high "Destroy factor" to not make the best strategy to keep evolution down to be immediately killing all the spawners that touch the pollution cloud. Negative values are possible too.

NextGenEvolution.label: Pollution damaging trees
NextGenEvolution.description: When trees are overwhelmed by pollution they take damage and absorb pollution. This factor changes how much pollution that is absorbed and damages trees will change evolution. Because natives that chew on the polluted fruits of nature get the dirt from your factory into their bodies.

NextGenEvolution.label: Pollution absorbed healthily by nature
NextGenEvolution.description: Trees can absorb pollution without taking damage if the pollution amount is low enough. Trees actually need CO2 to live, so it makes sense that this factor doesn't really increase pollution. So the suggested value here is a negative value so evolution is slightly decreased as long as the pollution isn't too strong.

NextGenEvolution.label: Trees killed
NextGenEvolution.description: This factor changes how much evolution increases when you kill trees. If you have set pollution that damages trees to increase evolution then it is suggested that you also set a value here to discourage killing off trees with your axe which would otherwise stop evolution from damaging pollution.

NextGenEvolution.label: Natives killed
NextGenEvolution.description: If you want spitters and biters that are killed to increase evolution, here's the setting. A recommended value is maybe 100 times lower than spawner killed factor (Map gen settings > Enemy > Evolution).

TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: [TNfP] Train: Held at signals

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: [TNfP] Train: Destination Full.  Waiting...
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: [TNfP] Train: Destination Full.  Waiting...

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Message Level
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Level of information to provide around deliveries.\n'detailed' is recommended at this early stage.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Message Delivery Target
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description:
How messages are delivered.
'mixed core' uses console for important messages and flying text for standard/detailed messages.
'mixed standard' uses console for important/standard and flying text for detailed messages.
'console' uses console only.
'flying text' uses flying text only.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Station Select Focus Search
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Automatically focus the search field when opening the Station Select dialog

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Station Select Default View
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Default station view in the Station Select dialog

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Modded Train Stop Dispatch Behaviour
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description:
Default dispatch behaviour for train stop types added by other mods.
'Ignore' will ignore modded train stops completely
'Safe' allows dispatch to certain modded train stops (i.e. LTN non-depots)
'All' allows dispatch to any modded train stop

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Train Arrival Timeout
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Amount of time permitted for a train to arrive, before we consider the request failed.  Measured in seconds, 0 waits forever.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Train Boarding Behaviour
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Train behaviour on player boarding.\n'Station Select' shows a station selection box from the trains schedule.\n'Manual Mode' switches the train to manual.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Train Boarding Timeout
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Amount of time a train should wait for you to board once its arrived, before returning to service.  Measured in seconds, applied as station wait condition.\nSet to 0 to use 'Passenger Not Present'

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Location Search Radius
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Search radius for a suitable arrival location.\nUses a square area with the given radius from the player position, measured in tiles.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Show Path to Arrival Station
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: On dispatch, briefly show a straight-line path to the station the train will arrive at.

TrainNetworkForPlayers.label: Override Vanilla Wait Conditions
TrainNetworkForPlayers.description: Override vanilla wait conditions for temporary stops to be 'Passenger Not Present'

FluidMustFlow.label: Enable duct auto-join [img=info]
FluidMustFlow.description: Small ducts will automatically be joined together into normal and long ducts when placed. Substantially reduces the number of items you have to deal with.

pyveganism.label: Hardcore Vegan Mode
pyveganism.description: Ensure your ethics by disabling all the machines that exploit animals.

pyveganism.label: Hardcore Vegetarian Mode
pyveganism.description: Ensure your ethics by disabling all the machines that kill animals.

pyveganism.label: Enable UPS-affecting techs
pyveganism.description: Enables techs (currently Cultivation Expertise and Plant Breeding) that periodically call lua scripts at runtime.

pyveganism.label: Checks per Tick
pyveganism.description: The number of machines whose boni from technologies like Cultivation Expertise are updated per tick.

pyveganism.label: Update all machines directly on research completion
pyveganism.description: Will likely cause a lag spike. Otherwise the machines will be gradually updated.

SchallPipeScaling.label: Increment length __ENTITY__pipe-to-ground__ (8)
SchallPipeScaling.description: Additional maximum length for each overtier.

SulfurFromOils.label: Enable other recipes
SulfurFromOils.description: Enables sulfur from light oil and petroleum gas recipes.\n\nDefault: False

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Chemical Science Pack
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Removes Sulfur Processing tech requirement of the Chemical Science Pack technology, and reverts the sulfur ingredient of the actual science pack back to solid fuel.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Laser techs
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Removes the Chemical Science Pack requirements from Laser and Laser Turret technologies.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Rocketry techs
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Moves the prerequisites of Rocketry from Flammables back to Rocket Fuel and removes the Chemical Science Pack & Advanced Oil Processing prerequisites from Rocket Fuel.\n\nDoes not affect the rocket fuel recipe itself.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Robotic techs
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Reverts all changed Robotic related technologies, electric engines, and lubricant to no longer require Chemical Science Pack & Advanced Oil Processing.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Solid Fuel tech unlock
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Moves the Solid Fuel from Heavy & Light oil recipes back to Oil Processing.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Rocket Fuel recipe
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Removes the Light oil ingredient from Rocket Fuel.\n\nDoes not affect the Rocket Fuel technology.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Flamethrower Ammo recipe
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Reverts the Flamethrower Ammo recipe to require 50/50 heavy & light oils instead of crude.

Pre0-17-60Oil.label: Revert Advanced Oil Processing recipe
Pre0-17-60Oil.description: Reverts the Advanced Oil Processing recipe ratio.

SchallMapTag.label: Disable features
SchallMapTag.description: Temporarily disable functionalities of this mod, when free placement of tags are needed.

SchallMapTag.description:
"Position coordinates": In units of tiles.
"Chunk (point) coordinates": In units of chunks.  Simply position divided by 32.
"Chunk (absolute) coordinates": Vanilla internal coordinates, using hard-coded spawn ↘ chunk as center.
"Chunk (relative) coordinates": Use calibrated coordinates from mod “Schall Radar Alignment”.

SchallMapTag.label: Append to tag text right
SchallMapTag.description:
"Position coordinates": In units of tiles.
"Chunk (point) coordinates": In units of chunks.  Simply position divided by 32.
"Chunk (absolute) coordinates": Vanilla internal coordinates, using hard-coded spawn ↘ chunk as center.
"Chunk (relative) coordinates": Use calibrated coordinates from mod “Schall Radar Alignment”.

SchallMapTag.description:

"O ", " O": German

"东 ", " 东": Simplified Chinese

SchallMapTag.description:

"-": Mathematical
"W ", " W": English, German

SchallMapTag.label: Custom sign in positive y / South
SchallMapTag.description:

"", "+": Mathematical
"S ", " S": English, German

SchallMapTag.label: Custom sign in negative y / North
SchallMapTag.description:
Examples:
"-": Mathematical
"N ", " N": English, German

SchallMapTag.description:

%v: Coordinate value.
Examples:
"%s%v": Sign before value.
"%v%s": Sign after value.
