deadlock_stacked_recipes.description: By default (-1) fluid only recipes using high-pressure fluids will be scaled by the same factor they were compressed by with the mod CompressedFluids, if any value >0 is set this value will be used instead.

deadlock_stacked_recipes.label: DSR recipes after beacons (experimental)
deadlock_stacked_recipes.description: Locks all deadlock stacked recipes behind beacons so people dont try making smelter blocks early game using compressed ores.

deadlock_stacked_recipes.label: Hide DSR recipes from player crafting queue
deadlock_stacked_recipes.description: Hide DSR recipes from player crafting queue

biter_hunt_group.label: Hunt Frequency Range Low Minutes
biter_hunt_group.description: The minimum number of minutes after a hunt starts before the next hunt. Default 20

biter_hunt_group.label: Hunt Frequency Range High Minutes
biter_hunt_group.description: The maximum number of minutes after a hunt starts before the next hunt. Default 45

biter_hunt_group.label: Hunt Group Size
biter_hunt_group.description: How many biters will be in a biter hunt group. Default 80

biter_hunt_group.label: Biter Evolution Bonus Percentage
biter_hunt_group.description: The biter's bonus percentage added to current evolution. Default: 10

biter_hunt_group.label: Group Spawn Radius From Target
biter_hunt_group.description: How many tiles away from the target the biters will try to spawn in a circle. Default: 100

biter_hunt_group.label: Group Tunnelling Time Seconds
biter_hunt_group.description: How many seconds the biters will have their tunnelling graphics before appearing. Default: 3

biter_hunt_group.label: Incoming Group Warning Seconds
biter_hunt_group.description: How many seconds before the tunnelling time begins a generic warning that a biter group is coming is shown. The target player is not identified in this warning. Default: 10

biter_hunt_group.label: Incoming Group Warning Text
biter_hunt_group.description: The text shown in a window top left when a biter group is comming.

biter_hunt_group.label: Group Hunting Text
biter_hunt_group.description: The text shown when a player is being hunted by the group. __1__ is the player's name, __2__ is the name of the surface/map layer/planet. Default: Pack hunting __1__ on __2__

biter_hunt_group.label: Players Targeted
biter_hunt_group.description: The player names that will be targeted by the group in a JSON list, blank or empty string/array for all players. List format is ["player1", "player2"]. Default: blank/empty

biter_hunt_group.label: Biter Quantity Formula
biter_hunt_group.description: A formula that's applied to calculate the number of biters at generation time. See Readme for full details. Default: blank/empty.

Roadrunner.label: Enable Sound Effects
Roadrunner.description: Should a sound effect be played if a player dies?

Roadrunner.label: Sound Effect Volume
Roadrunner.description: Volume of sound effects, from 0 (silent) to 100 (max volume)

Roadrunner.label: Train Scanning Distance
Roadrunner.description: Distance (in tiles) at which trains will stop for players within range

Roadrunner.label: Chance of Stopping
Roadrunner.description: How likely is the train to notice you in time?

Roadrunner.label: Death Message
Roadrunner.description: Message to display in the event a user dies by train

Roadrunner.label: Sound Effect
Roadrunner.description: What sound effect should be played?

MoreLoaderRedux.label: Snap loaders
MoreLoaderRedux.description: Snap loaders to the belts when built or adjacent belts are rotated.

MoreLoaderRedux.label: Use cargo wagons
MoreLoaderRedux.description:
Uses a lot of processing power since it has to place items in script

all trains: (default)
 any cargo wagon works with loaders

auto-only: 
only trains in automatic mode are used

disabled: 
 trains are ignored by loaders

PoweredBelts.label: Belts processed per tick:
PoweredBelts.description: Higher values = worse performance, but belts will update quicker. DEFAULT = 16

DamagedBelts.label: Belts processed per tick:
DamagedBelts.description: Higher values = worse performance, but belts will update quicker. DEFAULT = 16

PoweredBelts.label: Energy usage multiplier:
PoweredBelts.description: Scales energy usage of all belts. Multiplier of 0.5 means half energy usage, 2 means double etc. DEFAULT = 1

DamagedBelts.label: Energy usage multiplier:
DamagedBelts.description: Scales energy usage of all belts. Multiplier of 0.5 means half energy usage, 2 means double etc. DEFAULT = 1

IslandLocked.label: Disable Darkstar Utilities Terra Tech.
IslandLocked.description: Setting has no effect if Darkstar Utilities not enabled.

IslandLocked.label: Disable Darkstar Utilities Jackhammers.
IslandLocked.description: Setting has no effect if Darkstar Utilities not enabled.

IslandLocked.label: Use Vanilla Science for DMR Technologies.
IslandLocked.description: DMR normally uses tenemut (and derivatives) for researching replication recipes. Checking this setting switches those technologies to be unlocked with regular science packs and removes replication labs.

IslandLocked.label: Initial DMR replicator does not require tenemut.
IslandLocked.description: DMR normally uses tenemut (and derivatives) as a required ingredient for creating all replicators.  Checking this setting makes the first replicator not require tenemut...useful for adding DMR/replication ability to maps that have not generated any tenemut; but only when vanilla science is used for DMR as well.

NicerFuelGlow.label: Colour multiplier
NicerFuelGlow.description: "Pulls back" the colours of high-energy fuels. If you've set peak/floor fuel values appropriately, but everything still seems too blue, bump this up.

NicerFuelGlow.label: Peak fuel value
NicerFuelGlow.description: How the "hotness" of a fuel's tint is calculated. Low values mean more blue. High values mean more red. For best results, set the value to that of the "biggest" fuel you're regularly using. (Default: Nuclear Fuel)

NicerFuelGlow.label: Floor fuel value
NicerFuelGlow.description: Same deal. Low values mean more red. High values mean more blue. Set the value to that of the "smallest" fuel you're regularly using. (Default: Raw Wood)

NicerFuelGlow.label: Lock vanilla fuel colours
NicerFuelGlow.description: Locks the vanilla fuels at sensible colours.

KrastorioPorted.label: Improve radar
KrastorioPorted.description: Increases coverage, but also increases power consumption.

KrastorioPorted.label: Unlock Deep Mining Drills
KrastorioPorted.description: Allows you to mine rich rocks anywhere. Too cheat. Not recommended to turn on this option if you play with SE mod.

KrastorioPorted.label: Free circuit network wires
KrastorioPorted.description: Red and green circuit network wires have no cost, so you can craft it without use any ingredient(default: disabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Rebalance ores
KrastorioPorted.description: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! Rebalance ore conusme from 1 to 3 for increase the difficulty. ATTENTION! Krastorio is balanced on this setting, if is disabled the recipes balancing will be compromised(default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Multiply ore recipes ingredients and products
KrastorioPorted.description: Multiply in ore recipes(smelting): ingredients and products and time (the work/time yield don't change). This is for reduce the overmodules effect on furnaces that break the game products computation on tick(default: enabled)

KrastorioPorted.label: Disable matter is science
KrastorioPorted.description: Disable matter is science technology, for don't be able to create science pack directly from matter(default: disable/technology active)

KrastorioPorted.label: Automation science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

KrastorioPorted.label: Logistic science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

KrastorioPorted.label: Military science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

KrastorioPorted.label: Chemical science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

KrastorioPorted.label: Production science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

KrastorioPorted.label: Utility science pack recipe
KrastorioPorted.description: Choise what science pack recipe you prefer with the possible listed[color=red](Some recipes is adapted in some case, because is impossible to use with some modpack)[/color][color=orange](If only Krastorio installed, Krastorio recommended)[/color]

ConstructionTower.label: Better Robot Battery
ConstructionTower.description: Enables the technology to improve the battery of the robots. Needed to reach the corners of the Construction Towers construction area. (Default: Enabled)

ConstructionTower1dot1.label: Better Robot Battery
ConstructionTower1dot1.description: Enables the technology to improve the battery of the robots. Needed to reach the corners of the Construction Towers construction area. (Default: Enabled)

ConstructionTower.label: Drone Charging Station - Robot Slots
ConstructionTower.description: Amount of slots for robots to be stored inside the Drone Charging Station (Default: 0)

ConstructionTower1dot1.label: Drone Charging Station - Robot Slots
ConstructionTower1dot1.description: Amount of slots for robots to be stored inside the Drone Charging Station (Default: 0)

ConstructionTower.label: Construction Tower - Robot Slots
ConstructionTower.description: Amount of slots for robots to be stored inside the Construction Tower (Default: 0)

ConstructionTower1dot1.label: Construction Tower - Robot Slots
ConstructionTower1dot1.description: Amount of slots for robots to be stored inside the Construction Tower (Default: 0)

ConstructionTower.label: Drone Charging Station - Logistic Network Radius
ConstructionTower.description: Radius of the Logistic Network for the Drone Charging Station. If the value is bigger than 75, robots may not be able to reach the next station, without researching a better battery for the robots (Default: 18)

ConstructionTower1dot1.label: Drone Charging Station - Logistic Network Radius
ConstructionTower1dot1.description: Radius of the Logistic Network for the Drone Charging Station. If the value is bigger than 75, robots may not be able to reach the next station, without researching a better battery for the robots (Default: 18)

ConstructionTower.label: Construction Tower - Logistic Network Radius
ConstructionTower.description: Radius of the Logistic Network for the Construction Tower. If the value is bigger than 75, robots may not be able to reach the next station, without researching a better battery for the robots (Default: 18)

ConstructionTower1dot1.label: Construction Tower - Logistic Network Radius
ConstructionTower1dot1.description: Radius of the Logistic Network for the Construction Tower. If the value is bigger than 75, robots may not be able to reach the next station, without researching a better battery for the robots (Default: 18)

ats.label: Signal maximum
ats.description: Maximum number of signals train scanners would output

ats.label: Update interval
ats.description: Number of ticks between each update

QuickbarTemplates.label: Default template (blueprint string)
QuickbarTemplates.description: Default template that will be applied at the start of a new game.\n[color=255,57,48]Change this from the main menu, otherwise it will not effect new games![/color]

AGNClusterioBiterControl.label: Game Speed
AGNClusterioBiterControl.description: Sets the game speed to this value when all players have left the game (eg: 0.5 = 50% speed)

AGNClusterioBiterControl.label: Disable Biter AI When Server Is Empty
AGNClusterioBiterControl.description: Disables biter AI (Note: this will not disable all biter nests from attacking you if you have something close to one of their bases, like a turret)

AGNClusterioBiterControl.label: Disable Biter AI When Server Is Empty (Forced Mode)
AGNClusterioBiterControl.description: Forces the biter AI to be disabled (Note: This will fix the issue if biters are too close to your base defenses, these biters will also be disabled)

train-teleporter.label: Teleportation timeout
train-teleporter.description: The timeout between teleportation attempts, in ticks

ThickerLines.label: Thicker power wires
ThickerLines.description: Make copper power wires between poles thicker.

ThickerLines.label: Thicker circuit wires
ThickerLines.description: Make colored circuit wires between combinators, poles, and other entities thicker.

stargate.label: Flip stargate belt symmetry so belts output on the opposite side.
Allow placement in space in Space Exploration

coverage.label: Enable Line Counting during control.lua initialization
coverage.description: A coverage test named "startup" will be started as soon as the coverage tester is required into a lua state, and stopped in on_init/on_load.

coverage.label: Mod states to include in coverage counting
coverage.description: For all tests except "startup", only enable the coverage tester in these mods. If blank, the tester will be enabled in all mods. "level" is always included if supported. JSON Array.

coverage.label: Mods to exclude file output counts for
coverage.description: Files in these mods will be excluded from lcov output, in any modstate. JSON Array.

coverage.label: Mod to skip path translation for
coverage.description: These mods will be output in "__modname__" format. "level", "base" and "core" will always be on this list. JSON Array.

BotSpeed.label: Base Bot Speed
BotSpeed.description: Base speed of construction and logistic robots, in tiles/second (default: 0.06)

NPUtils_LITEv2.label: Base Bot Speed
NPUtils_LITEv2.description: Base speed of construction and logistic robots(before bonuses), in tiles/second (default: 0.06)

Mining-Space-Industries-II.label: Disable Camera Popup
Mining-Space-Industries-II.description: If checked, no camaras will pop up automatically for you

fishtorio.label: Added fish are catalysts (non-consumed ingredients).
fishtorio.description: Unchecked means this mod attempts to add 'Number of Fish' fish as a required ingredient to each recipe that does not already have fish as an ingredient.  Checked means this mod attempts to add 'Number of Fish' fish as a catalyst to all recipes that do not already have fish as an ingredient.

fishtorio.label: Number of Fish
fishtorio.description: The number of fish to add as additional ingredients or the number of fish to add as additional catalysts.

fishtorio.label: Make every recipe produce fish.
fishtorio.description: If checked, takes precedence over other checkmark options, and causes all recipes to produce 'Number of Fish' fish.

MiningUPSGrade.label: How many miners inside a single entity?
MiningUPSGrade.description: A value of 25 (default) means the single large miner, when beaconed and moduled, will be as fast as 25 beaconed and moduled normal miners.

LogisticsWagons.label: Syncronization ticks
LogisticsWagons.description: Syncronize proxies and wagons every X ticks.

LogisticsWagons.label: Wagon inventory sizes match chest sizes
LogisticsWagons.description: Wagons match chest inventory size and storage tank fluid capacities as appropriate.

LogisticsWagons.label: Use inventory size and fluid capacitity multipliers
LogisticsWagons.description: Apply a multiplier to the inventory size and fluid capacities as well as their recipes to be more inline with the wagons representative size.

LogisticsWagons.label: Adjust vanilla cargo wagon and fluid wagon
LogisticsWagons.description: Adjust the inventory size and fuild capacity of the base games wagons to be inline with the wagons representative size.

LogisticsWagons.label: Use appropriate chests in recipes
LogisticsWagons.description: Reduce the amount of steel plates required and use the appropriate chest type for wagon recipes.  Fluid wagons always use storage tanks in their recipe as-per vanilla.

LogisticsWagons.label: Cargo and Logistics wagon multiplier
LogisticsWagons.description: Multiplier for the inventory size of a given wagon type to be more inline with the wagons representative size.  This is also the number of chests required if using chests for recipes.

LogisticsWagons.label: Fluid wagon multipliers
LogisticsWagons.description: Multiplier for the fluid capacity of a given wagon type to be more inline with the wagons representative size.  This is also the number of storage tanks required if using chests for recipes.

LogisticsWagons.label: Base amount of steel plate required for a wagon
LogisticsWagons.description: Base amount of steel plate required for a wagon regardless of inventory size or capacity.  If chests are not used in the recipe additional steel plates are required taken from the steel chest recipe with the appropriate multiplier.

VolumeControl.label: Settings List
VolumeControl.description: A list of soundfile, volume pairs in the format {soundfile1, volume}, {soundfile2, volume}, ...\nWhitespaces are ignored.

InfiniteFuel.label: Balance recipe
InfiniteFuel.description: change the recipe/time to craft of the IF (extreme is more difficult)

InfiniteFuel.label: Balance Bonus
InfiniteFuel.description: change the accelleration/accelleration speed of the IF (extreme is less powerful)

InfiniteFuel.label: Balance Technology
InfiniteFuel.description: change the technology prerequisite/cost to unlok all teh IF (normal is more difficult)

lazytorio.label: Every time you hand-craft something, it gets more expensive (ON/OFF)
Recipe Cost Increase-Rate (in terms of count*x per craft)
Maximum cost factor (how many times the rate can be applied total)
Every time you hand-mine something, your mining speed gets slower (ON/OFF)
Mining speed *X every time you mine something

market2_autobuy.label: Switch to ghosts after bankrupcy
market2_autobuy.description: Usually when your last item is placed (and can't get refilled by your money), the game would usually clear your cursor.\nWith this setting, it will switch to ghosts instead.

market2_autobuy.label: Supply bots with items
market2_autobuy.description: Using this setting will scan your surroundings for ghosts and buy the missing items

MushroomCloud_RR.label: Enable Radiation
MushroomCloud_RR.description: Radiation damages nearby enemies for some percentage of their health and a small fixed amount

MushroomCloud_RR.label: Radius Multiplier
MushroomCloud_RR.description: Imo the radius of the most nuclear detonation is way too huge (40 tiles, for comparison Realistic reactors uses a detonation of 20 tiles).\nPlus you (probably) already got extra value from the radiation...

NoCliffDeconstruction.label: Only Decon Planner
NoCliffDeconstruction.description: True: only the decon planner can plan to remove cliffs.\nIf false, must destroy cliffs manually.

SandboxedLuaCombinator.label: Code highlighting
SandboxedLuaCombinator.description: Applies colors and fonts to keywords, strings, comments and numbers

SandboxedLuaCombinator.label: Code indentation
SandboxedLuaCombinator.description: Automatically indents code according to the keywords "do", "then", "else", "elseif", "{", "}", "end"\nManual identation is impossible with this setting.

EnchantedNuclear.label: Disable kovarex enrichment process
EnchantedNuclear.description: Disable it if you want to use only the Enchanted Nuclear process to get uranium-235.

RealisticUranium.label: Disable kovarex enrichment process
RealisticUranium.description: Disable it if you want to use only the Enchanted Nuclear process to get uranium-235.

EnchantedNuclear.label: Thorium as a normal nuclear fuel
EnchantedNuclear.description: Make thorium fuel also used in other nuclear reactors.

EnchantedNuclear.label: Disable very high temperature nuclear reactor

KS-Combat-sniper-fix.label: Range factor of the inaccuracy of sniper ammunition
Direction factor of the inaccuracy of sniper ammunition

TrainWagonCombinators.label: Fast Inventory
TrainWagonCombinators.description: Faster inventory querying, but not 100% perfect for empty stack sizes

TrainWagonCombinators.label: Max Wagons
TrainWagonCombinators.description: Count of wagons for wagon selector drop-down (default 10)

TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.label: Set beacon size to 3x3
TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.description: If set to true, will enlarge all upgraded beacon tiers to 3x3.

TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.label: Set beacon size to 3x3
TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.description: If set to true, will enlarge all upgraded beacon tiers to 3x3.

TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.label: Reduce the range of upgraded beacons
TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.description: If set to true, all beacon effect range will be set to that of normal beacons.

TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.label: Reduce the range of upgraded beacons
TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.description: If set to true, all beacon effect range will be set to that of normal beacons.

TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.label: Prevent usage of productivity modules
TarawindBeaconsRE3x3.description: If set to true, will prevent productivity modules from being used in mk1-6 beacons, still works for mk7

TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.label: Prevent usage of productivity modules
TarawindBeacons-SE-bridge.description: If set to true, will prevent productivity modules from being used in mk1-6 beacons, still works for mk7

StartEquipmentOP.label: Starting construction bots
StartEquipmentOP.description: How many construction bots to begin the game with. (default = 1000)

StartEquipmentOP.label: Repair Kit Quantity
StartEquipmentOP.description: How many repair kits to begin with.\n(default = 200)

MomoEasyEvolution.label: Decrease bitter factor
MomoEasyEvolution.description: Factor of how many evolution should decrease per trigger

MomoEasyEvolution.label: Trigger rate
MomoEasyEvolution.description: Rate at which decrease bitter evolution trigger in minute

MomoEasyEvolution.label: Max counter
MomoEasyEvolution.description: Each trigger, counter will increase by 1 and if it excess the max counter it will return to 0. Higher counter become more evolution will decrease

SchallMissileCommand.label: Enable __ITEM__Schall-missile-interception__
SchallMissileCommand.description: Optional for PvE games, but absolutely essential for PvP games!

SchallMissileCommand.label: Interceptable objects
SchallMissileCommand.description:
Objects that can be destroyed by __ITEM__Schall-missile-interception-shell__.
"projectile": Most projectiles including strategic missiles, rockets, cannon shells, etc.
"artillery-projectile": Projectiles of artillery shells.
"stream": Including spitter acid, flamethrower fire.

SchallMissileCommand.label: Show launch alert
SchallMissileCommand.description: Alert on launch of strategic missiles.

SchallMissileCommand.label: Show launch message
SchallMissileCommand.description: Message on launch of strategic missiles.

SchallArachnidPlatoon.label: Hide vanilla Spidertron tech
SchallArachnidPlatoon.description: Only affect tech, existing items remain.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to vehicles
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “car” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__car__ and __ENTITY__tank__.\nNote that they do NOT benefit from fuel bonuses any more.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to locomotives
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “locomotive” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__locomotive__.\nNote that they do NOT benefit from fuel bonuses any more.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to spider vehicles
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “spider-vehicle” and using chemical fuel, such as Light Spidertron in “Schall Arachnid Platoon” mod.\nNote that they do NOT benefit from fuel bonuses any more.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to inserters
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “inserter” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__burner-inserter__.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to mining drills
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “mining-drill” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__burner-mining-drill__.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to boilers
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “boiler” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__boiler__.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to furnaces
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “furnace” and using chemical fuel, such as __ENTITY__stone-furnace__ and __ENTITY__steel-furnace__.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to assembling machines
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Entities under category “assembling-machine” and using chemical fuel.

SchallPerpetualMachine.label: Add perpetual variant to generator equipment
SchallPerpetualMachine.description: Equipment under category “generator-equipment” and using chemical fuel, such as Vehicle fuel cell in “Schall Tank Platoon” mod.

SchallModulePlacement.label: Display module placement message
SchallModulePlacement.description: Shows how many modules is removed/inserted on machines.

SchallModulePlacement.label: Module placement on built
SchallModulePlacement.description: On entity built.\nOnly apply when the machine type is already specified in module placement GUI.\nNot applied on ghost building.

SchallModules.label: Allow productivity effects with beacons
SchallModules.description: Allow vanilla productivity modules (and possibly many others from various mods) to be placed in beacons.

SchallModules.label: Efficiency modules buff
SchallModules.description: Vanilla efficiency modules are weak and under-used, especially when compared to other modules.  Enabling this option increases their capabilities.

SchallModules.label: Enable multicomponent modules
SchallModules.description: Enable bicomponent and tricomponent modules, which are composed of two or three vanilla modules as components.  The composite modules will have the combined (but slightly reduced) effects of their components.

SchallModules.label: Multicomponent module effect strength
SchallModules.description: Asymptotic limit of effect strength in multicomponent modules.  Higher values reflect more components can be "stacked" together in the same module slot.

SchallModules.label: Recipe limitations __ITEM__Schall-productivity-speed-effectivity-module__
SchallModules.description: Limitations on __ITEM__Schall-productivity-speed-effectivity-module__.\nOn: Usable only on intermediates, like other productivity modules.\nOff: (Default) Usable on any recipes.

SchallChunkAlignment.label: Show chunk on cursor radar
SchallChunkAlignment.description: Whenever the cursor (stack or ghost) is a radar item, or contains radar in blueprint.

SchallChunkAlignment.label: Show chunk on cursor buildable only
SchallChunkAlignment.description: Used to limit the "cursor" options above.  Only items that can build entities or tiles will trigger showing.\nFor example, __ITEM__iron-plate__ and __ITEM__speed-module__ will not trigger.

SchallChunkAlignment.label: Tile grid
SchallChunkAlignment.description: The grid used in highlighting the current chunk and divisions (down to tiles) within.

SchallChunkAlignment.label: Chunk grid
SchallChunkAlignment.description: The grid used in highlighting the neighbouring chunks.

SchallGeowarfare.label: Pollution base __ITEM__Schall-planet-buster-warhead__ (100000)
SchallGeowarfare.description: Affects amount of pollution generated each detonation, thus also the increase in evolution factor.

SchallGeowarfare.label: Pollution base __ITEM__Schall-tectonic-warhead__ (25000)
SchallGeowarfare.description: Affects amount of pollution generated each detonation, thus also the increase in evolution factor.

SchallGeowarfare.label: Default rock
SchallGeowarfare.description: Generated by __ITEM__Schall-tectonic-missile__, when result depth is over plains.\nCan only use type "simple-entity".\nDefault: "sand-rock-big"

SchallRadioactiveWaste.label: Enable __ITEM__Schall-radiological-warfare__
SchallRadioactiveWaste.description:
EXPERIMENTAL FEATURE!
Still subject to big changes, due to balancing and practicality.
Adds __ITEM__Schall-dirty-bomb__ and __ITEM__Schall-decontamination-capsule__.
Allows mods to add radioactive effects to projectiles.

SchallRadioactiveWaste.label: Emissions __ENTITY__Schall-radioactive-contamination__ (0.05)
SchallRadioactiveWaste.description: In units of per second.\nEmitted by __ITEM__Schall-dirty-bomb__.

SchallRadioactiveWaste.label: Enable radioactive __ITEM__atomic-bomb__
SchallRadioactiveWaste.description:
Real-world nuclear bombs unleash immense radioactive contamination around ground zero.  Factorio ones are really too "clean" in comparison.
Requires __ITEM__Schall-radiological-warfare__ enabled.
On: (Default) Adds such effects to the vanilla __ITEM__atomic-bomb__.  (Internally, it is done to projectile "atomic-rocket".)
Off: Vanilla setting, no changes made.

SchallCircuitScaling.label: Lowest tier Circuit components
SchallCircuitScaling.description: 1: Down to tier -1, which is 1/2 in linear size (1/4 in area) of their vanilla counterparts.\n2: Down to tier -2, which is 1/4 in linear size (1/16 in area) of their vanilla counterparts.\n3: Down to tier -3, which is 1/8 in linear size (1/64 in area) of their vanilla counterparts.

SchallEntityInspector.label: Maximum entity instances
SchallEntityInspector.description: Maximum number of entity instances to be inspected simultaneously.

Pheromones.label: Enable biter relaxation pheromone
Pheromones.description: Whether to allow the production of the pheromone that makes biters simply go idle.

kazbots.label: Base Bot Speed

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium Patch Richness

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium Recipe Value
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Scales how much raw material you get from a single piece of Tiberium ore. Higher values make the game easier.\nDefault: 10

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium Damage
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Scale the damage that Tiberium will do to structures when it grows, players standing on it, or players holding it in their inventory. Save game must be reloaded after changing.\nDefault: 10

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium in Starting Area
Factorio-Tiberium.description:
This will include Tiberium as one of your starting ore patches.
Yes, it will spread and eat the other starting ore patches.
Yes, that will make the game significantly more difficult.
You can expect no mercy and only pain, you've been warned.

Factorio-Tiberium.description: Prevents biters from dying to Tiberium fields.  Does not affect damage dealt with Tiberium weapons.\nDefault: enabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Easy Mode
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Simplifies recipes by removing all catalysts and introducing early transmutation recipes so you never have to deal with centrifuging. For the full experience, also turn off the Waste settings below.\nDefault: disabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Refining Sludge Waste
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Whether refining recipes produce Tiberium Sludge waste.\nDefault: enabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Refining Sulfur Waste
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Whether refining recipes produce Sulfur waste.\nDefault: disabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Direct Sludge Waste
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Whether direct recipes produce Tiberium Sludge waste.\nDefault: disabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium Advanced Start
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Start with some basic tiberium refining equipment, so that you can do a tiberium only run. \nDefault: disabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Tiberium Ore Only
Factorio-Tiberium.description: Enables the Tiberium Ore in Start setting, and the Tiberium Advanced Start setting. \nDefault: disabled

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Inventory Tiberium Damage Scale
Factorio-Tiberium.description: If enabled, scales the damage from tiberium in your inventory to the number of stacks you have. You will die immediately if you have too many. \nDefault: disabled
Distance from nodes that Tiberium can be placed. Save game must be reloaded after changing.\nDefault: 30

Factorio-Tiberium.label: Override __1__ Outputs
Factorio-Tiberium.description:
Advanced setting: replace the automatically generated __1__ recipe output with something you feel is more appropriate for your mod combination.
Enter a delimited string of the items/fluids and amounts that should come from the recipe in the exact format "item1-internal-name:item1-amount,item2-internal-name:item2-amount" (with no quotation marks).
You can find items' internal names by loading into a game, pressing F4 to open debug settings, enabling "show-debug-info-in-tooltips", and then mousing over the desired item and noting the "item-name" field. For fluids, mouse over them in FNEI or the un-barreling recipes.

coin_generation.description: How many coins a nest is worth when killed by a player. Partial coin values are handled by chance. Default value: 10. Set all values to 0 to disable feature.

coin_generation.description: A multiplier thats applied to the value of coins players get for killing non biter nest things. The raw value is based on enemy health and scales logarithmically. Small biter is 1 coin, large is 4 and a behemoth is 7 coins. Partial coin values are handled by chance. Default value: 1. Set all values to 0 to disable feature.

se-science-scale.label: Terrestrial science multiplier

se-science-scale.description: How many first tier science packs to have per second tier science pack. (Tier 2 space science packs: currently only deep space.)

se-science-scale.label: Minimal cycle count
se-science-scale.description: Minimal cycle number a tech needs to have for it to be targeted by this mod. (Set to 0 to disable. Doesn't effect any leveled technologies. Note that this runs before the map's science cost multiplier.)

se-science-scale.label: Soft minimal cycle count
se-science-scale.description: If any targeted technology ends up with less cycles than this, it gets overwritten. (Set to 0 to disable. Doesn't effecy any leveled technologies. Note that this runs before the map's science cost multiplier.)

se-science-scale.label: Count scale
se-science-scale.description: A number to multiply the count diviser by, before applying it to the count. (1 = direct relation between pack numbers and count change. 0.5 = double effect. 2 = half the effect. 0 to disable. as long as this value is equivilent to the time scale value, tech research time should not change, barring rounding errors. setting very small values could cause unpredictable results.)

se-science-scale.label: Time scale
se-science-scale.description: A number to multiply the time multiplier by, before applying it to the time. (1 = direct relation between pack numbers and time change. 0.5 = half the effect. 2 = double effect. 0 to disable. as long as this value is equivilent to the count scale value, tech research time should not change, barring rounding errors. setting very small values could cause unpredictable results.)

se-science-scale.label: Ignore Quality of Life Research mod's techs
se-science-scale.description: Ignore techs provided by the QOL research mod, to avoid some weird interactions that cause inintended pack count shenanigans.

RampantResources.description: The maximum yield that will appear on a resource tile. Changing this value will cause existing worlds to regenerate all infinite resource tiles. Default 1.40 means 140% yield on a resource tile. Yields above 100% will produce extra resource per creation.

True-Nukes.label: Destroy resources in crater
True-Nukes.description: This setting can be used to make sure that resources aren't destroyed by nuclear weapons at all. No guarentees are made about this looking natural with tile transitions

True-Nukes.label: Enable craters filling with water
True-Nukes.description: With this setting enabled, the nuclear craters slowly fill with water, this can cause trouble when drones are trying to replace buildings above the crater. After the crater has finished building it will ghost landfill above itself, but up to this point, any landfill placed is repeatedly destroyed.

True-Nukes.label: Enable nuclear weapons causing large numbers of short lived fires
True-Nukes.description: With this setting enabled, nuclear weapons create lots of small, short lived fires, which can cause lag issues, but create a nice scorched effect.

True-Nukes.label: Large nuclear weapon fire reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the artillery nukes are so huge, this setting reduces the number of fires created in the crater. This can significantly improve performance, however the bare crater does not look as devastated. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the number of fires)

True-Nukes.label: Hiroshima scale weapon fire reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the larger nukes are so huge, this setting reduces the number of fires created in the crater. This can significantly improve performance, and few living creatures survive close enough to see the crater anyway, however the bare crater does not look as devastated. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the number of fires)

True-Nukes.label: 100kt weapon fire reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the 100kt nuke is so huge, this setting reduces the number of fires created in the crater. This can significantly improve performance, and few living creatures survive close enough to see the crater anyway, however the bare crater does not look as devastated. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the number of fires) This is very important for the 100kt, and can prevent the game crashing from running out of memory.

True-Nukes.label: 1Mt weapon fire reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the 1Mt nuke is so huge, this setting reduces the number of fires created in the crater. This can significantly improve performance, and few living creatures survive close enough to see the crater anyway, however the bare crater does not look as devastated. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the number of fires) This is very important for the 1Mt, and can prevent the game crashing from running out of memory.

True-Nukes.label: 15kt weapon blast range reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the 15kt nukes are so huge, this setting reduces simulated range of the blast. This can significantly improve performance, as the further out the wave goes, the more entities are hit. This does not increase the amount of world loaded, so a hard cutoff will still be present in unexplored areas. The default will usually stop at about the point where the blast is not longer destroying many buildings, only damaging them. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the blast radius)

True-Nukes.label: 100kt weapon blast range reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the 100kt nukes are so huge, this setting reduces simulated range of the blast. This can significantly improve performance, as the further out the wave goes, the more entities are hit. This does not increase the amount of world loaded, so a hard cutoff will still be present in unexplored areas. The default will usually stop at about the point where the blast is not longer destroying many buildings, only damaging them. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the blast radius)

True-Nukes.label: 1Mt weapon blast range reduction
True-Nukes.description: Since the 1Mt nukes are so huge, this setting reduces simulated range of the blast. This can significantly improve performance, as the further out the wave goes, the more entities are hit. This does not increase the amount of world loaded, so a hard cutoff will still be present in unexplored areas. The default will usually stop at about the point where the blast is not longer destroying many buildings, only damaging them. (A value of 2 here results in a halving of the blast radius)

True-Nukes.label: Enable nuclear flash (Please note warning)
True-Nukes.description:
If enabled, nuclear explosions will cause a bright flash in their vincinity.

EPILEPSY WARNING:
Some persons may experience epileptic seizures if they are exposed to certain light frequencies, flickering lights or geometric forms/patterns. In this case I strongly recommend to disable this option!

True-Nukes.label: Enable thermobaric weapons
True-Nukes.description: This mod is primarily about nuclear weapons, but with the ability to simulate blast waves, thermobaric weapons were not hard to add, however, as they are available earlier in the game, they may be much more balance-breaking. They are also a much less accurate rendering, merely desinged to look cool, as little data is readily available on the various effects of thermobaric weapons.

True-Nukes.label: Material for small weapons
True-Nukes.description:
What material should be used for low yield weapons?
Same as medium-large - same material will be used as is used for larger weapons - usually Uranium-235
True Nukes Default - uses Californium-251
Mod dependant - uses whatever other installed mods would put in this place, and defaults to the True Nukes varient
Custom - uses whatever is in the box below.

True-Nukes.label: Literal name for custom material for small weapons
True-Nukes.description: The literal in-game name for the material to be used - no guarantee of balance.

Custom - uses whatever is in the box below.

True-Nukes.label: Literal name for custom material for medium-large weapons

True-Nukes.label: Inert material
True-Nukes.description:

True-Nukes.label: Enable nuclear crater noise
True-Nukes.description: With this setting enabled some noise is produced at the edge of the larger craters to make them seem more natural.

True-Nukes.label: Enable the new crater tiles
True-Nukes.description: Enables the new crater tiles - disabling this option will break any pre-existing crater tiles in your map, so fill them in or dig them up first - primarily here for mod compatibility, although if this is required, feel free to submit a bug report on the mod's page, as I might be able to fix it.

True-Nukes.label: Use the new crater system for any craters created
True-Nukes.description: Enables the height aware crater system - disabling this will not break anything, but will mean any new nukes fired use the old system (no heights or water motion). This may improve performance significantly, particularly if the lag is happening for a long time after the detonation as the craters fill with water.

True-Nukes.label: Use optimised detonation system for 100kt.
True-Nukes.description: Always used for nukes >=1Mt. This causes damage to only be applied when a chunk loads. This may break many other mods, but is a lot quicker, uses less memory, and allows bigger nukes. It still has to proccess any already-generated chunks, so detonating bigger nukes in factories is still slow.

True-Nukes.label: Use more optimised detonation system (BETA)
True-Nukes.description: This is a more aggressively optimised way of doing the initial blast for the nukes. It may improve performance, and reduce memory usage, but may also break other mods and not be as nice-looking.

Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.label: Overwrite of compression factor (Stack size)
Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.description:
Allow overwrite of the stack size selected in Deadlock's Stacking Beltboxes & Compact Loaders mod of stacked ore and manually set the factor that the ore is compressed by.
[color=#8CB9E3]Useful in case some other mod makes changes to the Deadlock's Stacking stack size. This should be the same as the number of items making up each stacked item.[/color]
If the default "disabled" is selected, the stack size is automatically set to the value selected in the settings of Deadlock's Stacking Beltboxes & Compact Loaders.
[color=orange]WARNING: It is recommended to not change this setting or the Stack size setting in the mod settings of Deadlock's Stacking Beltboxes & Compact Loaders mid game.[/color]
Default: disabled

Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.label: High pressure offshore pump
Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.description:
If the mod Pressurized Fluids is enabled, adds a High pressure offshore pump that outputs High-pressurized water directly, but at a lower rate than a normal offshore pump.
[color=#8CB9E3]The pressurized output/second is adjusted automatically depending on the fluid compression rate selected in the settings of Pressurized fluids, meaning the (uncompressed) output/second stays the same overall.[/color]
If FactorioExtended Plus Transport is enabled, this also adds a High pressure offshore pump Mk2.
[color=#8CB9E3]Default: enabled[/color]

Stacked_Mining.label: High pressure offshore pump
Stacked_Mining.description:
If the mod Pressurized Fluids is enabled, adds a High pressure offshore pump that outputs High-pressurized water directly, but at a lower rate than a normal offshore pump.
[color=#8CB9E3]The pressurized output/second is adjusted automatically depending on the fluid compression rate selected in the settings of Pressurized fluids, meaning the (uncompressed) output/second stays the same overall.[/color]
If FactorioExtended Plus Transport is enabled, this also adds a High pressure offshore pump Mk2.

Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.label: Adjust the graphics of ores
Kythbloods_Stacked_Mining.description:
If enabled, the "stage_counts" of ores that are marked for stacked mining are changed in such a way that the same graphics are used as before they were marked.
[color=#8CB9E3]"stage_counts" is a list of values that define which stage of the animation is used depending on the amount of an ore patch.[/color]
Disabling this setting makes it easier to distinguish between normal ore and ore marked for stacked mining, because of the change of the graphics. However, ore patches with a low amount of ore can look quite barren.
[color=#8CB9E3]Default: disabled[/color]

car-finder.label: Show vehicle color
car-finder.description: When printing the list of vehicles, use the color of the vehicle.  For cars/tanks this is usually the color of the last player to drive it.  For spidertrons, this is the color set in the spidertron settings.

car-finder.label: Show distance and direction

car-finder.label: Show map coordinates

car-finder.label: Focus Spidertron when holding remote
car-finder.description: If you are holding a remote linked to a Spidertron, this option will focus your view on the Spidertron automatically instead of printing the list of vehicles

car-finder.label: Only show specific vehicles
car-finder.description:
Comma separated list of entity names that should be shown in the search results.

Make this setting empty to show all vehicles.

If you are playing a mod like AAI that adds many new vehicle entities, start with a list of vanilla names like [color=#e69100]car,tank,spidertron[/color] and you can add in any others that you want to be able to locate.

To get the entity name, turn on the mod setting to [font=default-bold]Show internal entity names[/font].  Alternatively, you can press F4 to open debug options, check the option for [font=default-bold]show-debug-info-in-tooltips[/font], hover over the vehicle, and write down the [font=default-bold]name[/font] value from the debug section in the tooltip.

car-finder.label: Hide vehicles from results
car-finder.description:
Comma separated list of entity names that should never be shown in the search results.

This will take precedence over the show-vehicles setting just above this one.

To get the entity name, turn on the mod setting to [font=default-bold]Show internal entity names[/font].  Alternatively, you can press F4 to open debug options, check the option for [font=default-bold]show-debug-info-in-tooltips[/font], hover over the vehicle, and write down the [font=default-bold]name[/font] value from the debug section in the tooltip.

car-finder.label: Show internal entity names
car-finder.description: Use this if you are trying to figure out the internal entity names for a vehicle you want to show/hide using the settings below.

BIG

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Which FX should be used for the fission bomb[item=atomic-bomb]/artillery[item=rfw-fission-artillery-shell]?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description:
[color=#ff7300]Vanilla[/color] = no change to the FX
[color=#ff7300]MIRV-like[/color] = FX that is similar to MIRV
[color=#ff7300]RFW[/color] = FX that uses parts of MIRV and parts of vanilla
[color=#ff7300]RFW with thermal radiation[/color] = the same as RFW, except that it starts fires at 2x the radius of the shockwave to simulate thermal radiation. If you're experiencing game freezes, use RFW instead.

[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = RFW[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Which FX should be used for the thermonuclear bomb[item=rfw-thermonuclear-bomb]/artillery[item=rfw-thermonuclear-artillery-shell]?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description:
[color=#ff7300]Vanilla-like[/color] = FX similar to vanilla
[color=#ff7300]MIRV-like[/color] = FX that is similar to MIRV's
[color=#ff7300]RFW[/color] = FX that uses parts of MIRV and parts of vanilla
[color=#ff7300]RFW with thermal radiation[/color] = the same as RFW, except that it starts fires at 2x the radius of the shockwave to simulate thermal radiation. If you're experiencing game freezes, use RFW instead.

[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = RFW[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Which FX should be used for the pure fusion bomb[item=rfw-fusion-bomb]/artillery[item=rfw-fusion-artillery-shell]?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description:
[color=#ff7300]Vanilla-like[/color] = FX similar to vanilla
[color=#ff7300]MIRV-like[/color] = FX that is similar to MIRV's
[color=#ff7300]RFW[/color] = FX that uses parts of MIRV and parts of vanilla
[color=#ff7300]RFW with thermal radiation[/color] = the same as RFW, except that it starts fires at 2x the radius of the shockwave to simulate thermal radiation. If you're experiencing game freezes, use RFW instead.

[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = RFW[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Which FX should be used for the antimatter bomb[item=rfw-antimatter-bomb]/artillery[item=rfw-antimatter-artillery-shell]?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description:
[color=#ff7300]Vanilla-like[/color] = FX similar to vanilla
[color=#ff7300]MIRV-like[/color] = FX that is similar to MIRV's
[color=#ff7300]RFW[/color] = FX that uses parts of MIRV and parts of vanilla
[color=#ff7300]RFW with thermal radiation[/color] = the same as RFW, except that it starts fires at 2x the radius of the shockwave to simulate thermal radiation. Freezes the game for some time on detonation.

[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = RFW[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Strength of the screen burn when detonating bombs:
'Realistic' plasma throwers?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description: In reality, plasma is just hot gas that would cool down really quickly after leaving the barrel, so a plasma thrower would be more like a fart thrower.\n\n[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = OFF[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Optimize the 100kt explosion?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description: Makes the 100kt explosion use a simpler crater generation method, and disables generating chunks on impact, meaning that the bomb will not affect anything outside of the revealed area on the map. The explosion should freeze the game for less than a second, as opposed to around a minute.\n\n[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = OFF[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Optimize the 1Mt explosion?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description: Makes the 1Mt explosion use a simpler crater generation method, and disables generating chunks on impact, meaning that the bomb will not affect anything outside of the revealed area on the map. The explosion should freeze the game for just a few seconds, as opposed to a few minutes.\n\n[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = OFF[/color]

RealisticFusionWeaponry.label: Optimize the 50Mt explosion?
RealisticFusionWeaponry.description:
Makes the 50Mt explosion use a simpler crater generation method, and disables generating chunks on impact, meaning that the bomb will not affect anything outside of the revealed area on the map. The explosion still freezes the game for a few minutes, as opposed to probably an hour (I never let it run for long enough to see how long it'd actually take, but it is definitely well over 30 minutes of processing time on a 4GHz Ryzen 5 2600).
You might be able to disable this setting if you're playing factorio on a supercomputer, otherwise I do not recommend even trying it.

[color=#008cff]DEFAULT = ON[/color]

nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Choose between the different types of batteries, mod specific types will be added later on.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of batteries
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: This number will set a cap at how many batteries can be provided, due to the limited grid in the different armors you will not receive more batteries than what is reasonable.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide night vision
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Check to be provided night vision gear, priority 2.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Type of personal roboport
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Choose type of personal roboport to be provided

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of roboports
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Maximum number of roboports to be provided, priority 3.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of exoskeletons
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Maximum number of exoskeleton to be provided, priority 4.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Type of energy shield
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Choose type of energy shield to be provided

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of energy shields
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Maximum number of energy shields to be provided, priority 5.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide belt immunity equipment
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Check to provide belt immunity equipment, priority 8.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide discharge defense
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Check to provide discharge defense, priority 6.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of personal laser defense
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Maximum number of personal laser defense, priority 7.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Max number of solar panels or fusion reactors
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Maximum number of power sources, priotrity 1.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Fill empty spot with solar panels
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Check this to fill empty spot, that cant hold any other equipment, with solar panels

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Don't place equipment in armor
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Instead of trying to fit the equipment in the armor grid the equipment is placed in player inventory.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Which type of logistic system will be used
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: This determines whether the player is provided belts or logistic robots, note that if both belt and robots are enabled the player inventory might get full, and some of the stuff will get lost

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of roboports
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Must be an integer between 0 and 50

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of logistic robots
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Must be an integer between 0 and 1000

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of construction robots
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Must be an integer between 0 and 250. When choosing personal roboports in the armor the appropriate amount of construction robots will be added, these excluded, since these are meant for the normal roboports.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide both passive and active provider chests
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: If this box is checked player will receive both active and passive providers, otherwise the player will only receive passive

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of provider chests
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: The total amount of provider chests provided to the player

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide buffer chests
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: If this box is checked the player will receive buffer chests together with storage chests

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of requester chests
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: The total amount of requester chests provided to the player

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of storage chests
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: The total amount of storage and buffer chests provided to the player

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Use robots from mod
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Choose from which mod the robots should be provided. Tier 1 of the selected mod will be used.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Type of roboports
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Choose which mod the roboports should be taken from.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide robots even when not receiving any roboports
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: If you choose to not receive any roboport (personal roboports excluded) you will still receive robots if this is checked.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide logistic chests even when not receiving any roboports
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: If you choos to not receive any roboports you will still be provided logistic chests if this is checked.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide custom items (Advanced users)
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Enter wanted items and amount in the following format:   iron-plate:1   Spelling error may cause error at start.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of uranium fuel cells provided per portable reactor
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Specify how many uranium fuel cells you wish to receive per reactor, that is if hte number is set to 50, and you receive 2 reactors, then you will receive 100 fuel cells in total.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide construction robots
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Provides the maximal number of commandable construction robots for the provided personal roboports, if robot mod "None" is selected vanilla robots will be provided.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Let this mod provide weapons and ammo
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: If checked all guns and ammo will be purged and replaced by what's selected below. Might cause problems with some mods.

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide weapon
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Provides specified handheld weaponry at start, choose a compatible ammo below

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Ammo type
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Provides specified ammo

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Number of ammo
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Amount of ammo provided

nihilist_quickstart_bne.label: Provide a gas mask
nihilist_quickstart_bne.description: Check this to receive a gas mask to reduce your oxygen usage

bobs-custom-circuitry.description: Replaces [item=electronic-circuit] with [item=basic-circuit-board] in [item=constant-combinator], [item=arithmetic-combinator], [item=decider-combinator], [item=power-switch] & [item=programmable-speaker] \nNote: Please use the 'Align Recipes' setting below from now own, this one will be removed at some point in the future! \n(defalut: false)

Incorporates cable and circuit selection in technology adjustments. 
F.e when used with [item=copper-cable] or [item=basic-circuit-board], the tech will have [item=logistic-science-pack] removed and some prerequisites changed. 
Best used with Angel's mods 
Somewhat experimental

admin-config.label: Creative chest size
admin-config.description:
Usable inventory size of each __ENTITY__admin-config_creative-chest__ and __ENTITY__admin-config_creative-provider-chest__.
An extra slot will be added for trashing.
Its value affects how many chests you need to place for one item cycle. Larger inventory size means fewer chests are needed. However, it is also more likely to cause performance issue when hovering the chests.
Changing its value for an existing game will cause item regrouping.

admin-config.label: Creative chests contain hidden items

RampantFixed.label: World: Units affected by tiles
RampantFixed.description: (Can cause Desyncs) Units are affected by tile movement modifiers

RampantFixed.label: Map: Revert Enemy Map Color
RampantFixed.description: Reverts the enemy map color to the vanilla enemy map color

RampantFixed.label: World: Unit Nest breath air
RampantFixed.description: Now unit spawners breath air so they are affected by things like poison capsules

RampantFixed.label: Projectiles: Use blockable projectiles
RampantFixed.description: Use the projectile attacks that are blockable. This should be checked if you are using the new enemies.

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Starting chunk attack threshold
RampantFixed.description: The total score that a chunk must reach in order for an attack wave to spawn. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves. Scaling linearly with evolution factor (starting threshold @ 0.0 evolution)

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Ending chunk attack threshold
RampantFixed.description: The total score that a chunk must reach in order for an attack wave to spawn. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves. Scaling linearly with evolution factor (ending threshold @ 100.0 evolution)

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Max biter group size that can be directly formed
RampantFixed.description: If you wish to change how the attack wave scales with evolution you will need to modify the config.lua in the zip file.

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Max number of attack groups that can be active at once
RampantFixed.description: More squads requires more UPS.

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Max number of building groups that can be active at once
RampantFixed.description: More builders requires more UPS.

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Enable building safety.
RampantFixed.description: This needs to be toggle for the safe building toggles to work. This will cause entities made safe to regenerate with the destructible flag set to false, which causes them to never be targeted or damaged again.

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make curved rails safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make curved rails safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make straight rails safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make straight rails safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make big electric poles safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make big electric poles safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make rail chain signals safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make rail chain signals safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make rail signals safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make rail signals safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make train stops safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make train stops safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: AI: Nocturnal Mode
RampantFixed.description: Toggling this will cause Rampant attack waves to spawn at night. Works better with the clockwork mod or a mod that extends night.

RampantFixed.label: AI: Action points scaling
RampantFixed.description: Between 0.0 and 100.0. This scales how many action points the ai gets per logic cycle to perform actions like making attack waves. 0.3 - very easy, 0.75 - easy, 1.0 - medium, 1.25+ - hard

RampantFixed.label: AI: Difficulty
RampantFixed.description: Hard - default level. Lite - for a more comfortable game. The response to the player's actions is weaker, attacks are less frequent

RampantFixed.label: AI: Print Point Spending to Chat
RampantFixed.description: Print a message to chat whenever Rampant spends points. Includes GPS coordinates. Keep disabled for the hardest Rampant experience. Heads up: can fill up chat quickly during busy battles!

RampantFixed.label: AI: Print Point Gains to Chat
RampantFixed.description: Print a message to chat whenever Rampant gains points. Does not show passive point generation. Keep disabled for the hardest Rampant experience. Heads up: can fill up chat quickly during busy battles!

RampantFixed.label: Safety; Increase wall resistance to spitters
RampantFixed.description: Toggling this will cause a 60% acid and 75% poison resistance to be added to all wall entities to reduce the damage done by spitters to walls.

RampantFixed.label: Safety: Make lamps safe from biters
RampantFixed.description: Make lamps safe from biters

RampantFixed.label: Optimization: Remove blood particles (Reduces lag spikes)
RampantFixed.description: The blood particles that are created when biters are being killed can cause UPS spikes, this removes them.

RampantFixed.label: Notification: Enable attack wave warnings
RampantFixed.description: Shows a message warning players that an attack wave is incoming

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Enable the swarm
RampantFixed.description: This reduces the size of the unit collision_mask causing them to reduce pathing collisions and smooth out the attacks

RampantFixed.label: World: Enable new enemies
RampantFixed.description: Adds news enemies that will be dispersed over the world. This increases the RAM requirements. With 1 variation for each biter, worm, and nest and 5 tiers expect upto a 2GB RAM increase. With 20 variations and 10 tiers set expect up to 9GB RAM increase. Variations add randominess to each tier of biter, worms, or nests. Tiers are the power level of the biters.

RampantFixed.label: World: Allow other enemies, new factions only from the specified side
RampantFixed.description: Only in a new game or on a map without Rampant. Restricts the placement of <new enemies>, leaving room for the enemies of the other mods.

RampantFixed.label: World: settle the factions on the selected side
RampantFixed.description: Only in a new game or on a map without Rampant. New factions will appear only on the specified side if the <allow other enemies> setting is enabled

RampantFixed.label: World: Enemy Random Seed
RampantFixed.description: The seed that powers all of the unit generation, so change this if you want the enemy stats to change

RampantFixed.label: World: Enemy deadzone frequency
RampantFixed.description: The percentage of zones that start without worms or nests

RampantFixed.label: World: Enemy Variations (highly recommended = 1)
RampantFixed.description: This number corresponds to the number of variations per tier. This adds randominess to each tier power level (example:2 fire bitters lvl 1, with diff stats). Min 1, Max 20

RampantFixed.label: World: Enable Bobs as a faction
World: Enable NE as a faction
Safety: Disallow Friendly Fire Splash Damage
RampantFixed.description: Prevents enemy spitters and worms from damaging units or buildings from the same force through splash damage

RampantFixed.label: World: Beginning enemy level
RampantFixed.description: This is the starting level of the enemy that will be used when generating the set of enemies for the specified number of tiers and increases linearly to the end tier for as many tiers selected. Roughly healthwise each tier is a follows (1-15,2-75,3-150,4-250,5-1000,6-2000,7-3500,8-7500,9-15000,10-30000). min 1, max 10

RampantFixed.label: World: Ending enemy level (recommended = 5)
RampantFixed.description: This is the ending tier level that is reached after increasing linearly from the start tier for as many tiers selected. Roughly healthwise each tier is as follows (1-15,2-75,3-150,4-250,5-1000,6-2000,7-3500,8-7500,9-15000,10-30000). min 1, max 10, , recommended =5 (slightly weaker normal biters)

RampantFixed.label: World: Long range immunity for some factions
RampantFixed.description: Some factions can't be killed from long range. Disabling the setting may make these factions too weak

RampantFixed.label: World: Oneshot protection for some factions
RampantFixed.description: Some factions reqiure multiple hits to die. Disabling the setting may make these factions too weak

RampantFixed.label: AI: Enable Migration
RampantFixed.description: This will allow the ai to expand its worms and nests. Respects the map settings for biter expansion. (Be carefull! This is hard mode!)

RampantFixed.label: AI: Enable Peaceful
RampantFixed.description: The Rampant AI can roll the peaceful state. If this is disabled and the biters roll the peaceful state, they are instead changed to aggressive or migrating state depending on AI: Enabled Migration setting. This does not relate to whether your map has Factorio's Peaceful Mode enabled or disabled. Disable for the hardest Rampant experience.

RampantFixed.label: AI: Print State Changes to Chat
RampantFixed.description: Gives you information in the game chat about Rampant's AI state. Messages are displayed for each surface. Disable for the hardest Rampant experience.

RampantFixed.label: DEBUG: Print Temperament Changes to Chat
RampantFixed.description: Prints to chat AI temperament information that controls AI state rolls. This is used for debugging.

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Use Player Proximity as attack trigger
RampantFixed.description: Include player pheromones amount for threshold on chunks with biter nests that will generate a Rampant attack wave. DOES NOT affect vanilla biters waves

RampantFixed.label: Attack Wave: Player score contribution threshold
RampantFixed.description: The score that a chunk must reach for it to contribute to the attack threshold. Increasing reduces player pheromone cloud impact.

RampantFixed.label: World: Unkillable logistic bots
RampantFixed.description: This will make logistic bots immune to all damage

RampantFixed.label: World: Unkillable construction bots
RampantFixed.description: This will make construction bots immune to all damage

RampantFixed.description: Reduce the collision box size of nests and worms by 50%. May cause overlapping entities due to the collision box being smaller than the entity graphic.
